IUT3.ThmA.content: Introductory version of Theorem 3.11 (multiradial algorithms for LGP-monoids). For distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, with n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Theorem 1.5 (i)): (i) the multiradial representation n,◦R^LGP, consisting of (a) tensor packets of log-shells, (b) splitting monoids of LGP-monoids acting on them, (c) copies labeled by j ∈ F*_l of the number field F_mod acting on them, regarded up to the indeterminacies (Ind1) (automorphisms of the procession Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T)) and (Ind2) (the non-(Ind1) portion arising from automorphisms of the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips in the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link, at v ∈ V^non the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on local copies of O^{×μ}), is constructed by an algorithm in Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T), functorial for isomorphisms of processions, and the permutation symmetries of the étale-picture induce compatible poly-isomorphisms Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T) ≅ Prc(n',◦D^⊢_T), n,◦R^LGP ≅ n',◦R^LGP, compatible with the bi-coricity poly-isomorphisms n,◦D^⊢_0 ≅ n',◦D^⊢_0; (ii) the log-Kummer correspondence: inverse Kummer isomorphisms between (a), (b), (c) and the Frobenioid-theoretic data of each n,mHT, mutually compatible as m varies for (b) and (c) up to roots of unity, and for (a) only upper semi-compatible (Ind3), but precisely compatible with log-volumes; (iii) compatibility of the Kummer isomorphisms with the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links, up to (Ind2).
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1

a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data, thought of as arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii))
for each n ∈ Z, n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater determined up to isomorphism by the n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}, m ∈ Z, via vertical coricity (Theorem 1.5 (i); Remark 3.8.2)
IUT3.ThmA.conclusion: (i) n,◦R^LGP, regarded up to (Ind1) and (Ind2), may be constructed via an algorithm in Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T) functorial with respect to isomorphisms of processions of D^⊢-prime-strips; for n, n' ∈ Z the permutation symmetries of the étale-picture induce compatible poly-isomorphisms Prc(n,◦D^⊢_T) ≅ Prc(n',◦D^⊢_T) and n,◦R^LGP ≅ n',◦R^LGP, compatible with the bi-coricity poly-isomorphisms n,◦D^⊢_0 ≅ n',◦D^⊢_0 of Theorem 1.5 (iii). (ii) For n, m ∈ Z the inverses of the Kummer isomorphisms of the F-prime-strips and NF-bridges of n,mHT induce inverse Kummer isomorphisms between the vertically coric data (a), (b), (c) and the Frobenioid-theoretic data of n,mHT; as m varies, the Kummer isomorphisms of the splitting monoids (b) and of the copies of F_mod (c) are mutually compatible relative to the log-links of the n-th column, the only portions possibly related via the log-links being roots of unity (an 'addition by zero', i.e. no indeterminacy); those of the tensor packets of log-shells (a) are only 'upper semi-compatible' (Ind3), via natural inclusions at v_Q ∈ V^non_Q and natural surjections at v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q, and are precisely compatible with the respective log-volumes (Proposition 3.9 (iv)). (iii) The Kummer isomorphisms of (ii) are compatible with the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links: for (a) with the unit group portion (−)^{⊢×μ} of the link (up to (Ind2)); for (b) the identity automorphism on the objects used to construct the splitting monoids via mono-theta environments is compatible with the link relative to the Kummer isomorphisms and isomorphisms of mono-theta environments (up to (Ind2)); for (c) the identity automorphism on the objects used to construct the copies of F_mod is compatible with the link relative to the Kummer isomorphisms and cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms (up to (Ind2)).
obligations: No proof is given on pages 19 to 21; each clause refers to Theorem 3.11 'for more details'. Theorem A is the introductory form of Theorem 3.11 and carries its proof status; see the record IUT3.Thm3_11.
Check that the clauses of Theorem A agree with Theorem 3.11 (i), (ii), (iii) clause by clause, including the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3).
ambiguities: Page 20: (Ind2) is described 'in particular, [for simplicity]' at v ∈ V^non only; the archimedean part of (Ind2) is left to Theorem 3.11 (i).

Page 21: the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibilities (iii) are stated as compatibilities 'relative to the relevant Kummer isomorphisms' with a reference to (Ind2), without saying which commutative diagrams are meant; the precise form is deferred to Theorem 3.11 (iii) (a) to (d).

IUT3.ThmB.content: Introductory version of Corollary 3.12. In the situation of Theorem A, let −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} be the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume (average over j ∈ F*_l) of the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of a Θ-pilot object, relative to the relevant Kummer isomorphisms, in the multiradial representation regarded as subject to (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3); let −|log(q)| ∈ R be the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the image of a q-pilot object in the multiradial representation, not regarded as subject to these indeterminacies. Then −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Theorem A (IUT3.ThmA)

−|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞}: the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume (average over j ∈ F*_l; Remark 3.1.1 (ii), (iii), (iv); Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii); Theorem 3.11 (i) (a)) of the holomorphic hull (Remark 3.9.5 (i)) of the union of the possible images of a Θ-pilot object (Definition 3.8 (i)), relative to the relevant Kummer isomorphisms (Theorems A (ii), 3.11 (ii)), in the multiradial representation of Theorems A (i), 3.11 (i), regarded as subject to (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3)

−|log(q)| ∈ R: the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the image of a q-pilot object (Definition 3.8 (i)), relative to the relevant Kummer isomorphisms, in the same multiradial representation, not regarded as subject to (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3)
the symbol △ is the result of identifying the labels 0 and ⟨F*_l⟩ (IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (i))
IUT3.ThmB.conclusion: −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|; i.e., C_Θ ≥ −1 for any real number C_Θ ∈ R such that −|log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ·|log(q)|. Page 22 also states, as an aside, that |log(q)| > 0 'is easily computed' in terms of the q-parameters of E_F at v ∈ V^bad (≠ ∅).
obligations: No proof is given on pages 21 to 22; Theorem B is the introductory form of Corollary 3.12 and carries its proof status; see the record IUT3.Cor3_12 and its step records.
Prove |log(q)| > 0 from the definition of the q-parameters at v ∈ V^bad ≠ ∅ (page 22: 'is easily computed'; no computation is given).
ambiguities: As in Corollary 3.12, the 'i.e.' clause of page 22 reformulates only the inequality; finiteness −|log(Θ)| ∈ R is a separate conjunct (see IUT3.Cor3_12).

Page 21: the average is stated to be over j ∈ F*_l, while the q-pilot object lives over the label △, which identifies 0 and ⟨F*_l⟩ (page 22); how the label 0 enters the procession-normalized average is not stated here.

IUT3.Def1_1.content: Given an F-prime-strip †𝔉 = {†F_v} relative to initial Θ-data, defines for each v the tautological log-link †F_v → log(†F_v), log-links and full log-links (post-composition with a poly-isomorphism, resp. the full poly-isomorphism), and the log-shell I_{†F_v} inside Ψ^gp of log(†F_v); then the same objects for the whole prime-strip (iii), and mono-analytic log-shells constructed only from the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip (iv) to (vi). Writes (−)^{gp} with an underline for the formal union of the groupification with {0}.
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1
an F-prime-strip †𝔉 = {†F_v}_{v ∈ V} relative to these data (IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (i)), with associated F^⊢-, F^{⊢×μ}- and D-prime-strips
implicit_hypotheses: the functorial algorithm Ψ_cns(†𝔉) of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (i), well defined only up to †Π_v-conjugacy at nonarchimedean v
IUT3.Def1_1.conclusion: Defines: for v nonarchimedean, a Frobenioid log(†F_v) from the perfection of the units with the ind-topological field structure given by the p_v-adic logarithm, and the log-shell I_{†F_v} = (p_v^*)^{-1} times the pre-log-shell (image of the G_v(†Π_v)-invariant units), p_v^* = p_v for odd p_v and p_v^2 for p_v = 2; for v archimedean, log(†F_v) via the pointed universal covering and the complex logarithm, with log-shell the Ψ^×-orbit of the closed line segment preserved by ±1 whose endpoints differ by a generator of the kernel of the covering; the log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 as tautological log-link post-composed with a poly-isomorphism log(†𝔉) → ‡𝔉 (full when that is the full poly-isomorphism); the collection I_{†𝔉} ⊆ log(†𝔉) of log-shells; and the mono-analytic analogues I_{†𝔉^{⊢×μ}} ⊆ log(†𝔉^{⊢×μ}). See parts (i) to (vi).
external_dependencies: AbsTopIII: Definition 3.1 (iv), Proposition 3.2 (iii), (v), Definition 4.1 (iv), Proposition 4.2 (i), (ii), Definition 5.4 (iii), (v), Proposition 5.8 (v), Remark 3.1.1
IUTchI: Definition 3.1, Definition 5.2 (i), Remark 5.2.1, Remark 3.3.2, Example 3.4 (ii)
obligations: Formalize F-prime-strips, poly-isomorphisms and the full poly-isomorphism.

Construct the p_v-adic logarithm on the perfection of the units and the induced ind-topological field structure. Only the logarithm on Z_p^x for the base field Q_p is formalized (IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def, IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp).

Define the nonarchimedean log-shell and prove it is a compact topological module (the compactness is recalled from AbsTopIII, Definition 3.1 (iv)). Done only for the base field Q_p, with the Galois-invariant units taken to be Z_p^x (an identification not formalized): IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp defines the log-shell (p*)^(-1) log(Z_p^x) and proves it equal to Z_p, and IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp proves it compact. Finite extensions of Q_p are open.
Define the archimedean log-shell via the pointed universal covering and the complex logarithm.
Show that the mono-analytic constructions of (iv), (v) depend only on the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip.
ambiguities: A definition, so there is no proof; proof_status NOT_EXTRACTED records that nothing is proved here.

The phrase 'object associated to the codomain of any log-link, determined by a portion of the domain' (pages 24 to 27) is interpretive; a formalization must fix which of the two identifications is meant in each later use.

IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp.content: The log-shell of page 24 in the case where the local field is Q_p, with the Galois-invariant units taken to be Z_p^x: I = (p*)^(-1) log(Z_p^x), p* = p for odd p and p^2 for p = 2. It equals Z_p inside Q_p. The lemma padicLogShell_eq_two_mul shows that the factor (2p)^(-1) gives the same set.
explicit_hypotheses: p a prime
IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp.conclusion: padicLogShell p = range of the inclusion Z_p -> Q_p.
IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp.covers: Page 24: the log-shell as (p_v*)^(-1) times the pre-log-shell, with p_v* = p_v for odd p_v and p_v^2 for p_v = 2, in the case where the local field is Q_p.
IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp.not_covered: The Frobenioid-theoretic and anabelian setting (F-prime-strips, log-links, Psi monoids, Galois actions); finite extensions K_v of Q_p, which are the cases used in the papers; the archimedean log-shell. The identification of the G_v-invariant units with Z_p^x is an interpretation, not formalized.
ambiguities: The Galois-invariant units of page 24 are interpreted as Z_p^x for the base field Q_p.
IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT3.Def1_1.i.content: Nonarchimedean v: the units Ψ^× of Ψ_{†F_v}, their perfection Ψ^~ = (Ψ^×)^pf, the p_v-adic logarithm giving an ind-topological field structure on Ψ^~, the monoid Ψ_{log(†F_v)} ⊆ Ψ^~ of nonzero integers, the Frobenioid log(†F_v), the tautological log-link, log-links, full log-links, the pre-log-shell and the log-shell.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^non
an F-prime-strip †𝔉 as in IUT3.Def1_1
IUT3.Def1_1.i.conclusion: Definitions: log(†F_v) is the Frobenioid determined by †Π_v acting on Ψ_{log(†F_v)} (naturally isomorphic to †F_v but related to it by the diagram Ψ ⊇ Ψ^× → Ψ^~ = Ψ^gp_{log}); a log-link †F_v → ‡F_v is the tautological log-link followed by a poly-isomorphism log(†F_v) → ‡F_v; the pre-log-shell is the image in Ψ^~ of the G_v(†Π_v)-invariants of Ψ^×, a compact topological module; the log-shell is I_{†F_v} = (p_v^*)^{-1}·(pre-log-shell) ⊆ Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)}, with p_v^* = p_v if p_v is odd and p_v^2 if p_v = 2.
obligations: Construct the ind-topological field structure on the perfection of the units via the p_v-adic logarithm.
Prove compactness of the pre-log-shell (recalled from AbsTopIII, not proved here).
Check compatibility of the diagram with the actions of †Π_v and G_v(†Π_v) (asserted on page 24 as an observation).

IUT3.Def1_1.ii.content: Archimedean v: the pointed universal covering Ψ^~ of the groupification Ψ^gp, viewed also as a covering of Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N}; the complex archimedean logarithm gives a topological field structure on Ψ^~ and a Kummer structure on †U_v = †D_v; the collection of data log(†F_v), the tautological log-link, log-links, full log-links, the pre-log-shell and the log-shell.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^arc
an F-prime-strip †𝔉 as in IUT3.Def1_1
IUT3.Def1_1.ii.conclusion: Definitions: Ψ_{log(†F_v)} ⊆ Ψ^~ is the monoid of nonzero integral elements (norm ≤ 1); log(†F_v) is the triple (Ψ_{log}, †U_v, the Ψ^~-Kummer structure); the pre-log-shell is the compact subquotient of Ψ^~ determined by the units; the log-shell I_{†F_v} ⊆ Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)} is the Ψ^×_{log}-orbit of the unique closed line segment of Ψ^~ preserved by multiplication by ±1 whose endpoints differ by a generator of the kernel of Ψ^~ → Ψ^gp (equivalently, of N times such a segment for the covering of Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N}).
obligations: Construct the complex logarithm on the pointed universal covering of the topological group Ψ^gp and the induced field structure.
Prove existence and uniqueness of the closed line segment used to define the log-shell (asserted as 'uniquely determined' on page 26).
ambiguities: The equivalence of the two descriptions of the log-shell (segment for Ψ^gp versus N times the segment for Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N}) is stated with 'or, equivalently' on page 26 without argument.

IUT3.Def1_1.iii.content: Global (prime-strip) versions: the collection of ind-topological modules log(†𝔉) underlined, the F-prime-strip log(†𝔉), the tautological log-link †𝔉 → log(†𝔉), log-links and full log-links of F-prime-strips, and the log-shell I_{†𝔉} = {I_{†F_v}}.
explicit_hypotheses: an F-prime-strip †𝔉 as in IUT3.Def1_1
IUT3.Def1_1.iii.conclusion: Definitions: log(†𝔉) (underlined) = {Ψ^~_{†F_v}}_v with its additive structure and, for v nonarchimedean, its G_v(†Π_v)-action; log(†𝔉) = {log(†F_v)}_v; a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 is the tautological log-link post-composed with a poly-isomorphism log(†𝔉) → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips, full when it is the full poly-isomorphism; the log-shell I_{†𝔉} ⊆ log(†𝔉) is the collection of natural inclusions indexed by v.
obligations: Assemble the local constructions into F-prime-strips and poly-isomorphisms of F-prime-strips.

IUT3.Def1_1.iv.content: Nonarchimedean v: the log-shell with its G_v(†Π_v)-action can be built from the F^{⊢×μ}-portion alone, since only the perfection of the units is used and the perfection is unaffected by dividing by a torsion subgroup.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^non
IUT3.Def1_1.iv.conclusion: Observation and definition: I_{†F_v} ⊆ log(†F_v) (underlined), with G_v(†Π_v)-action, may be constructed solely from †F_v^{⊢×μ}; the resulting objects are written I_{†F_v^{⊢×μ}} ⊆ log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}) and regarded as constructed from †F_v^{⊢×μ}.
obligations: Prove that the perfection of the units, with its G_v-action and log-shell, depends only on the quotient of the units by its torsion subgroup (stated on page 27 as following 'immediately').

IUT3.Def1_1.v.content: Archimedean v: applying the algorithms of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (v), to the split Frobenioid portion of †F_v^⊢ gives a topological module log(†F_v^⊢) and a closed subspace I_{†F_v^⊢}; the algorithm uses only the units, and by arguing as in (ii) only their quotient by N-torsion with a pointed universal covering, so it is an algorithm in †F_v^{⊢×μ}.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^arc
IUT3.Def1_1.v.conclusion: Observation and definition: there is a functorial algorithm in †F_v^{⊢×μ} producing a topological module log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}) with a closed subspace I_{†F_v^{⊢×μ}}, corresponding to k^~(G) and I(G) of AbsTopIII.
obligations: Formalize the algorithm of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (v), and show it factors through the quotient of the unit portion by N-torsion with a pointed universal covering.

IUT3.Def1_1.vi.content: Collects the mono-analytic objects of (iv), (v) over all v.
IUT3.Def1_1.vi.conclusion: Definition: I_{†𝔉^{⊢×μ}} = {I_{†F_v^{⊢×μ}}}_v ⊆ log(†𝔉^{⊢×μ}) = {log(†F_v^{⊢×μ})}_v, regarded as constructed solely from the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip †𝔉^{⊢×μ} and not from †𝔉.
obligations: Assemble the local mono-analytic log-shells into a collection indexed by V.

IUT3.Rem1_1_1.content: (i) log-links are correspondences between portions of the ind-topological monoids in their domain and codomain; in iterates of log-links these correspondences are understood as defined only on the local units in the domains. For a global number field embedded in an idèlic product, the log-links are defined only on the product of the groups of local units. The only reason for introducing log-links is the construction of log-shells from the local units, which does not use the local or global value group portions. (ii) At v ∈ V^arc, the local units are regarded as 'Aut-holomorphic semi-germs': projective systems of arbitrarily small neighborhoods of S^1 in C^× (O^×(C_v) in O^▷(C_v)^gp), with the restricted Aut-holomorphic structure, the restricted group germ, and a choice of one of the two connected components of the complement of the units in a small neighborhood.
explicit_hypotheses: for (i): iterates of log-links as in Definition 1.1
for (ii): v ∈ V^arc, in the notation of IUTchI, Example 3.4 (i) and Remark 3.4.2
IUT3.Rem1_1_1.conclusion: (i) A convention: log-links in iterates are defined only on local units, and on products of local unit groups in the idèlic setting. (ii) Aut-holomorphic semi-germs are rigid: they admit no nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms ('one verifies immediately', page 29); hence the approach to Kummer structures via Aut-holomorphic structures and co-holomorphicizations of IUTchI, Remark 3.4.2, carries over without change (AbsTopIII, Corollary 2.3 (i)); by the discreteness of the image of the units of a number field under the logarithms of the archimedean valuations ([Lang], page 144, Theorem 5), the idèlic aspects of (i) are unaffected.
external_dependencies: Lang: page 144, Theorem 5 (discreteness of the logarithmic image of the units of a number field)
obligations: Define Aut-holomorphic semi-germs precisely (a germ of neighborhoods of S^1 in C^× with the induced holomorphic structure up to Aut, group germ and choice of component) and prove that they admit no nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms (page 29: 'one verifies immediately'; no argument is given).

The discreteness of the logarithmic image of the unit group of a number field is the Dirichlet unit theorem setting; Mathlib has the logarithmic embedding of units (NumberField.Units), which may cover the cited fact.
ambiguities: Page 29: the rigidity statement 'do not admit any nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms' does not say whether automorphisms must preserve the chosen connected component and the group germ; the list on page 29 suggests all four data are preserved.

IUT3.Rem1_1_2.content: (i) For the tautological log-link †F_v → log(†F_v) of Definition 1.1 (i) there is a tautological identification between the †Π_v's in the data giving rise to its domain and codomain; for the full log-link †F_v → ‡F_v, †Π_v and ‡Π_v are related only by a full poly-isomorphism. The specific isomorphism of the tautological log-link is a 'rigidifying path' constructed using the Frobenius-like monoids related by the p_v-adic logarithm (Galois-equivariance of its power series). 'Path' is meant as in the étale groupoid, but allowing arbitrary automorphism indeterminacies. The paper works mainly with the full log-link, because the multiradial algorithms of §3 must express the relation between the étale-like Π_v's in purely étale-like terms, free of dependence on Frobenius-like monoids; this is achieved by the 'tautologically indeterminate isomorphism' underlying the full log-link. (ii) An analogous discussion applies for v ∈ V^arc (Definition 1.1 (ii)); routine details are left to the reader.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Definition 1.1 (i) (for (i)) and Definition 1.1 (ii), v ∈ V^arc (for (ii))
IUT3.Rem1_1_2.conclusion: (i) The full log-link relates †Π_v and ‡Π_v only up to a full poly-isomorphism, whereas the tautological log-link carries a specific isomorphism depending on Frobenius-like monoids; the full log-link is the one used in the paper, so that the relation between domain and codomain Π_v's is free of any dependence on Frobenius-like monoids. (ii) The same holds at v ∈ V^arc (details left to the reader, page 30).
obligations: Formalize the difference between the two links as: the tautological link carries one distinguished isomorphism of the Π_v's, the full link carries the full poly-isomorphism (the set of all isomorphisms).
ambiguities: Page 30: for v ∈ V^arc 'we leave the routine details to the reader'; the archimedean analogue is not written out.

IUT3.Prop1_2.content: Properties of a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 between F-prime-strips, read through the diagrams (*non) Ψ ⊇ Ψ^× → log(†F_v) = Ψ^gp_{log} ≅ Ψ^gp_{‡F_v} and (*arc) Ψ ⊆ Ψ^gp ↞ log(†F_v) = Ψ^gp_{log} ≅ Ψ^gp_{‡F_v}: coricity of D-prime-strips (i), compatibility with ring structures (ii) and with log-volumes (iii), failure of Kummer compatibility (iv), properties of holomorphic (v), mono-analytic (vi) to (viii) and coric holomorphic (ix) log-shells, and the Frobenius-picture (x).
explicit_hypotheses: F-prime-strips †𝔉 = {†F_v} and ‡𝔉 = {‡F_v} relative to the given initial Θ-data (IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (i))
a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 (IUT3.Def1_1.iii)
implicit_hypotheses: the associated F^{⊢×μ}-, D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, and the poly-isomorphisms on the right of (*non), (*arc) induced by the log-link
IUT3.Prop1_2.conclusion: (i) the log-link induces poly-isomorphisms †D ≅ ‡D, †D^⊢ ≅ ‡D^⊢ and Ψ_cns(†D) ≅ Ψ_cns(‡D); (ii) the diagrams are compatible with the ring structures on both ends; (iii) they are compatible with p_v-adic, angular and radial log-volumes; (iv) the Kummer isomorphisms are not compatible with the poly-isomorphism of (i); (v) holomorphic log-shells are compact, of finite log-volume, and contain the stated invariant submonoids; (vi), (vii) mono-analytic log-shells are constructible from D^⊢_v, with compatible (poly-)isomorphisms to the holomorphic ones; (viii) these assemble over V; (ix) for the full log-link from F(*D) to itself there is an algorithm in *D giving coric holomorphic log-shells; (x) a Z-chain of full log-links gives chains of full poly-isomorphisms of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, the Frobenius-picture, with a Z-translation symmetry and no arbitrary permutation symmetries. Statements in the part records.
definitions_required: p_v-adic, angular and radial log-volume (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7, Corollary 5.10)
external_dependencies: AbsTopIII: Proposition 5.7 (i), (ii), Proposition 5.8 (ii), (v), Corollary 5.5 (iv), (v), Corollary 5.10 (i), (ii), (iv), Definition 5.4 (iii), (v), §0
IUTchII: Corollary 4.5 (i), (ii), Corollary 4.6 (i), (ii), Remark 4.5.1 (i), Example 1.8 (iv), Definition 4.9
obligations: See part records. The proof (page 35) says only that all assertions follow immediately from the definitions and the cited references, so each part reduces to the cited results of AbsTopIII and IUTchII.
ambiguities: The proof on page 35 is one sentence; no derivation is given for any part beyond the references.

IUT3.Prop1_2.i.content: Coricity of associated D-prime-strips: the log-link does not change the étale-like data.
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop1_2.i.conclusion: The log-link induces poly-isomorphisms †D ≅ ‡D and †D^⊢ ≅ ‡D^⊢; the one between D-prime-strips induces a poly-isomorphism Ψ_cns(†D) ≅ Ψ_cns(‡D) of the collections of monoids with auxiliary data of IUTchII, Corollary 4.5 (i).
obligations: Show that the tautological log-link leaves †Π_v (resp. the archimedean data †D_v) unchanged, so that any log-link induces the stated poly-isomorphisms; then apply the functoriality of Ψ_cns.

explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop1_2.ii.conclusion: At v ∈ V^non the natural †Π_v-actions on the four Ψ's of (*non) are compatible with the ind-topological ring structures on Ψ^gp_{†F_v} and Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)}; at v ∈ V^arc the co-holomorphicizations determined by the natural Ψ^gp_{†F_v}- and Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)} (= Ψ^~)-Kummer structures on †U_v, which are compatible with (*arc), are compatible with the topological ring structures on these two groups.
definitions_required: Kummer structure on an Aut-holomorphic space
obligations: Prove Galois equivariance of the p_v-adic logarithm on the perfection of the units, and the corresponding archimedean statement for Kummer structures.

explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
implicit_hypotheses: the weight N convention of Remark 1.2.1 (i) for Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N} at archimedean v
IUT3.Prop1_2.iii.conclusion: At v ∈ V^non, (*non) is compatible with the natural p_v-adic log-volumes on the subsets of †Π_v-invariants of Ψ^gp_{†F_v} and Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)}; at v ∈ V^arc, (*arc) is compatible with the natural angular log-volume on Ψ^×_{†F_v} and the natural radial log-volume on Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)}.
definitions_required: p_v-adic log-volume, angular and radial log-volume (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7, Corollary 5.10 (ii))
obligations: Define the log-volumes on both ends and prove that the p_v-adic logarithm preserves them on the relevant compact subsets (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7).
ambiguities: 'Compatible' is not defined on page 31; Remark 1.2.1 (ii) (page 35) reads the archimedean case as invariance of the natural metrics under the log-link. A formalization must choose: equality of the log-volumes of corresponding subsets is the natural reading.

IUT3.Prop1_2.iv.content: Kummer theory: the log-link does not commute with the Kummer isomorphisms.
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop1_2.iv.conclusion: The Kummer isomorphisms Ψ_cns(†𝔉) ≅ Ψ_cns(†D) and Ψ_cns(‡𝔉) ≅ Ψ_cns(‡D) of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (i), fail to be compatible with the poly-isomorphism Ψ_cns(†D) ≅ Ψ_cns(‡D) of (i), relative to (*non), (*arc), viewed as relating Ψ_{†F_v} and Ψ_{‡F_v} via log(†𝔉) ≅ ‡𝔉.
obligations: State non-compatibility precisely: the square formed by the two Kummer isomorphisms, the log-link and the poly-isomorphism of (i) does not commute (for every member of the poly-isomorphism); prove it, for example by exhibiting an element whose two images differ (the logarithm is not multiplicative).
ambiguities: A negative statement: 'fail to be compatible' needs a quantifier over the poly-isomorphism and over elements to become a precise claim.

IUT3.Prop1_2.v.content: Holomorphic log-shells: compactness and containment properties.
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop1_2.v.conclusion: At v ∈ V^non, the log-shell I_{†F_v} ⊆ log(†F_v) (≅ Ψ^gp_{‡F_v}) is (a) compact, hence of finite log-volume; (b) contains the submonoid of †Π_v-invariants of Ψ_{log(†F_v)}; (c) contains the image of the submonoid of †Π_v-invariants of Ψ^×_{†F_v}. At v ∈ V^arc, I_{†F_v} is (a) compact, hence of finite radial log-volume; (b) contains Ψ_{log(†F_v)}; (c) its image in Ψ^gp_{†F_v} contains Ψ^×_{†F_v} (in essence the pre-log-shell).
obligations: Prove compactness of the log-shell and the inclusions (b), (c) at nonarchimedean and archimedean v; the nonarchimedean inclusions depend on the normalizing factor (p_v^*)^{-1} of Definition 1.1 (i). For the base field Q_p at nonarchimedean v (with the Galois-invariant units taken to be Z_p^x, not formalized), compactness and the inclusions (b), (c) are proved in IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp; finite log-volume, finite extensions of Q_p and archimedean v are open.

IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp.content: Properties (a_non), (b_non), (c_non) of Proposition 1.2 (v) for the log-shell of Q_p (with the interpretations of the fragment IUT3.Def1_1.frag.log_shell_Qp): Z_p is contained in the log-shell; the log-shell is compact; log(Z_p^x) is contained in the log-shell.
explicit_hypotheses: p a prime
IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp.conclusion: range of the inclusion Z_p -> Q_p is contained in padicLogShell p; padicLogShell p is compact; range (u mapsto padicLogUnit p u) is contained in padicLogShell p.
IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp.covers: Pages 31 and 32, (v) at v in V^non: (a_non) compactness, (b_non) the log-shell contains the invariants of the integers of the codomain (here Z_p), (c_non) it contains the image of the invariant units (here log(Z_p^x)), for the local field Q_p.
IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp.not_covered: Finite log-volume in (a_non); the log-link and Frobenioid setting; finite extensions of Q_p; the archimedean properties (a_arc) to (c_arc).
ambiguities: The invariants of Psi_log(F_v) and of Psi^x are interpreted as Z_p and Z_p^x for the base field Q_p.
IUT3.Prop1_2.v.frag.nonarch_Qp.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT3.Prop1_2.vi.content: Nonarchimedean mono-analytic log-shells built from the D^⊢-prime-strip, with compatible isomorphisms to the holomorphic log-shells.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^non
†D^⊢_v = B(†G_v)^0, the portion of †D^⊢ indexed by v
IUT3.Prop1_2.vi.conclusion: There is a functorial algorithm in †D^⊢_v producing log(†D^⊢_v) = {†G_v acting on k^~(†G_v)} and the mono-analytic log-shell I_{†D^⊢_v} = I(†G_v) ⊆ k^~(†G_v) with a p_v-adic log-volume; a functorial algorithm in †F_v^{⊢×μ} producing an Ism-orbit of isomorphisms log(†D^⊢_v) ≅ log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}); and a functorial algorithm in †F_v producing isomorphisms log(†D^⊢_v) ≅ log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}) ≅ log(†F_v) (≅ Ψ^gp_{‡F_v}). These are compatible with each other, with the †G_v- and G_v(†Π_v)-actions (via †G_v = G_v(†Π_v)), with the log-shells and with the log-volumes.
obligations: Formalize the mono-anabelian reconstruction of k^~(G) and I(G) from a profinite group of the type of G_v (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (ii)).
Prove the compatibilities with the actions, log-shells and log-volumes.

IUT3.Prop1_2.vii.content: Archimedean mono-analytic log-shells built from the D^⊢-prime-strip, related to the holomorphic ones by poly-isomorphisms that are orbits under independent ±1 actions.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^arc
†D^⊢_v regarded as an object of the category TM^⊢ of IUTchI, Example 3.4 (ii)
IUT3.Prop1_2.vii.conclusion: There is a functorial algorithm in †D^⊢_v producing log(†D^⊢_v) = k^~(†G_v) and I_{†D^⊢_v} = I(†G_v) ⊆ k^~(†G_v) with angular and radial log-volumes; a functorial algorithm in †F_v^{⊢×μ} producing a poly-isomorphism log(†D^⊢_v) ≅ log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}), the orbit of isomorphisms under the independent {±1}-actions on the direct factors of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (v); and a functorial algorithm in †F_v producing such poly-isomorphisms log(†D^⊢_v) ≅ log(†F_v^{⊢×μ}) ≅ log(†F_v) (≅ Ψ^gp_{‡F_v}). These are compatible with one another, with the log-shells and with the angular and radial log-volumes.
obligations: Formalize AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (v), and the {±1}-orbit indeterminacy on each direct factor.

IUT3.Prop1_2.viii.content: Mono-analytic log-shells assembled over all v.
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †𝔉 → ‡𝔉 of F-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop1_2.viii.conclusion: The (poly-)isomorphisms of (vi), (vii) give collections indexed by V: log(†D^⊢) ≅ log(†𝔉^{⊢×μ}), I_{†D^⊢} ≅ I_{†𝔉^{⊢×μ}}, log(†D^⊢) ≅ log(†𝔉^{⊢×μ}) ≅ log(†𝔉) (≅ Ψ^gp_cns(‡𝔉)) and I_{†D^⊢} ≅ I_{†𝔉^{⊢×μ}} ≅ I_{†𝔉}, where each Ψ^gp_{‡F_v}, v ∈ V^non, carries its G_v(‡Π_v)-action.
obligations: Assemble the local poly-isomorphisms into poly-isomorphisms of collections indexed by V.

IUT3.Prop1_2.ix.content: Coric holomorphic log-shells: for the full log-link from the F-prime-strip determined by a D-prime-strip to itself, the holomorphic log-shells can be constructed from the D-prime-strip.
explicit_hypotheses: a D-prime-strip *D, with F(*D) the F-prime-strip determined by Ψ_cns(*D) (IUTchII, Remark 4.5.1 (i))
the given log-link F(*D) → F(*D) is the full log-link
IUT3.Prop1_2.ix.conclusion: There is a functorial algorithm in *D constructing a collection of topological subspaces I_{*D} := I_{†𝔉} (coric holomorphic log-shells) of Ψ^gp_cns(*D), naturally identified with Ψ^gp_cns(‡𝔉), together with natural isomorphisms I_{*D^⊢} ≅ I_{*D}, where *D^⊢ is the D^⊢-prime-strip determined by *D.
obligations: Show that, for the full log-link, the log-shell is invariant under the full poly-isomorphism and hence descends to an object constructed from *D.

IUT3.Prop1_2.x.content: Frobenius-picture: a Z-indexed chain of full log-links of F-prime-strips induces chains of full poly-isomorphisms of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, depicted as an oriented graph with a horizontal chain of vertices and Kummer arrows to a coric vertex ◦. The graph admits a Z translation symmetry fixing ◦ but no arbitrary permutation symmetries; for instance no automorphism swaps two adjacent vertices.
explicit_hypotheses: a collection of distinct F-prime-strips indexed by Z linked by full log-links
IUT3.Prop1_2.x.conclusion: Chains of full poly-isomorphisms; Z-action; no adjacent swap.
obligations: Formalize the oriented graph and verify that its automorphism group is Z (a purely combinatorial obligation once the graph is fixed).

IUT3.Rem1_2_1.content: (i) In the situation of Definition 1.1 (ii), Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N} carries the metric descended from Ψ^gp but is given weight N, so its log-volume equals that of Ψ^×. (ii) The archimedean compatibility of Proposition 1.2 (iii) between angular and radial log-volumes can be read as invariance of metrics: on a complex archimedean field k, metrics (Riemannian, compatible with both almost complex structures, translation invariant) form an R_{>0}-torsor, and via k^× ≅ O^×_k × R_{>0} any metric is determined by its restriction to O^×_k or to R_{>0}.
explicit_hypotheses: for (i): the situation of IUT3.Def1_1.ii, N ∈ N_{≥1}
for (ii): a complex archimedean field k
IUT3.Rem1_2_1.conclusion: (i) A convention: the weight N makes log-volumes on Ψ^gp/Ψ^{μ_N} agree with those on Ψ^×, so passing to the quotient does not affect log-volume computations. (ii) Any metric on k (in the stated sense) is uniquely determined by its restriction to O^×_k ⊆ k or to R_{>0} ⊆ k; hence the compatibility of Proposition 1.2 (iii) is equivalent to invariance of the natural metrics under the log-link.
definitions_required: metric on k in the sense of page 35
obligations: Prove that translation-invariant Riemannian metrics on C compatible with both complex structures form an R_{>0}-torsor and are determined by their restriction to the unit circle or to R_{>0} (stated on page 35 as verified 'immediately'). This is elementary and within reach of Mathlib.
ambiguities: 'Compatible with the two natural almost complex structures' (page 35) is not defined further; the natural reading is that the metric is Hermitian for both i and −i, which for a translation-invariant metric means a positive multiple of the standard one.

IUT3.Rem1_2_2.content: The Frobenius-picture diagram is far from commutative; coric holomorphic log-shells satisfy only upper semi-commutativity; there is no lower semi-commutativity; the diagram is commutative with respect to log-volumes.
obligations: Make 'upper semi-commutativity' precise as a containment of images along different paths.
ambiguities: 'commutative with respect to log-volumes' is not defined as a formal property; reading it as equality of log-volumes of images along different paths is an interpretation.

IUT3.Rem1_2_3.content: (i) In the notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), a multiplicative indeterminacy by a subgroup H ⊆ O^×_k acting on O^▷_k at some '•' of the diagram Γ⃗ gives rise to an additive indeterminacy by log_k(H) on the copy of O_k at the subsequent '•'; if H consists of roots of unity, then log_k(H) = {0}, so the additive indeterminacy ceases to exist. This is to be applied in §3 to the constant multiple rigidity of the canonical splittings of theta and Gaussian monoids. (ii) Global arithmetic line bundles amount to multiplicative translates by f ∈ F^×_mod of the product of the O^×_k's over v ∈ V; such translates are disjoint except when f is a unit at all v ∈ V, which by elementary algebraic number theory happens exactly when f is a root of unity; hence quotients by F^×_mod at one '•' give an additive indeterminacy by logarithms of roots of unity at the next '•', which vanishes at v ∈ V^non and at v ∈ V^arc amounts to quotients of the copies of O^×_k (i.e., S^1) by some finite subgroup.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), (ii): local fields k, the diagram Γ⃗ of iterated log-links
for (i): a subgroup H ⊆ O^×_k
for (ii): f ∈ F^×_mod, v ranging over V
IUT3.Rem1_2_3.conclusion: (i) A multiplicative indeterminacy by H ⊆ O^×_k becomes an additive indeterminacy by log_k(H) after one log-link, and log_k(H) = {0} when H consists of roots of unity. (ii) Multiplicative translates of ∏_v O^×_k by f ∈ F^×_mod are disjoint unless f is a root of unity, so the multiplicative action of F^×_mod yields at the next step an additive indeterminacy by logarithms of roots of unity, trivial at v ∈ V^non and a finite-subgroup quotient of S^1 at v ∈ V^arc.
external_dependencies: Lang: page 144, proof of Theorem 5 (an element of a number field that is a unit at every place is a root of unity)
obligations: Prove that log_k vanishes on roots of unity of a p-adic field (log of a torsion element is zero) and that the image of a subgroup H under log_k is the additive indeterminacy described.

The fact used in (ii), that an element of F^×_mod with absolute value 1 at every place is a root of unity, is cited from [Lang]; Mathlib has NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_eq_one for algebraic integers with all archimedean absolute values 1, which together with integrality at all finite places covers it.
ambiguities: Page 39, (ii): 'unit at all v ∈ V' must include the archimedean v (absolute value 1); the text uses 'unit' for both kinds of place.

IUT3.Rem1_2_4.content: (i) The log-link is incompatible with the ring structures of Ψ^gp_{†F_v} and Ψ^gp_{log(†F_v)} (it does not arise from a ring homomorphism); this barrier is the 'log-wall' of AbsTopIII, §I4. Hence objects whose structure depends on these ring structures cannot be transported via the log-link by transport of structure: the log-wall is incompatible with conventional scheme-theoretic basepoints, with Galois groups defined as automorphism groups of rings, and with Kummer theory (Proposition 1.2 (iv)). The only structure of interest manifestly compatible with the log-link is the associated D-prime-strip (abstract topological groups at v ∈ V^non, abstract Aut-holomorphic spaces at v ∈ V^arc). (ii) Further structures incompatible with the log-wall: (a) the additive structure on the image of the Kummer map; (b) in the birational situation, the collection of closed points determining the affine curve, equivalently the natural outer surjection Π^birat_v ↠ Π_v. (iii) Writing Δ^birat_v, Δ_v for the kernels of Π^birat_v ↠ G_v, Π_v ↠ G_v, the groups G_v, Δ^birat_v, Δ_v with their outer G_v-actions make sense on both sides of the log-wall, but a particular outer surjection Δ^birat_v ↠ Δ_v fails to be compatible with the log-link (Fig. 1.2: independent basepoint indeterminacies obstruct the relation between birational and affine geometric fundamental groups); this is reminiscent of compatibility of outer homomorphisms (IUTchI, Remark 4.5.1 (i)).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Proposition 1.2 (ii)
for (ii) (b), (iii): the birational situation, with Π^birat_v the absolute Galois group of the function field of the affine curve giving rise to Π_v; for simplicity v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non
IUT3.Rem1_2_4.conclusion: Structures that depend essentially on ring structures (scheme-theoretic basepoints, Galois groups as ring automorphism groups, Kummer theory, the additive structure on the Kummer image, the outer surjection Π^birat_v ↠ Π_v and the induced Δ^birat_v ↠ Δ_v) are not compatible with the log-link, whereas the associated D-prime-strip is compatible with it (Proposition 1.2 (i), (ii)).
obligations: Make 'incompatible with the log-link' precise (for instance: no ring homomorphism induces the log-link; or: a given structure is not preserved by some automorphism of the domain data that the log-link does not see) and prove each instance; the arguments are deferred to AbsTopIII, Remark 3.7.7.
ambiguities: 'Incompatible' and 'manifestly compatible' (pages 39 to 40) are not given a formal meaning; the remark is explanatory.
Fig. 1.2 (page 41) is labeled with a question mark between the birational and affine geometric fundamental groups; its content is the sentence of (iii), not a separate claim.

IUT3.Rem1_2_5.content: Relates the incompatibility of the log-wall with ring/scheme-theoretic structures (Remark 1.2.4) to avoiding fixed ring/scheme-theoretic reference models in mono-anabelian algorithms: such algorithms are those whose dependence on data from fixed reference models is invariant, or coric, with respect to the action of log on these models; AbsTopIII, §3, gives a precise formulation via observables, families of homotopies and telecores.
IUT3.Rem1_2_5.conclusion: Interpretive: mono-anabelian construction algorithms in the context of the log-link are characterized as algorithms whose dependence on fixed reference models is coric with respect to log; the failure of the ring structure of a fixed reference model to be coric is formulated in AbsTopIII, Corollary 3.6 (iv) and Corollary 3.7 (iv). No mathematical assertion beyond the cited results.
obligations: None of its own; a formalization of 'coric with respect to log' would follow AbsTopIII, §3.
ambiguities: Remark without a proof; 'invariant' and 'coric' are used informally here and defined only in AbsTopIII.

IUT3.Prop1_3.content: Log-links between Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, defined from an isomorphism of the associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters by applying Definition 1.1 (iii) to each F-prime-strip in the Θ- and Θ^±-bridges.
explicit_hypotheses: Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters †HT and ‡HT relative to the given initial Θ-data (IUTchI, Definition 6.13 (i)), with associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters (IUTchI, Definition 6.13 (ii))
IUT3.Prop1_3.conclusion: (i) a fixed isomorphism Ξ of the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters determines a log-link †F_□ → ‡F_□ for each F-prime-strip †F_□ among †F_>, †F_≻ and the constituent F-prime-strips of the capsules †F_J, †F_T; the collection is a log-link †HT → ‡HT (full when Ξ is the full poly-isomorphism); (ii) every log-link of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters induces a poly-isomorphism of the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters and coincides with the log-link built from it in (i); (iii) each constituent log-link satisfies the analogues of Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (ix); (iv) a Z-chain of full log-links of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters gives a chain of full poly-isomorphisms of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters and an oriented graph with a Z-translation symmetry fixing the core and no arbitrary permutation symmetries. Statements in the part records.
obligations: See part records. The proof (page 43) says that all assertions follow immediately from the definitions and the cited references.
ambiguities: The proof on page 43 is one sentence; no derivation is given beyond the references.

IUT3.Prop1_3.i.content: Construction of the log-link between Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters.
explicit_hypotheses: an isomorphism Ξ: †HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} ≅ ‡HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters
†F_□ one of the F-prime-strips †F_>, †F_≻ of the Θ- and Θ^±-bridges or a constituent F-prime-strip of the capsules †F_J, †F_T; ‡F_□ the corresponding F-prime-strip of ‡HT
IUT3.Prop1_3.i.conclusion: The poly-isomorphism determined by Ξ between the D-prime-strips of †F_□ and ‡F_□ uniquely determines a poly-isomorphism log(†F_□) ≅ ‡F_□ (IUTchI, Corollary 5.3 (ii)), hence a log-link †F_□ → ‡F_□. Definition: a log-link †HT → ‡HT is Ξ together with these log-links for all □; for a poly-isomorphism Ξ it is the collection over its constituent isomorphisms; for the full poly-isomorphism it is the full log-link.
obligations: Prove that a poly-isomorphism of D-prime-strips determines a unique poly-isomorphism of the associated F-prime-strips (IUTchI, Corollary 5.3 (ii)).
Define the log-link of Hodge theaters as a structured collection of data.

IUT3.Prop1_3.ii.content: Coricity of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters under log-links.
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → ‡HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}
IUT3.Prop1_3.ii.conclusion: Any log-link †HT → ‡HT induces (and may be thought of as lying over) a poly-isomorphism †HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} ≅ ‡HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF}, and coincides with the log-link constructed in (i) from that poly-isomorphism.
obligations: Follows from the definition in (i) once log-links are defined as data containing Ξ; a formalization checks the round trip.
ambiguities: Since by (i) a log-link consists of Ξ together with the induced log-links, the assertion appears definitional; the content lies in the uniqueness of (i).

IUT3.Prop1_3.iii.content: Further properties: each constituent log-link of a log-link of Hodge theaters inherits Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (ix).
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → ‡HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}
an F-prime-strip †F_□ as in (i)
IUT3.Prop1_3.iii.conclusion: For each †F_□, the log-link †F_□ → ‡F_□ has the properties corresponding to Proposition 1.2 (ii) to (ix): simultaneous compatibility with ring structures and log-volumes, failure of Kummer compatibility, and the log-shell properties.
obligations: Apply Proposition 1.2 to each constituent log-link; the blocking is inherited from Proposition 1.2.
ambiguities: Proposition 1.2 (ix) concerns the full log-link from F(*D) to itself; how it applies to an arbitrary log-link of Hodge theaters is not stated.

explicit_hypotheses: a collection {nHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n ∈ Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data
IUT3.Prop1_3.iv.conclusion: The full log-links nHT → (n+1)HT give an infinite chain inducing a chain of full poly-isomorphisms of the associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters; this is an oriented graph with a horizontal chain of vertices and Kummer arrows (implicit in (iii)) to a core vertex ◦ standing for the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater up to isomorphism. The graph admits a natural Z-action by translation fixing ◦ but no arbitrary permutation symmetries; for instance no automorphism switches two adjacent vertices and fixes the others.
obligations: Formalize the oriented graph and prove that it has translation automorphisms and no automorphism transposing two adjacent vertices while fixing the rest (combinatorial, once the graph is fixed).
ambiguities: 'Does not admit arbitrary permutation symmetries' refers to automorphisms of the oriented graph; whether the claim concerns automorphisms of the graph or of the underlying diagram of Hodge theaters is not spelled out.

IUT3.Rem1_3_1.content: Explains why Proposition 1.3 (i) builds the log-link first for a single isomorphism Ξ rather than a poly-isomorphism: to keep compatibility with the ±-synchronization inherent in a Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater.
IUT3.Rem1_3_1.conclusion: Methodological: constructing the log-link from a single Ξ maintains compatibility with the ±-synchronization of IUTchI, Remark 6.12.4 (iii), and IUTchII, Remark 4.5.3 (iii). No new assertion.
obligations: None of its own.
ambiguities: The claim that a poly-isomorphism would break ±-synchronization is stated without argument.

IUT3.Rem1_3_2.content: In Proposition 1.3 (i) the constituent F-prime-strips †F_t, t ∈ T, of the capsule †F_T are treated without regard to the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetries; nevertheless the log-links attached to them, more precisely to the labeled collections of monoids Ψ_cns(†F_≻)_t, are compatible with the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetrizing isomorphisms of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (iii), hence with the conjugate synchronization they determine.
explicit_hypotheses: the construction of IUT3.Prop1_3.i
IUT3.Rem1_3_2.conclusion: The log-links associated to the labeled collections Ψ_cns(†F_≻)_t, t ∈ T, are compatible with the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetrizing isomorphisms and with the resulting conjugate synchronization. Proof: 'verifies immediately'; details left to the reader (page 44), with a pointer to Step (vi) of the proof of Corollary 3.12.
obligations: State the compatibility as commutativity of the square formed by a symmetrizing isomorphism between labels t, t' and the log-links at t and t', and prove it (it should reduce to functoriality of the log-link construction in the F-prime-strip).
ambiguities: Routine details are left to the reader (page 44); no argument is given.

IUT3.Rem1_3_3.content: (i) The relationship between Frobenioid-theoretic portions of the Hodge theaters in the domain and codomain of the log-link of Proposition 1.3 (i) contains no data incompatible, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms, with the coricity of étale-like structures of Proposition 1.3 (ii), because these portions are fully faithfully controlled by étale-like structures via functorial algorithms. (ii) The global portion of the Θ^ell-bridges contains no Frobenioid-theoretic data, so the issue concerns (a) the F-prime-strips, (b) the underlying Θ-Hodge theaters, (c) the global portion of the NF-bridges; (c) gives independent basepoints for the F_l^*-symmetry, (b) and part of (a) are related only by full poly-isomorphisms, and the F-prime-strips in the Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater are the delicate part, handled because ±-synchronizations are defined via the coric D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater.
explicit_hypotheses: the context of IUT3.Prop1_3
IUT3.Rem1_3_3.conclusion: Interpretive observation: the Frobenioid-theoretic relationships across the log-link of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters are compatible with coricity of the étale-like structures; justified by reference to IUTchI, Corollary 5.3, Corollary 5.6, Remark 6.12.4 (iii), Remark 6.12.6 (iii), Examples 4.3, 4.4, and IUTchII, Remark 4.5.3 (iii), Remark 4.7.6.
external_dependencies: IUTchI: Corollary 5.3 (i), (ii), (iv), Corollary 5.6 (i), (ii), (iii), Definition 6.11 (ii), Examples 4.3, 4.4, Remark 6.12.4 (iii), Remark 6.12.6 (iii)
obligations: Make precise what 'data incompatible with coricity relative to the Kummer isomorphisms' means and prove its absence for each of (a), (b), (c).
ambiguities: The central notion, data 'incompatible relative to the Kummer isomorphisms with the coricity property' (page 44), is defined only by reference to Remark 1.2.4 (ii), (iii); the observation is argued informally.

IUT3.Def1_4.content: The log-theta-lattice: given distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters n,mHT indexed by (n,m) ∈ Z × Z, the diagram whose vertical arrows n,mHT → n,m+1HT are full log-links and whose horizontal arrows n,mHT → n+1,mHT are Θ^{×μ}-links (non-Gaussian) or Θ^{×μ}_gau-links (Gaussian) of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (iii).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Proposition 1.3
a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m ∈ Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data
IUT3.Def1_4.conclusion: Definition: either of the two diagrams (vertical arrows: full log-links increasing m; horizontal arrows: Θ^{×μ}-links, resp. Θ^{×μ}_gau-links, increasing n) is a log-theta-lattice, called non-Gaussian, resp. Gaussian; it is represented by the oriented graph Z × Z with arrows (n,m) → (n,m+1) and (n,m) → (n+1,m), the vertices standing for the n,mHT.
obligations: Represent the lattice as a Z × Z-indexed diagram with two kinds of arrows, the vertical ones full log-links and the horizontal ones Θ^{×μ}- or Θ^{×μ}_gau-links, once these links are formalized.
ambiguities: A definition, so there is no proof. The diagram is not required to commute; Remark 1.4.1 (i) says its squares are far from 1-commutative.

IUT3.Rem1_4_1.content: (i) The squares of the log-theta-lattice are far from 1-commutative: vertical arrows use the logarithms at v, which depend on local ring structures, while horizontal arrows are incompatible with these ring structures. (ii) Horizontal arrows identify the O^{×μ}'s on both sides; to use log-shells, the Hodge theater in which one works must be the codomain of a log-link, so each horizontal arrow obligates a subsequent vertical arrow; by (i), multiradiality can then only be realized with objects invariant under the vertical arrows (vertical cores). (iii) Analogy with p-adic Teichmüller theory: vertical arrows correspond to Frobenius in positive characteristic, horizontal arrows to the mixed characteristic extension structure of Witt vectors (Fig. 1.3).
explicit_hypotheses: a log-theta-lattice as in IUT3.Def1_4
IUT3.Rem1_4_1.conclusion: (i) The squares of each log-theta-lattice are not 1-commutative. (ii) Multiradiality, that is simultaneous compatibility with the arithmetic holomorphic structures on both sides of a horizontal arrow, requires working with objects invariant under the Z-action of Proposition 1.3 (iv) on vertical lines. (iii) An analogy, not an assertion.
obligations: State non-commutativity of a square precisely: which two composites of a log-link and a Θ^{×μ}-link are compared, as maps between which objects, and prove that they differ.
Make 'can only be realized' in (ii) a precise necessity statement.
ambiguities: 'Far from being 1-commutative' (page 46) is not quantified; even the composites around a square are not maps between the same objects without further identifications.
The necessity claim in (ii) (page 47) is argued by reference to Remark 1.2.2 (iii), not proved.

IUT3.Rem1_4_2.content: (i) Horizontal and vertical arrows of the log-theta-lattice (Definition 1.4) are both incompatible with the local ring structures and with conventional scheme-theoretic basepoints. The linking data of the vertical arrows (the log-link) is rigid and corresponds to a single fixed rigid arithmetic holomorphic structure in which addition and multiplication are subject to 'rotations' (AbsTopIII, §I3); the linking data of the horizontal arrows (Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links), concretely the O^{×μ}'s at v ∈ V^non, is subject to a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy, which obliterates the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line. (ii) If one tries to force the horizontal arrows to be compatible with the arithmetic holomorphic structures by declaring, as for the log-link, that they induce isomorphisms of the Π_v's at v ∈ V^non, the common structure rigidified by the isomorphic copies of Π_v is obliterated whenever a nontrivial element of Ẑ^× acts on the O^{×μ}; one must then record paths of 'Π_v-rigidifying' and 'Ẑ^×-indeterminacy' operations, and the horizontal lines of the lattice amount to universal covering spaces of the resulting loops; so such an attempt gives no substantive simplification.
explicit_hypotheses: the log-theta-lattices of Definition 1.4
for simplicity v ∈ V^non
IUT3.Rem1_4_2.conclusion: The horizontal arrows of the log-theta-lattice carry a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy on the O^{×μ}'s that obliterates the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line, unlike the rigid vertical arrows; forcing the horizontal arrows to induce isomorphisms of the Π_v's leads to recording paths of rigidifying and Ẑ^×-indeterminacy operations and does not simplify the theory.
obligations: Formalize the Ẑ^×-indeterminacy as the action of Ẑ^× on O^{×μ} and the claim that it does not preserve the ring structure carried by a fixed copy of Π_v.
ambiguities: The conclusion of (ii) ('does not result in any substantive simplification', page 48) is a judgment about the organization of the theory, not a mathematical statement.

explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε)
a Gaussian log-theta-lattice
IUT3.Thm1_5.conclusion: The conjunction of parts (i) to (v), as recorded in the part records: (i) Full poly-isomorphisms n,m HT^{D-Θ±ellNF} ≅ n,m+1 HT^{D-Θ±ellNF}; (ii) Full poly-isomorphisms along rows; (iii) F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△), up to a certain class of isomorphisms, is invariant under both kinds of arrows; (iv) Poly-isomorphisms of log-shell pairs I ⊆ log(−); (v) Isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioid data across the lattice.
obligations: See the part records.

IUT3.Thm1_5.i.content: Vertical coricity: vertical arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms of the associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, n fixed, m varying.
explicit_hypotheses: inherits the hypotheses of IUT3.Thm1_5
IUT3.Thm1_5.i.conclusion: Full poly-isomorphisms n,m HT^{D-Θ±ellNF} ≅ n,m+1 HT^{D-Θ±ellNF}.
obligations: Show the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater is unchanged up to full poly-isomorphism by a log-link.

IUT3.Thm1_5.ii.content: Horizontal coricity: horizontal arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms of the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips n,m 𝔉_△^{⊢×μ} → n+1,m 𝔉_△^{⊢×μ}, m fixed.
explicit_hypotheses: inherits the hypotheses of IUT3.Thm1_5
obligations: Formalize F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and the Θ^{×μ}-link.

IUT3.Thm1_5.iii.content: Bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△): poly-isomorphisms induced by (i) along columns and by (ii) along rows; the vertical collection is in general strictly smaller than the horizontal one, and the horizontal poly-isomorphisms are not full. Composition gives poly-isomorphisms for arbitrary (n,m), (n',m'). Kummer isomorphisms n,m 𝔉^{⊢×μ}_△ ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△) compatible with (ii).
IUT3.Thm1_5.iii.conclusion: F^{⊢×μ}_△(n,m D^⊢_△), up to a certain class of isomorphisms, is invariant under both kinds of arrows.
external_dependencies: IUTchII: Cor 4.5 (ii), (iii), Cor 4.6 (i), Cor 4.10 (i), Def 4.9, Remark 1.8.1
obligations: Identify the class of isomorphisms relative to which the bi-coric strip is 'invariant'.
Prove the stated strict containment of poly-isomorphism collections.
ambiguities: 'regarded up to a certain class of isomorphisms' (page 49 to 50) is not given an explicit description in the statement.

IUT3.Thm1_5.iv.content: Bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells: the poly-isomorphisms of (iii) induce poly-isomorphisms of mono-analytic log-shells for arbitrary (n,m), (n',m'), compatible with Prop 1.2 (viii); natural poly-isomorphisms to the holomorphic log-shell I_{n,m 𝔉_△}.
explicit_hypotheses: inherits the hypotheses of IUT3.Thm1_5
IUT3.Thm1_5.iv.conclusion: Poly-isomorphisms of log-shell pairs I ⊆ log(−).
obligations: Formalize log-shells and the induced poly-isomorphisms.

IUT3.Thm1_5.v.content: Bi-coric mono-analytic global realified Frobenioids D^⊩(n,m D^⊢_△), with isomorphisms of collections of data compatible with R_{>0}-orbits of local isomorphisms.
explicit_hypotheses: inherits the hypotheses of IUT3.Thm1_5
IUT3.Thm1_5.v.conclusion: Isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioid data across the lattice.
obligations: Formalize global realified Frobenioids.

IUT3.Rem1_5_1.content: (i) Conjugate synchronization (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.5 (iii), 4.6 (iii)) is essential for the bi-coricity of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v): it is a descent mechanism from label-dependent data (labels t ∈ LabCusp^±(−), which depend on the arithmetic holomorphic structure and make sense only within a vertical line) to label-independent data, which allows horizontally coric objects; vertically coric objects require passing to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms. Bi-coricity of the O^{×μ} at v ∈ V^non is thus a consequence of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization. (ii) A naive replacement: for a topological group G (e.g. G_v, v ∈ V^non), instead of a diagonal embedding G ↪ G × ... × G use its (G × ... × G)-conjugacy class. For two factors, identifying the diagonal with its conjugates forces identifications (g, g) ~ (g, hgh^{-1}) = (g, [h, g]·g), which is incompatible with using distinct copies of G to carry distinct Galois-theoretic Kummer classes (distinct theta values); this incompatibility is a consequence of the highly nonabelian nature of G. (iii) Combinatorially, conjugate synchronization resembles the label synchronization of IUTchI, Remark 4.9.2; both are combinatorial representations of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Theorem 1.5
for (ii): a topological group G, for instance G_v with v ∈ V^non; for simplicity two copies of G
IUT3.Rem1_5_1.conclusion: (i) The bi-coricity of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v) may be thought of as a consequence of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization. (ii) Replacing conjugate synchronization by working with the conjugacy class of the diagonal forces identifications (g, g) ~ (g, [h, g]·g), incompatible with distinct Kummer classes at distinct components; this naive approach is inadequate. (iii) Conjugate and label synchronization are both combinatorial representations of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line.
obligations: The identity (g, hgh^{-1}) = (g, [h, g]·g) holds with the convention [h, g] = hgh^{-1}g^{-1}; this is elementary group theory.
Make precise the claimed incompatibility in (ii): for nonabelian G, the conjugacy class of the diagonal is not the diagonal, so distinct elements (1 and [h, g]) at distinct components get identified.
ambiguities: Page 52: the commutator convention is not stated; the displayed equality forces [h, g] = hgh^{-1}g^{-1}.

IUT3.Rem1_5_2.content: (i) Unlike the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry on labeled copies of G_v (v ∈ V^non), no analogous conjugate synchronization exists for the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F̄ (IUTchII, Remark 4.7.2); the closest analogue is the action of the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F_mod ⊆ F_sol ⊆ F̄ and on the pseudo-monoid of ∞κ-coric rational functions. A consequence is that the reconstruction of the ring structure on labeled copies of F_sol subject to the F*_l-symmetry fails to be compatible with the localization operations of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (IUTchI, Remark 5.1.5); this is one essential reason bi-coricity analogous to Theorem 1.5 (iii) cannot be established for F^×_sol. The bi-coric mono-analytic global realified Frobenioids of Theorem 1.5 (v), i.e. the notion of log-volume, are a closest possible approximation to a bi-coric F^×_sol, which does not exist; alternatively, the bi-coric O^{×μ}'s, in the form of the bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells of Theorem 1.5 (iv), serve in §3 as 'multiradial containers' for labeled copies of F_mod via the localization functors (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (iii), 4.8 (iii)), transporting F^×_mod up to certain indeterminacies between distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures. (ii) Kummer theory is crucial for constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links); the incompatibility of solvable reconstructions of the ring structure with localization reflects the dismantling of the global prime-tree structure and the requirement of Kummer-compatible conjugate synchronization relative to the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. (iii) Although labeled copies of F^×_mod have no natural bi-coric structure, the global Frobenioids attached to them contain genuine conventional arithmetic line bundles (unlike the realified Frobenioids of Theorem 1.5 (v)); using the ring structure of F_mod one can push them forward to arithmetic vector bundles over Z and form tensor products, which is used in §3 and in IUTchIV.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^non for the local Galois groups G_v
the subfields F_mod ⊆ F_sol ⊆ F̄ and the F*_l-symmetry of IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (ii), 4.8 (ii)
IUT3.Rem1_5_2.conclusion: There is no conjugate synchronization for the F*_l-symmetry on labeled copies of F̄, and no bi-coric F^×_sol; log-volumes (Theorem 1.5 (v)) and the bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells (Theorem 1.5 (iv)) used as multiradial containers are the substitutes; the global Frobenioids attached to copies of F^×_mod contain genuine arithmetic line bundles, which can be pushed forward to arithmetic vector bundles over Z and tensored.
obligations: The nonexistence claims ('it is not possible to establish', page 52; 'fails to be compatible', page 53) are cited from IUTchII, Remark 4.7.2 and IUTchI, Remark 5.1.5; they need precise statements before they can be checked.
Pushforward of arithmetic line bundles over F_mod to arithmetic vector bundles over Z and their tensor products (page 54) are standard Arakelov constructions.
ambiguities: 'Closest possible approximation' (page 53) has no formal meaning.

IUT3.Rem1_5_3.content: (i) In [QuCnf], holomorphic structures on Riemann surfaces are represented by squares or rectangles and quasiconformal Teichmüller deformations by parallelograms (affine linear deformations dilating one real dimension by a factor in R_{>0}). Conjugate synchronization, a rigidity representing the arithmetic holomorphic structure of a vertical line, may be thought of as a nonarchimedean arithmetic analogue of this: the right angles of squares synchronize the metrics of the two real dimensions (Fig. 1.4). (ii) The naive approach of Remark 1.5.1 (ii) (identifying the conjugates of the diagonal embedding) corresponds to treating a holomorphic structure as an equivalence class modulo Teichmüller deformations, which avoids rigidifying the relation between the two metrics but makes any theory of deformations of a holomorphic structure unfeasible. (iii) The analogy applies also to κ-sol-conjugate synchronization (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (ii), 4.8 (ii)) between labeled non-realified and realified global Frobenioids via the F*_l-symmetry, especially for realified ones, which carry a natural R_{>0}-action: the synchronization of global realified Frobenioids by the F*_l-symmetry may be related, via the isomorphisms of Frobenioids of IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (iii), 4.8 (iii), to the global realified Frobenioid portion of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii)); the synchronization of non-realified global Frobenioids is a further rigidification, used in §3.
IUT3.Rem1_5_3.conclusion: An analogy, not a mathematical assertion: conjugate synchronization is to the arithmetic holomorphic structure what right angles of squares and rectangles are to a complex holomorphic structure; the naive alternative of Remark 1.5.1 (ii) corresponds to holomorphic structures modulo Teichmüller deformation; the F*_l-synchronization of realified global Frobenioids relates to the global realified Frobenioid portion of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link, and that of non-realified ones is a further rigidification.
definitions_required: conjugate synchronization; κ-sol-conjugate synchronization (IUTchII, Corollaries 4.7 (ii), 4.8 (ii); IUTchI, Remark 5.1.5)
external_dependencies: QuCnf: theory of holomorphic structures via squares and rectangles
obligations: None formal: the remark is an analogy. The sentence that the F*_l-synchronization 'may be related' to the global realified Frobenioid portion of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (page 55) would need a precise statement before it could be checked.
ambiguities: Fig. 1.4 (page 55) displays labeled copies of G_v indexed by −l*, ..., l* and an R_{>0}-action on a diagram of arrows; it is an illustration and carries no statement beyond the text.

IUT3.Rem1_5_4.content: (i) A main theme (IUTchII, Remark 3.8.3 (iii)) is an explicit description of one arithmetic holomorphic structure (a vertical line of the log-theta-lattice) from the point of view of a distinct one, related to it only via a mono-analytic core such as the bi-coric structures of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v). The objects of interest are Frobenius-like (main example: the Gaussian monoids of IUTchII, §3, §4), needed for constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links). The description splits into (a) passing from Frobenius-like to étale-like structures via Kummer isomorphisms and (b) transporting étale-like structures between arithmetic holomorphic structures by multiradiality; the indeterminacies ('departures from rigidity') arising in (a) are called Kummer-detachment indeterminacies, those in (b) étale-transport indeterminacies. (ii) Étale-transport indeterminacies typically arise from anabelian or group-theoretic algorithms; a fundamental example is given by automorphisms of the local absolute Galois groups G_v, v ∈ V^non, not of scheme-theoretic origin (Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv); AbsTopIII, §I3). (iii) Examples of Kummer-detachment indeterminacies: the non-commutative Frobenius-picture diagrams of Propositions 1.2 (x), 1.3 (iv) (which path to take from a '•' to the coric '◦'), whose upper semi-commutativity for the coric holomorphic log-shells (Remark 1.2.2 (iii)) is an upper estimate of this indeterminacy; and the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of Remark 1.4.2 (cf. the Kummer isomorphisms of the final display of Theorem 1.5 (iii)).
explicit_hypotheses: the log-theta-lattice of Definition 1.4 and the bi-coric structures of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), (v)
IUT3.Rem1_5_4.conclusion: Terminology: indeterminacies arising when Frobenius-like objects are passed to étale-like ones via Kummer isomorphisms are 'Kummer-detachment indeterminacies'; those arising when étale-like objects are transported by multiradiality are 'étale-transport indeterminacies'. Examples: automorphisms of G_v (v ∈ V^non) not of scheme-theoretic origin are étale-transport indeterminacies; the non-commutativity of the Frobenius-picture diagrams of Propositions 1.2 (x), 1.3 (iv), estimated from above by upper semi-commutativity of the coric log-shells, and the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of Remark 1.4.2 are Kummer-detachment indeterminacies.
obligations: Give a precise definition of each indeterminacy class as a set of maps or a group action, so that the classification of the examples in (ii) and (iii) becomes checkable.
ambiguities: A terminological remark: the two classes of indeterminacy are named by the step in which they arise, with no formal definition; 'typically amount to' (page 56) does not delimit étale-transport indeterminacies.

IUT3.Prop2_1.content: Vertical coricity and Kummer theory of theta monoids. For a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} and a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice: (i) vertically coric theta monoids Ψ_env(†D_>)_v, ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)_v and the global realified Frobenioid D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>), constructed algorithmically from the D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, with compatible isomorphisms induced by the vertical arrows; (ii) Frobenius-like theta monoids and C^⊩_env(†HT^Θ) with functorial Kummer isomorphisms to the data of (i), yielding isomorphisms †F^⊢_env ≅ F^⊢_env(†D_>) and †F^⊩_env ≅ F^⊩_env(†D_>); (iii) at v ∈ V^bad the Kummer isomorphisms come from Kummer classes of mono-theta environments, and the composite of the exterior cyclotome map with the projection to (Ψ_{†F^Θ_v})^{×μ} is zero; (iv) at v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non and (v) at v ∈ V^arc the unit portions come from labeled versions of IUTchII, Propositions 4.2, 4.4; (vi) natural isomorphisms with the constant monoids, compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms of (ii) and of Theorem 1.5 (iii). Proof: 'follow immediately from the definitions and the references quoted' (page 61).
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1
†HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater relative to the given initial Θ-data (IUTchI, Definition 6.13 (i))
{n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters indexed by pairs of integers, thought of as arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 1.4)
Aut_{F^⊩}(−) denotes the group of automorphisms of the F^⊩-prime-strip in parentheses
IUT3.Prop2_1.conclusion: Parts (i) to (vi); see the part records.
obligations: See part records. The proof (page 61) consists of the references quoted in the statement.

IUT3.Prop2_1.i.content: Vertically coric theta monoids: functorial algorithms in the D- and D^⊢-prime-strips †D_>, †D^⊢_> associated to †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} construct V ∋ v ↦ Ψ_env(†D_>)_v and V ∋ v ↦ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)_v and a global realified Frobenioid D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>) with a bijection Prime(D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>)) ≅ V and local isomorphisms for each v ∈ V (IUTchII, Corollary 4.5 (v)); each isomorphism of the full poly-isomorphism induced (Theorem 1.5 (i)) by a vertical arrow of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice induces a compatible collection of isomorphisms Ψ_env(n,mD_>) ≅ Ψ_env(n,m+1D_>), ∞Ψ_env(n,mD_>) ≅ ∞Ψ_env(n,m+1D_>), D^⊩_env(n,mD^⊢_>) ≅ D^⊩_env(n,m+1D^⊢_>).
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Prop2_1
the notation of IUTchII, Corollary 4.5 (iv), (v), and the assignment '0, ≻ ↦ >' of IUTchI, Proposition 6.7
IUT3.Prop2_1.i.conclusion: Functorial algorithms in †D_>, †D^⊢_> construct the collections Ψ_env(†D_>)_v, ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)_v (v ∈ V) and the global realified Frobenioid D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>) with Prime(D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>)) ≅ V and local isomorphisms; each isomorphism of the full poly-isomorphism induced by a vertical arrow induces compatible isomorphisms between the corresponding data at (n, m) and (n, m+1), the final isomorphism of Frobenioids being compatible with the bijections involving Prime(−) and with the local isomorphisms for each v ∈ V.
obligations: Formalize the algorithms of IUTchII, Corollary 4.5 (v) and prove functoriality, from which vertical coricity follows by Theorem 1.5 (i).

IUT3.Prop2_1.ii.content: Kummer isomorphisms: functorial algorithms in †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} construct V ∋ v ↦ Ψ_{F_env}(†HT^Θ)_v, ∞Ψ_{F_env}(†HT^Θ)_v and a global realified Frobenioid C^⊩_env(†HT^Θ) with Prime(C^⊩_env(†HT^Θ)) ≅ V and local isomorphisms (IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (v)), and Kummer isomorphisms Ψ_{F_env}(†HT^Θ) ≅ Ψ_env(†D_>), ∞Ψ_{F_env}(†HT^Θ) ≅ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>), C^⊩_env(†HT^Θ) ≅ D^⊩_env(†D^⊢_>), the last compatible with the bijections involving Prime(−) and the local isomorphisms. Each such isomorphism on cohomology is induced by the isomorphism on exterior cyclotomes Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})) ≅ Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†F_v)). The composite Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})) ⊗ Q/Z → (Ψ_{†F^Θ_v})^{×μ}, obtained from this isomorphism tensored with Q/Z, the natural inclusion Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†F_v)) ⊗ Q/Z ↪ (Ψ_{†F^Θ_v})^× and the natural projection (Ψ_{†F^Θ_v})^× ↠ (Ψ_{†F^Θ_v})^{×μ}, is the zero map.
