IUT3.Rem2_1_1.content: Summary of the main properties of mono-theta environments established in [EtTh] and their roles: (a) cyclotomic rigidity, (b) discrete rigidity, (c) constant multiple rigidity, (d) isomorphism class compatibility, (e) Frobenioid structure compatibility. (d) refers to compatibility with the convention that objects of the tempered Frobenioids (and base categories) are known only up to isomorphism; the compatibility with the topology of the tempered fundamental group mentioned in the Introduction of [EtTh] is a consequence of (d). (i) (e): the Frobenius-like monoidal portion with its Galois action is used in constructions not bound to conventional scheme theory (log-, Θ-, Θ^{×μ}-, Θ^{×μ}_gau-links) and related to étale-like structures by Kummer theory. (ii) (d): each object of a Kummer tower corresponds to a single field, whose ring structure is needed for the log-link (vertical coricity, Proposition 2.1 (i)); the N-th power morphisms of a Kummer tower are 'algebraic', so fundamental groups on either side are related up to inner automorphisms; the objects of these towers arise from nontrivial line bundles on tempered coverings of a Tate curve, so extracting N-th roots yields mutually non-isomorphic objects, related algorithmically only via indeterminate isomorphisms. (iii) (c): used for the canonical splittings of theta monoids via restriction to the zero section. (iv) (a): a consequence of the nondegeneracy of the commutator [−, −] of the theta groups ('the degree of the commutator is precisely 2'); concretely a specific isomorphism between interior and exterior cyclotomes, a rigidification of a 'projective line of cyclotomes', nonlinear in nature: composing it with an N-th power morphism sacrifices (c); its multiradiality (IUTchII, Corollary 1.10), in contrast with MLF-Galois pair cyclotomic rigidity, is central in §2. (v) (b): a consequence of 'the degree of the commutator is ≤ 2' (EtTh, Proposition 2.14 (ii), (iii)); it allows restriction to Z-multiples and powers rather than Ẑ-multiples and powers of divisors, line bundles and rational functions (such as the q-parameter) on tempered coverings of a Tate curve. The author's answer to whether a theory of Ẑ-divisors, line bundles and rational functions parallel to perfections and realifications of Frobenioids exists is 'no': Ẑ has no notion of positivity (−1 ∈ Ẑ is a limit of positive integers), so such a theory would confuse effective and negative divisors, i.e. work birationally, sacrificing the isomorphisms between line bundles needed for the Frobenioid-theoretic mono-theta environment.
explicit_hypotheses: mono-theta environments arising from tempered Frobenioids at bad primes, as in Proposition 2.1 (iii) and [EtTh]
IUT3.Rem2_1_1.conclusion: Expository: the roles of properties (a) to (e) of mono-theta environments in the theory; in particular cyclotomic rigidity is multiradial (IUTchII, Corollary 1.10) and nonlinear, discrete rigidity restricts to Z-multiples, and in the author's view no theory of Ẑ-divisors parallel to realifications is available because Ẑ has no positivity.
external_dependencies: EtTh: Introduction; Corollary 5.12; Remarks 5.12.1, 5.12.2, 5.12.3, 5.12.5; Proposition 1.1; Lemma 5.9; Proposition 2.12; Proposition 2.14 (ii), (iii); Remarks 2.19.2, 2.19.4
FrdI: perfections and realifications of Frobenioids
obligations: The rigidity properties (a) to (e) are results of [EtTh]; none is proved here.
The elementary fact that −1 ∈ Ẑ is a limit of positive integers (page 63) holds: −1 = lim (n! − 1) in Ẑ.
ambiguities: Page 63: the negative answer to the question on Ẑ-divisors is stated as 'as far as the author can see at the time of writing'; it is an opinion, not a theorem.
'The degree of the commutator is precisely 2' and 'is ≤ 2' (pages 62 to 63) are informal; their precise content is in [EtTh], Proposition 2.14.

IUT3.Rem2_1_2.content: (i) The global bookkeeping operations on labels of evaluation points in the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, together with the profinite nature of the global étale fundamental groups, force the use of the 'complements on tempered coverings' of IUTchI, §2 at v ∈ V^bad, so as to restrict to discrete Z-conjugates rather than profinite Ẑ-conjugates of the theta functions; this is called 'evaluation discrete rigidity'. (ii) In the situation of IUTchII, Proposition 2.1, fix v ∈ V^bad, Π := Π_v, Π̂ its profinite completion, with natural surjections Π ↠ l·Z ⊆ Z and Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ ⊆ Ẑ, and Π† := Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z ⊆ Π̂. Evaluation discrete rigidity concerns whether the coordinates of the evaluation points lie in Z or in Ẑ. The partially tempered group Π† cannot replace Π: there is an '[easily verified]' natural isomorphism N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z, so Π† fails various absolute anabelian properties of Π (SemiAnbd, Theorems 6.6, 6.8) and its profinite conjugacy indeterminacies give Ẑ-translation indeterminacies of the coordinates of evaluation points, which for Π are avoided by the complements on tempered coverings, a consequence of the highly anabelian nature of Π.
explicit_hypotheses: for (ii): the situation of IUTchII, Proposition 2.1; v ∈ V^bad; Π := Π_v the tempered fundamental group, Π̂ its profinite completion
the natural surjections Π ↠ l·Z (⊆ Z), Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ (⊆ Ẑ), and Π† := Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z ⊆ Π̂
IUT3.Rem2_1_2.conclusion: (i) The complements on tempered coverings (IUTchI, §2) provide an 'evaluation discrete rigidity'. (ii) N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z naturally; consequently Π† lacks absolute anabelian properties of Π and its profinite conjugacy indeterminacies act by Ẑ-translations on the coordinates of evaluation points, so Π† cannot replace the full tempered fundamental group Π.

external_dependencies: EtTh: absolute anabelian properties used in its theory
obligations: Prove the natural isomorphism N_Π̂(Π†)/Π† ≅ Ẑ/Z (page 64: '[easily verified]'; no argument is given).
Make precise which absolute anabelian properties Π† fails, with reference to SemiAnbd, Theorems 6.6, 6.8.
ambiguities: Page 64: Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ is written with the target underlined as a subgroup of Ẑ; the fiber product Π̂ ×_Ẑ Z is taken over the composite Π̂ ↠ l·Ẑ ⊆ Ẑ and the inclusion Z ⊆ Ẑ, which is the natural reading.

IUT3.Thm2_2.ii.content: Kummer aspects of multiradiality at bad primes. For v ∈ V^bad let ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v ⊆ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)_v and ∞Ψ^⊥_{F_env}(†HT^Θ)_v ⊆ ∞Ψ_{F_env}(†HT^Θ)_v be the submonoids corresponding to the splittings (IUTchII, Corollaries 3.5 (iii), 3.6 (iii)), generated by ∞θ^ι_env(M^Θ_*) and the torsion subgroups. There is a commutative diagram with rows ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v ⊇ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^μ_v ⊆ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^×_v ↠ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^{×μ}_v ≅ Ψ^ss_cns(†D^⊢_△)^{×μ}_v and the analogous Frobenius-like row ending in Ψ^ss_cns(†F^⊢_△)^{×μ}_v; the first four vertical arrows are induced by the inverse of the second Kummer isomorphism of Proposition 2.1 (ii), the last vertical arrow is the inverse of the Kummer poly-isomorphism of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (ii), the final upper horizontal arrow is the poly-isomorphism obtained by composing the inverse of the natural isomorphism of Proposition 2.1 (vi) with the poly-automorphism of Ψ^ss_cns(†D^⊢_△)^{×μ}_v induced by the full poly-automorphism of †D^⊢_△, and the final lower horizontal arrow is determined by commutativity of the final square. The diagram is compatible with the group actions relative to Π_X(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})) ↠ G_v(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})) and the full poly-automorphism of G_v(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})). Each composite ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^μ_v → Ψ^ss_cns(†F^⊢_△)^{×μ}_v is the zero map. Hence the identity automorphism on (a_v) ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v ⊇ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^μ_v, (b_v) Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})) ⊗ Q/Z relative to the natural isomorphism to ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^μ_v (IUTchII, Remark 1.5.2), (c_v) the projective system of mono-theta environments M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v}), (d_v) the splittings ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v ↠ ∞Ψ_env(†D_>)^μ_v by restriction to zero-labeled evaluation points, is compatible, relative to the natural morphisms of the diagram, with the collection of automorphisms of Ψ^ss_cns(†F^⊢_△)^{×μ}_v induced by arbitrary automorphisms in Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(†F^{⊢×μ}_△).

IUT3.Rem2_2_1.content: Conceptual reading of Theorem 2.2 (ii). (i) Write Π_v := Π_X(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), G_v := G_v(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), Π_μ := Π_μ(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), (l·Δ_Θ) := (l·Δ_Θ)(M^Θ_*(†D_{>,v})), an object constructed from Π_v (IUTchII, Proposition 1.4). The projective system of mono-theta environments is an 'amalgamation of Π_v and Π_μ' allowing reconstruction of the mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l·Δ_Θ) ≅ Π_μ itself (IUTchII, Proposition 1.5 (iii)), not just its Ẑ^×-orbit. (ii) The Kummer classes in ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v of the étale theta functions are, for suitable characteristic open H ⊆ Π_v, twisted homomorphisms H → Π_μ restricting on (l·Δ_Θ) to the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism. The essential content of Theorem 2.2 (ii): since the Kummer-theoretic link between étale-like and Frobenius-like data at v ∈ V^bad is made via mono-theta environments, which do not involve the monoids (−)^{×μ}, the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (not just its Ẑ^×-orbit) is immune to the automorphisms of the (−)^{×μ} arising from isomorphisms of coric data; this is a decoupling of geometric (Δ_v ⊆ Π_v) and base-field-theoretic (Π_v ↠ G_v) data, a splitting into purely radial (Π_μ) and purely coric ((−)^{×μ}) components. (iii) This contrasts with the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies of cyclotomic rigidity from MLF-Galois pairs, whose input data is O^▷: in the diagram O^μ ⊆ O^× ⊆ O^▷ ⊆ O^gp ⊆ O^{gp^} with O^× ↠ O^{×μ}, a Ẑ^×-indeterminacy on O^{×μ} lifts naturally only to Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on O^×, O^{gp^} (Fig. 2.1), so only the Ẑ^×-orbit of the MLF-Galois-pair cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism is recovered; mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity is insulated (Fig. 2.2: identity action on Π_μ ≅ O^μ, Ẑ^× on O^{×μ}). (iv) Mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity insulates the étale theta function from the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies acting on the coric log-shells; the techniques do not apply immediately to Gaussian monoids, whose multiradiality (§3) requires log-shells but depends essentially on that of theta monoids. Treating theta values q^{j^2}_v merely as elements of the base field, without the étale theta function, leaves only MLF-Galois pairs to rigidify cyclotomes, giving Ẑ^×-indeterminacies, i.e. confusion between q^{j^2}_v and their Ẑ^×-powers.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Theorem 2.2 (ii), v ∈ V^bad
for (iii): the notation O^μ, O^×, O^▷, O^gp, O^{gp^}, O^{×μ} for the monoids of Theorem 2.2, as in IUTchII, Example 1.8 (ii), (iii), (iv), (vii)
IUT3.Rem2_2_1.conclusion: Interpretation: the mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (l·Δ_Θ) ≅ Π_μ is reconstructed exactly and is immune to the automorphisms of the coric monoids (−)^{×μ}, whereas MLF-Galois-pair cyclotomic rigidity is recovered only up to its Ẑ^×-orbit because Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on O^{×μ} lift only to Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on O^×; this insulation of the étale theta function is what the multiradiality of Gaussian monoids in §3 depends on.
obligations: State 'immune to automorphisms of (−)^{×μ}' as: the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism is fixed by every automorphism of the data that acts trivially on Π_v and arbitrarily (through Ẑ^×) on O^{×μ}; prove it from IUTchII, Proposition 1.5 (iii).

State and prove that a Ẑ^×-action on O^{×μ} lifts naturally only to Ẑ^×-actions on O^×, O^{gp^} (page 68), so that MLF-Galois-pair cyclotomic rigidity is determined only up to Ẑ^× (IUTchII, Corollary 1.11).
ambiguities: Page 68: 'lifted naturally' is not defined; the claim that one 'can only recover the Ẑ^×-orbit' is a statement about what a natural construction can achieve, with no formal formulation given.

IUT3.Rem2_2_2.content: (i) Naive question: can the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link q ↦ q^{(1^2, ..., (l*)^2)} (IUTchII, Remark 4.11.1) be replaced by q ↦ q^λ for an arbitrary positive integer λ? The answer given is 'no': such a correspondence lacks the multiradiality machinery of the étale theta function (mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity, splittings by zero-labeled evaluation points), so there is no insulation of its Kummer classes from the Ẑ^×-indeterminacies on (−)^{×μ}, and no decoupling of the coric log-shells from its purely radial (value group) portion; realizing such a splitting by Galois evaluation with λ = j^2 raises symmetry issues between the zero-labeled evaluation point and the one for λ, which the theory resolves via the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, and leads to conditions on the collection of evaluation points (IUTchII, Remark 2.6.3); 'it is difficult to see' how to build the theory with evaluation points other than those of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link. (ii) The multiradial formulations of Gaussian monoids in §3 are subject to indeterminacies sufficiently mild for the volume computations of IUTchIV but substantially more severe than those for theta monoids in §2, which essentially consist of multiplication by roots of unity (IUTchII, Proposition 3.1 (i)), are essentially negligible and come from the Kummer theory of mono-theta environments; this exactness would be lost with correspondences q ↦ q^λ. (iii) The Kummer-compatibility of the multiradial splitting via Galois evaluation relates the Kummer theory of theta monoids in the domain of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link to the ×μ-Kummer structures in its horizontally coric portion (Fig. 2.3): restricted to ∞θ, the Ism-orbit of arrows from O^× to O^{×μ} becomes a single arrow because ∞θ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ}; the multiradial structure on the theta monoid O^×·∞θ given by the splittings into coric and radial components is compatible with the Kummer theories of O^× and of the coric O^{×μ}. For a naive correspondence q ↦ q^λ the analogous arrows map q^λ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ} and are incompatible with passage to Kummer classes, since the Kummer class of q^λ in a cohomology group of Π/Δ is by no means mapped, via the poly-isomorphism Π/Δ ≅ G, to the trivial element of the corresponding cohomology group of G.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Theorem 2.2 and of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (IUTchII, Remark 4.11.1)
for (i): λ an arbitrary positive integer
IUT3.Rem2_2_2.conclusion: A naive correspondence q ↦ q^λ cannot replace the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link: it lacks mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity and zero-labeled splittings, its indeterminacies would not be essentially negligible, and its analogue of Fig. 2.3 (q^λ ↦ 1 ∈ O^{×μ}) is incompatible with passage to Kummer classes because the Kummer class of q^λ is not mapped to the trivial class of G.
external_dependencies: EtTh: theory of the étale theta function
obligations: Prove the final claim of (iii) (page 72): the Kummer class of q^λ (λ a positive integer) in the relevant cohomology group of Π/Δ is not mapped to the trivial element under Π/Δ ≅ G; this is asserted ('by no means') without computation.
The negative answer in (i) is supported only by 'it is difficult to see how' (page 70); it is not a theorem and cannot be formalized as stated.
ambiguities: Page 70: 'one of the j^2 [where j is a positive integer]' for λ; the range of j is not restated (in the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link j runs over 1, ..., l*).
Fig. 2.3 (page 71) uses Π, Δ, G, O^×, O^{×μ}, ∞θ without subscripts; the text identifies them with the objects at v ∈ V^bad of Theorem 2.2 (ii).

IUT3.Cor2_3.content: Étale-picture of multiradial theta monoids. In the notation of Theorem 2.2, for distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters n,mHT arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice, with associated D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters n,mHT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF}, a radial environment (IUTchII, Example 1.7 (ii)) is defined. Radial data †R = (†HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF}, F^⊩_env(†D_>), †R^bad, F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△), F^{⊢×μ}_env(†D_>) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△)) consist of (a_R) a D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater, (b_R) the F^⊩-prime-strip of Proposition 2.1 (ii), (c_R) the data (a_v) to (d_v) of Theorem 2.2 (ii) for v ∈ V^bad, denoted †R^bad, (d_R) the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (e_R) the full poly-isomorphism F^{⊢×μ}_env(†D_>) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△). Morphisms †R → ‡R consist of (a_Mor) an isomorphism of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, (b_Mor), (c_Mor) the isomorphisms it induces on F^⊩_env and on R^bad, (d_Mor) an isomorphism F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(‡D^⊢_△); (e_Mor) observes that (b_Mor), (d_Mor) are necessarily compatible with the poly-isomorphisms (e_R). Coric data †C = (†D^⊢, F^{⊢×μ}(†D^⊢)) with morphisms given by (a_MorC) an isomorphism †D^⊢ ≅ ‡D^⊢ and (b_MorC) an isomorphism F^{⊢×μ}(†D^⊢) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}(‡D^⊢) inducing it. The radial algorithm is †R ↦ †C = (†D^⊢_△, F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△)), on morphisms determined by (d_Mor). Conclusions (i) to (iv); proof: 'follow immediately from the definitions and the references quoted' (page 75).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Theorem 2.2 (initial Θ-data; Aut_{F^□}(−))
{n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data, thought of as arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 1.4)
n,mHT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater associated to n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}
the radial data, coric data, their morphisms and the radial algorithm as defined on pages 72 to 74
IUT3.Cor2_3.conclusion: Parts (i) to (iv); see the part records.
external_dependencies: IUTchII: Example 1.7 (ii); Corollary 4.5 (ii); Definition 4.9 (vi), (vii); Corollary 4.11 (ii); Remarks 4.1.1 (iii), 4.3.1
obligations: See part records. The proof (page 75) consists of the references quoted in the statement.
ambiguities: Page 73, (e_Mor): 'we observe that ... are necessarily compatible' is part of the definition of morphisms, not a separate condition; it holds because (e_R) is a full poly-isomorphism (all isomorphisms).

IUT3.Cor2_3.i.content: The functor associated to the radial algorithm †R ↦ †C is full and essentially surjective; in particular the radial environment is multiradial.
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses and definitions of IUT3.Cor2_3
IUT3.Cor2_3.i.conclusion: The radial algorithm functor from radial data to coric data is full and essentially surjective; hence the radial environment is multiradial (in the sense of IUTchII, Example 1.7 (ii)).
obligations: Prove fullness: every isomorphism of coric data F^{⊢×μ}_△(†D^⊢_△) ≅ F^{⊢×μ}_△(‡D^⊢_△) lifts to a morphism of radial data; by the definition of morphisms, (d_Mor) is an arbitrary isomorphism independent of (a_Mor), so fullness reduces to the existence of some isomorphism (a_Mor) of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters and to compatibility of the induced (c_Mor) with an arbitrary (d_Mor), which is the content of Theorem 2.2 (ii).
Prove essential surjectivity: every coric datum arises from some radial datum.
ambiguities: No argument specific to (i) is given; the proof on page 75 refers to the definitions and quoted references.

IUT3.Cor2_3.ii.content: Each n,mHT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} defines radial data n,mR; the poly-isomorphisms induced by vertical arrows (Theorem 1.5 (i)) induce poly-isomorphisms ... ≅ n,mR ≅ n,m+1R ≅ ...; n,◦R denotes the radial data obtained by identifying the n,mR, m ∈ Z, via these, and n,◦C the associated coric data. The horizontal arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms ... ≅ n,mD^⊢_△ ≅ n+1,mD^⊢_△ ≅ ... (Theorem 1.5 (ii)); ◦,◦C denotes the coric data obtained by identifying the n,◦C, n ∈ Z. Applying the radial algorithm to each n,◦R gives an étale-picture of radial data (Fig. 2.4), which admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (labels n ∈ Z) and is compatible with the étale-picture of D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters of IUTchII, Corollary 4.11 (ii).
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses and definitions of IUT3.Cor2_3
n, m ∈ Z
IUT3.Cor2_3.ii.conclusion: The vertical arrows induce poly-isomorphisms of radial data n,mR ≅ n,m+1R and the horizontal arrows full poly-isomorphisms n,mD^⊢_△ ≅ n+1,mD^⊢_△; the resulting étale-picture of radial data (Fig. 2.4), with core F^{⊢×μ}_△(◦,◦D^⊢_△) and spokes F^⊩_env(n,◦D_>) + n,◦R^bad + ..., admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes and is compatible with the étale-picture of IUTchII, Corollary 4.11 (ii).
obligations: Prove that the permutation symmetries of the spokes exist, using the fullness of (i) to lift arbitrary permutations of the labels n to compatible isomorphisms of radial data over the identity of the core.
ambiguities: Page 74: n,mR is defined 'in an evident way' from n,mHT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF}; the construction is not spelled out.
Page 74: 'compatible, in the evident sense' with IUTchII, Corollary 4.11 (ii) is not made precise.

IUT3.Cor2_3.iii.content: The poly-isomorphisms of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips of or induced by (e_R), (b_Mor), (d_Mor) (and (e_Mor)) are compatible, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 (ii) (and (vi)) and Theorem 1.5 (iii), with the poly-isomorphisms of Theorem 1.5 (ii) arising from the horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice.
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses and definitions of IUT3.Cor2_3
IUT3.Cor2_3.iii.conclusion: The (poly-)isomorphisms of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips of or induced by (e_R), (b_Mor), (d_Mor) are compatible, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 (ii), (vi) and Theorem 1.5 (iii), with the horizontal-arrow poly-isomorphisms of Theorem 1.5 (ii).
obligations: State the compatibility as commutativity of the relevant squares and prove it from Proposition 2.1 (ii), (vi) and Theorem 1.5 (ii), (iii).

IUT3.Cor2_3.iv.content: The algorithmic construction of the isomorphisms F^⊩_env(†D_>) ≅ F^⊩_env(‡D_>), †R^bad ≅ ‡R^bad of (b_Mor), (c_Mor), and of the Kummer isomorphisms and poly-isomorphisms of projective systems of mono-theta environments of Proposition 2.1 (ii), (iii) (and (vi); the second display of Theorem 2.2 (ii)) and Theorem 1.5 (iii), (v), are compatible with the horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice (e.g. the full poly-isomorphisms of Theorem 1.5 (ii)): these constructions are stabilized, equivariant and functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of the domain and codomain of these horizontal arrows.
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses and definitions of IUT3.Cor2_3
IUT3.Cor2_3.iv.conclusion: The algorithmic constructions of (b_Mor), (c_Mor) and of the Kummer isomorphisms and mono-theta poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 (ii), (iii) and Theorem 1.5 (iii), (v) are stabilized, equivariant and functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of the domain and codomain of the horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice (cf. the final portions of Theorems 1.5 (v), 2.2 (ii)).
obligations: Formalize 'stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms' and prove it from Theorem 2.2 (ii) (the vanishing of the composites to (−)^{×μ}) and Theorem 1.5 (v).
ambiguities: Page 75: the three adjectives 'stabilized/equivariant/functorial' are given together, without saying which applies to which construction.

IUT3.Rem2_3_1.content: (i) The étale-picture of Fig. 2.4 recalls the analogy (IUTchII, 1.12.5 (i), (ii)) between étale-pictures and the polar coordinate representation of the classical Gaussian integral. (ii) The étale-picture of Corollary 2.3 (ii) may be thought of as a canonical splitting of the portion of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice involving theta monoids. (iii) The multiradiality of Corollary 2.3 (iv) at v ∈ V^bad corresponds essentially to that of IUTchII, Corollary 1.12 (iii) and Proposition 3.4 (i).
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Corollary 2.3
IUT3.Rem2_3_1.conclusion: Interpretation: the étale-picture of Corollary 2.3 is analogous to polar coordinates for the Gaussian integral and is a canonical splitting of the theta-monoid portion of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice; the multiradiality of Corollary 2.3 (iv) at v ∈ V^bad is essentially that of IUTchII, Corollary 1.12 (iii) and Proposition 3.4 (i).
obligations: None formal: the remark is interpretive.
ambiguities: Page 75: the reference '[IUTchII], 1.12.5, (i), (ii)' does not say whether it is a remark; it is presumably Remark 1.12.5.

IUT3.Rem2_3_2.content: A result similar to Corollary 2.3 may be formulated for the multiradiality of the Kummer theory of ∞κ-coric structures (IUTchII, Corollary 4.8): the Kummer theory of the localization poly-morphisms {π^{κ-sol}_1(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ}}_j → †M_{∞κv_j} ⊆ †M_{∞κ×v_j}, v ∈ V (IUTchII, Corollary 4.8 (iii)), rests on the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms for ∞κ-coric structures (IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v); Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii)), which have insulation properties analogous to those of mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity (Remark 2.2.1). The reconstruction of ∞κ-coric structures from ∞κ×-structures via restriction of Kummer classes, ‡M_{∞κv_j} ⊆ ‡M_{∞κ×v_j} → ‡M^×_{∞κ×v_j} ≅ ‡M^×_{v_j}, is a decoupling into radial ({π^{κ-sol}_1(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ}}_j; †M_{∞κv_j}; ‡M_{∞κv_j}) and coric (the quotient of ‡M^×_{∞κ×v_j} ≅ ‡M^×_{v_j} by its torsion subgroup) components, analogous to Remark 2.2.2 (iii); the Galois evaluation giving the theta values q^{j^2}_v corresponds to the Galois evaluation construction of the monoids †M^⊛_mod by restricting Kummer classes of ∞κ-coric structures. The routine details of a formulation in the style of Corollary 2.3 are left to the reader.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUTchII, Corollary 4.8, and IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii)
IUT3.Rem2_3_2.conclusion: An analogue of Corollary 2.3 holds for the Kummer theory of ∞κ-coric structures, with radial/coric decoupling via restriction of Kummer classes (Galois evaluation) and insulation of the associated cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms; the formulation is left to the reader (page 76).
obligations: State the analogue of Corollary 2.3 for ∞κ-coric structures (radial data, coric data, radial algorithm) and prove it; page 76 leaves 'the routine details of giving a formulation in the style of Corollary 2.3 to the reader'.
ambiguities: The statement is asserted to exist but is not formulated (page 76), so its exact content is not determined by the text.

IUT3.Rem2_3_3.content: Comparison of multiradiality in the theta case (Remarks 2.2.1, 2.2.2, Corollary 2.3) and the number field case (Remark 2.3.2), summarized in Fig. 2.7 (page 84). (i) Similarity: both use the geometric dimension of the elliptic curve as a 'multiradial geometric container' for radial arithmetic data (theta values q^{j^2}_v, resp. copies of F_mod): theta functions on Tate curves [EtTh], resp. Belyi maps as Belyi cuspidalizations [AbsTopIII]; both pass to the data by Galois evaluation. (ii) Interpretation of the dismantling of the two combinatorial dimensions of a number field, by analogy with base change from R to C: multiradial containers as realizations of two-dimensional scheme-theoretic data (an elliptic curve over a number field) and the multiradial representations of Theorem 3.11 as realizations of 'suitable descent data'; compare parallel transport (IUTchII, Remark 1.7.1) and PD-envelopes (IUTchII, Remark 1.9.2 (iii)). (iii) Both Galois evaluations occur in the context of the log-link; difference: theta values depend on the labels j ∈ F*_l (which correspond to cuspidal inertia groups in Δ ⊆ Π), copies of F_mod do not. It is called a 'quite nontrivial fact' that Galois evaluation and Kummer theory in the theta case are compatible with both the labels and the arithmetic holomorphic structures. (iv) It is called a 'highly nontrivial fact' that the construction of the mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism admits F^{⋊±}_l-symmetries consistently with the label dependence of the theta values; from the naive Kummer approach of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), this would require a rational function invariant under the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetries with distinct valuations on an orbit, which is self-contradictory. (v) Replacing Π by a closed subgroup of infinite index (to kill Kummer classes of the obstruction to symmetry) has two deficiencies: absolute anabelian results of AbsTopIII, §1 may not generalize to such subgroups, and vanishing of Kummer classes on restriction need not be compatible with ring structures. (vi) Using distinct rational functions (a symmetric one for cyclotomic rigidity, a non-symmetric one for evaluation) conflicts with the identification of the cuspidal cyclotomes μ^*_et into μ^∀_et (AbsTopIII, Proposition 1.4 (ii)) and the tautological identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et needed for multiradial containers; the cyclotomic rigidity of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) identifies the μ^*_et with sub-cyclotomes of μ_Fr via multiplication by the orders of zeroes and poles, so under the identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et one must allow indeterminacy by the submonoid I^ord ⊆ ±N_{≥1} := N_{≥1} × {±1} generated by those orders, with images I^ord_{≥1} ⊆ N_{≥1}, I^ord_± ⊆ {±1}. Nontrivial I^ord is incompatible with constructions analogous to theta values ('it follows immediately' that independent indeterminacies at distinct v contradict the product formula). In the theta case I^ord = {1} because the order of zeroes and poles of the theta function at every cusp is 1 ([EtTh], Proposition 1.4 (i)), impossible for an algebraic rational function, whose orders sum to 0. In the number field case the I^ord_{≥1} part is avoided by Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}, which remains valid after the identification of μ_Fr with μ^∀_et, while the I^ord_± part, avoided in IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) by the non-κ-coricity of inverses of nonconstant κ-coric functions, is incompatible with that identification; hence the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms, and the copies of F^×_mod ∪ {0}, are subject to an indeterminacy {±1}, which causes no obstacle since F^×_mod is stabilized by {±1} (Remark 3.11.4); the copies of F^×_mod are constructed globally and compatibly with the F*_l-symmetry, without product formula compatibilities between distinct v. (vii) These are a multiple cusp version of the 'N-th power versus first power' and linearity issues (IUTchII, Remark 3.6.4 (iii)); mono-theta cyclotomic rigidity is compatible with the topology of the tempered fundamental group, whereas the algorithms of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v) depend on Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}, which is incompatible with the profinite topology (N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ). (viii) The same indeterminacy issues occur for the cyclotomic rigidity algorithms of IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (vi) for mixed-characteristic local fields, which yield the same isomorphism as AbsTopIII, Proposition 3.2 (iv) (IUTchII, Proposition 4.2 (i)) and are compatible with the profinite topology because they use uniformizers (one zero of order 1, no poles), reflecting the canonical valuation of an MLF; so theta functions, resp. one-dimensional function fields, are a 'qualitative geometric model' of MLFs, resp. number fields, at the level of valuations. (ix) Analogy with the upper half-plane: q = e^{2πiz} (eigenfunction for additive symmetries, theta case) is highly transcendental, w = (z − i)/(z + i) (multiplicative symmetries, number field case) is algebraic. (x) Fig. 2.7 summarizes the comparison.
explicit_hypotheses: the theta case of Remarks 2.2.1, 2.2.2 and Corollary 2.3 and the number field case of Remark 2.3.2

for (vi): rational functions on hyperbolic curves with cusps '*', the cuspidal cyclotomes μ^*_et, μ^∀_et, μ_Fr and the submonoid I^ord ⊆ ±N_{≥1} := N_{≥1} × {±1} generated by the orders of zeroes and poles
IUT3.Rem2_3_3.conclusion: Expository comparison (Fig. 2.7). Mathematical assertions made along the way: in the theta case the indeterminacy submonoid I^ord is {1}, because the theta function has order 1 at every cusp; for algebraic rational functions the orders sum to 0; Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}; N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ; nontrivial independent indeterminacies at distinct v ∈ V are incompatible with the product formula; in the number field case the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms and the copies of F^×_mod ∪ {0} are subject to a {±1}-indeterminacy, under which F^×_mod is stable.
definitions_required: μ^*_et, μ^∀_et, μ_Fr and I^ord (pages 79 to 81)
external_dependencies: EtTh: Proposition 1.4 (i) (order of zeroes and poles of the theta function at every cusp is 1)
obligations: Prove that independent indeterminacies by a nontrivial submonoid I^ord on the valuations at distinct v ∈ V are incompatible with the product formula (page 81: 'it follows immediately'; no argument is given).

Elementary facts used, all provable: Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1} (a positive rational that is a unit at every prime is 1); N_{≥1} is dense in Ẑ; the orders of zeroes and poles of a nonconstant rational function on a proper curve sum to 0 (degree of a principal divisor); w = (z − i)/(z + i) is a rational function of z.
The order 1 of the theta function at every cusp is cited from [EtTh], Proposition 1.4 (i).
The 'quite nontrivial' and 'highly nontrivial' facts of (iii), (iv) (pages 78) are cited from IUTchII, Corollary 3.6 and Remark 1.1.1 (v); they are not proved here.
ambiguities: Page 80: the indeterminacy is generated by the orders 'of the zeroes/poles of the rational function(s)'; whether poles contribute negative orders (hence the sign component ±1) or their absolute values is left implicit; the decomposition ±N_{≥1} = N_{≥1} × {±1} suggests signed orders.
Page 81: 'Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}' is written without saying in which ring the intersection is taken; the natural reading is inside the finite adeles (or Q ⊆ Q ⊗ Ẑ).
Pages 76 to 77 ((ii)) and 83 ((viii), (ix)) are analogies with no formal content.

IUT3.Rem2_3_4.content: The essential content of [EtTh] in light of Remark 2.3.3. (i) Non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters (log-links and Θ-links) are built from Frobenius-like structures; étale-like structures relate the two sides; Kummer theory relates the two kinds and must be multiradial, which is achieved by radial/coric decouplings via multiradial geometric containers followed by Galois evaluation, since direct use of theta values or number fields gives a Kummer theory without the desired multiradiality (Remarks 2.2.1, 2.3.2). (ii) The naive Kummer theory of algebraic rational functions (IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v); Definition 5.2 (vi)) is, at v ∈ V^bad, incompatible with the profinite topology (Remark 2.3.3 (vi), (vii), (viii); Figs. 2.5, 2.6), so one uses the Kummer theory of theta functions truncated modulo N; the naive version of that is incompatible with discrete rigidity (Remark 2.1.1 (v)), owing to the lack of 'shifting automorphisms' (EtTh, Proposition 2.14 (ii); Remark 2.14.3), and with the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry; one therefore uses the Kummer theory of the first Chern classes of the line bundles associated to theta functions. Summary: truncated Kummer theory of theta functions is compatible with profinite/tempered topologies; truncated Kummer theory of first Chern classes of line bundles is compatible with discrete rigidity and the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. (iii) This amounts to the partially truncated arithmetic fundamental group of the G_m-torsor of such a line bundle, i.e. the topological group portion of a mono- or bi-theta environment (EtTh, Definition 2.13 (ii) (a), (iii) (a)), which carries two distinguished classes of sections, theta sections and algebraic sections. With neither: indeterminacy by multiplication by constant units O^×, incompatible with constant multiple rigidity. With both (bi-theta environments): the lack of symmetries of the truncated theory, incompatible with discrete rigidity and the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry. With algebraic sections only: not enough data for the commutator property of EtTh, Proposition 2.12, incompatible with cyclotomic rigidity. With theta sections only (mono-theta environments): compatible with the tempered topology, the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry and all three rigidities. (iv) The approach of [EtTh] differs from the function-theoretic (explicit series, EtTh, Proposition 1.4) and representation-theoretic (irreducible representations of theta groups) approaches, which depend on ring structures and are ill-suited to theta functions in distinct ring/scheme theories related only via tempered Frobenioids (multiplicative monoids) and tempered fundamental groups (Galois actions).
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^bad for the local discussion of (ii), (iii)
line bundles associated to theta functions on tempered coverings of a Tate curve, as in [EtTh]
IUT3.Rem2_3_4.conclusion: Of the four options for the sections carried by the partially truncated arithmetic fundamental group of the G_m-torsor of the theta line bundle, only working with theta sections and not algebraic sections (mono-theta environments) is compatible with the tempered topology, the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry and all three rigidities (cyclotomic, discrete, constant multiple); the other three options each fail one of these.
obligations: Each of the four compatibility claims of (iii) rests on results of [EtTh] (Propositions 2.12, 2.14; Definition 2.13) that are cited, not proved here.
ambiguities: 'Fatal drawback' and 'incompatible' (pages 85 to 87) are not given formal meanings.

IUT3.Def2_4.content: (i) For an F^⊢-prime-strip ‡F^⊢ = {‡F^⊢_v}_{v∈V}: at w ∈ V^bad the splittings of the split Frobenioid ‡F^⊢_w determine submonoids O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^▷(−) and quotients O^⊥(−) ↠ O^▶(−) (quotient by the torsion subgroup) (IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (ii)); at w ∈ V^good the splitting determines a submonoid O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^▷(−) with trivial unit group (when w ∈ V^good ∩ V^non; IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (iv)), and O^▶(−) := O^⊥(−). ‡F^{⊢⊥} = {‡F^{⊢⊥}_v}_{v∈V} and ‡F^{⊢▶} = {‡F^{⊢▶}_v}_{v∈V} are obtained by replacing the split Frobenioid portion of each ‡F^⊢_v by the Frobenioids determined by O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^▷(−), resp. O^▶(−). (ii) An F^{⊢⊥}-prime-strip *F^{⊢⊥} = {*F^{⊢⊥}_v}_{v∈V}: (a) for v ∈ V^non, *F^{⊢⊥}_v is a Frobenioid isomorphic to ‡F^{⊢⊥}_v; (b) for v ∈ V^arc, it consists of a Frobenioid and an object of TM^⊢ (IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (ii)) such that *F^{⊢⊥}_v is isomorphic to ‡F^{⊢⊥}_v. F^{⊢▶}-prime-strips are defined in the same way with ‡F^{⊢▶}_v. A morphism of F^{⊢⊥}- (resp. F^{⊢▶}-) prime-strips is a collection of isomorphisms, indexed by V, between the constituent objects (IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (iii)). (iii) An F^{⊩⊥}-prime-strip *F^{⊩⊥} = (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V, *F^{⊢⊥}, {*ρ_v}_{v∈V}) satisfies conditions (a) to (f) of IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (iv) for an F^⊩-prime-strip, with the F^⊢-prime-strip portion replaced by an F^{⊢⊥}-prime-strip; an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip *F^{⊩▶} = (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V, *F^{⊢▶}, {*ρ_v}_{v∈V}) likewise with an F^{⊢▶}-prime-strip; routine details are left to the reader. A morphism of F^{⊩⊥}- (resp. F^{⊩▶}-) prime-strips is an isomorphism between collections of data.
explicit_hypotheses: an F^⊢-prime-strip ‡F^⊢ = {‡F^⊢_v}_{v∈V} relative to the given initial Θ-data
IUT3.Def2_4.conclusion: Definitions: the collections ‡F^{⊢⊥}, ‡F^{⊢▶} attached to ‡F^⊢ via the submonoids O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^▷(−) and the quotients O^▶(−); F^{⊢⊥}- and F^{⊢▶}-prime-strips (placewise isomorphic to these, with an object of TM^⊢ at v ∈ V^arc) and their morphisms (V-indexed collections of isomorphisms); F^{⊩⊥}- and F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips (data (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V, *F^{⊢⊥} or *F^{⊢▶}, {*ρ_v}) satisfying IUTchI, Definition 5.2 (iv) (a) to (f) with the substitution) and their morphisms (isomorphisms of data).

IUT3.Rem2_4_1.content: (i) Applying Definition 2.4 (i) to the F^⊩-prime-strips F^⊩_env(†D_>) of Corollary 2.3, the multiradiality of Corollary 2.3 (i) implies a corresponding multiradiality assertion for the associated F^{⊩⊥}-prime-strips F^{⊩⊥}_env(†D_>). (ii) In that situation, at v ∈ V^bad the submonoids O^⊥(−) ⊆ O^▷(−) may be regarded naturally (Proposition 2.1 (ii); Theorem 2.2 (ii)) as submonoids of ∞Ψ^⊥_env(†D_>)_v of Theorem 2.2 (ii), (a_v); the resulting inclusion is compatible with the multiradiality of (i) and with the multiradiality of the data †R^bad of Corollary 2.3, (c_R), implied by Corollary 2.3 (i).

IUT3.Rem2_4_2.content: (i) 'One verifies immediately' that, as for F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips (IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)), one may associate to an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip *F^{⊩▶} a pilot object in its global realified Frobenioid portion *C^⊩. (ii) For v ∈ V over v ∈ V_mod and v_Q ∈ V_Q := V(Q): r_v := [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}]·log(p_v) ∈ R if v ∈ V^good; r_v := [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}]·ord_v(q_v)·log(p_v) ∈ R if v ∈ V^bad, where ord_v : K^×_v → Q is the p_v-adic valuation normalized by ord_v(p_v) = 1 and q_v is as in IUTchI, Example 3.2 (iv); and r^▶_v := −r_v / Σ_{w ∈ V^bad} r_w (IUTchI, Example 3.5, Remark 3.5.1; weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii)). (iii) An ordered monoid M isomorphic to R determines (M, {M_v}_{v∈V}, {ρ_{M_v} : M_v ≅ M}_{v∈V}), with M_v a copy of M and ρ_{M_v} multiplication by r^▶_v (an isomorphism of monoids that reverses the ordering). (iv) A pilot element η_M ∈ M, η_M < 0, gives η_{M_v} ∈ M_v and (M, {M^▶_v}, {ρ_{M^▶_v} : M^▶_v ↪ M}): for v ∈ V^non, M^▶_v ⊆ M_v the submonoid generated by η_{M_v} (≅ N); for v ∈ V^arc, M^▶_v ⊆ M_v the submonoid of elements ≤ 0 (≅ R_{≥0}); ρ_{M^▶_v} the restriction of ρ_{M_v}; 'it follows immediately' that ρ_{M^▶_v}(η_{M_v}) = r^▶_v·η_M for each v ∈ V. (v) A converse to (i): the Picard group constructions Pic_Φ(−), Pic_C(−) of [FrdI], Theorem 5.1 (i), applied to any object of *C^⊩ give canonically isomorphic groups Pic(*C^⊩), which by [FrdI], Theorem 6.4 (i), (ii) carries a canonical ordered monoid structure isomorphic to R; the pilot object determines a negative element η_{*C^⊩} ∈ Pic(*C^⊩); 'one verifies immediately' that (iii) with M := Pic(*C^⊩) suffices to reconstruct (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V), and (iv) with M := Pic(*C^⊩), η_M := η_{*C^⊩} suffices to reconstruct (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V, {Φ_{*F^{⊢▶}_v}}_{v∈V}, {*ρ_v}_{v∈V}), where Φ_{*F^{⊢▶}_v} is the constant divisor monoid (≅ N or R_{≥0}) of *F^{⊢▶}_v ([FrdI], Corollary 4.11 (iii); [FrdII], Theorem 1.2 (i)). (vi) Consequently, starting from M = Pic(*C^⊩), the Frobenioid *C^⊩ is a common container in which distinct choices of negative pilot element, and the data reconstructed from them, may be compared. Comparing the constructions of (v) for positive and negative η_M (i.e. reversed order structures) yields Frobenioids whose pre-steps (inclusions of line bundles; [FrdI], Definition 1.2 (iii)) go in opposite directions; they can be compared only in an ambient category where pre-steps are invertible, in which all objects become isomorphic, so that distinguishing distinct elements of Pic(*C^⊩), i.e. distinct arithmetic degrees, becomes meaningless (cf. positivity in Remark 2.1.1 (v)).
explicit_hypotheses: for (i), (v), (vi): an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip *F^{⊩▶} as in Definition 2.4 (iii)
for (ii): v ∈ V lying over v ∈ V_mod and v_Q ∈ V_Q := V(Q); q_v as in IUTchI, Example 3.2 (iv); ord_v the p_v-adic valuation on K^×_v normalized by ord_v(p_v) = 1
for (iii): an ordered monoid M isomorphic as an ordered monoid to R with its usual additive and order structures
for (iv): a pilot element η_M ∈ M with η_M < 0
implicit_hypotheses: V^bad ≠ ∅ and Σ_{w ∈ V^bad} r_w ≠ 0, so that r^▶_v is defined (V^bad ≠ ∅ is part of the initial Θ-data, IUTchI, Definition 3.1 (b))
IUT3.Rem2_4_2.conclusion: (i) A pilot object is associated to each F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip. (ii) Definitions of r_v and r^▶_v = −r_v / Σ_{w ∈ V^bad} r_w. (iii), (iv) Constructions from (M, η_M), with ρ_{M^▶_v}(η_{M_v}) = r^▶_v·η_M for each v ∈ V. (v) With M = Pic(*C^⊩) (an ordered monoid isomorphic to R) and η_M the class of the pilot object, the data of (iii) reconstruct (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V) and the data of (iv) reconstruct (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V, {Φ_{*F^{⊢▶}_v}}, {*ρ_v}). (vi) Distinct negative pilot elements can be compared inside the common container *C^⊩, whereas comparing positive and negative pilot elements forces an ambient category in which pre-steps are invertible and all objects isomorphic, making distinct arithmetic degrees indistinguishable.
definitions_required: Pic_Φ, Pic_C of a Frobenioid ([FrdI], Theorem 5.1 (i)); divisor monoid; pre-step ([FrdI], Definition 1.2 (iii))
obligations: Prove (i): existence of the pilot object of an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip (page 89: 'one verifies immediately').
Prove (iv): ρ_{M^▶_v}(η_{M_v}) = r^▶_v·η_M; immediate from ρ_{M_v} being multiplication by r^▶_v and η_{M_v} the copy of η_M.

Prove (v): the reconstruction of (*C^⊩, Prime(*C^⊩) ≅ V) and of the divisor monoids and the *ρ_v from Pic(*C^⊩) and η_{*C^⊩} (page 90: 'one verifies immediately'); it also relies on [FrdI], Theorems 5.1 (i), 6.4 (i), (ii).

Check that r^▶_v < 0 for all v ∈ V, so that ρ_{M_v} reverses the ordering (page 90): this needs r_v > 0 for every v and the bad-place sum to be positive, i.e. ord_v(q_v) > 0 at v ∈ V^bad and log(p_v) > 0.
Use these normalizations consistently with the weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, and the procession-normalized log-volumes of Proposition 3.9 and Corollary 3.12.
ambiguities: Page 89: log(p_v) at archimedean v ∈ V^good is not defined on this page; the convention for p_v at archimedean places must be taken from IUTchI, §0 or Example 3.5.
Page 89: the denominator of r^▶_v sums over V^bad only, while r^▶_v is defined for every v ∈ V, including v ∈ V^good; this is as printed.
Page 91, (vi): 'meaningless' is an informal conclusion; the formal content is that in a category where all pre-steps are invertible all objects of the Frobenioid become isomorphic.

IUT3.Prop3_1.content: Local holomorphic tensor packets. For an n-capsule {α𝔉}_{α∈A} of F-prime-strips and v | v_Q, log(αF_v) is an inductive limit of topological modules of finite dimension over Q_{v_Q}; the 1-tensor packet is v_Q ↦ log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{v|v_Q} log(αF_v), and the n-tensor packet is log(AF_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α∈A} log(αF_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{{v_α}} {⊗_α log(αF_{v_α})}, tensor products of ind-topological modules (page 92). (i) The ind-topological field structures on the log(αF_v) determine an ind-topological ring structure on log(AF_{v_Q}), an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields; the decompositions are determined by the ring structure and compatible with the action of αΠ_v. (ii) For α ∈ A, v | v_Q: log(A,αF_v) = log(αF_v) ⊗ {⊗_{β∈A∖{α}} log(βF_{v_Q})} ⊆ log(AF_{v_Q}) is a direct summand and an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields. Tensoring with 1's in the factors β ≠ α gives a natural injective ring homomorphism log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) which, for suitable cofinal objects of the inductive systems, induces an isomorphism of an object of the domain onto each direct summand field of the corresponding object of the codomain. Hence the integral structure Ψ̄ = Ψ_{log(αF_v)} ∪ {0} ⊆ log(αF_v) determines integral structures on each direct summand field of log(A,αF_v) and log(AF_{v_Q}) (page 93). Remark 3.1.1 (i) (page 94): log(αF_v) ≅ k̄, Ψ̄ ≅ O_k̄, log(A,αF_v) ≅ ⊗ k̄ ≅ lim ⊕ k̄ ⊇ lim ⊕ O_k̄, so the integral structures are copies of O_k̄ in the copies of k̄.
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in IUTchI Def 3.1
an n-capsule {α𝔉}_{α∈A} of F-prime-strips (IUTchI §0, Def 5.2 (i))
v ∈ V, v_Q ∈ V_Q with v | v_Q (part (ii) also fixes α ∈ A)
IUT3.Prop3_1.conclusion: (i) log(AF_{v_Q}) carries an ind-topological ring structure, an inductive limit of direct sums of ind-topological fields, with decompositions determined by the ring structure and αΠ_v-compatible; (ii) log(A,αF_v) is a direct summand of the same kind, the map log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) is injective and induces isomorphisms onto each direct summand field for cofinal objects, and Ψ̄ determines, through these isomorphisms, an integral structure on each direct summand field.
obligations: Formalize topological tensor products of local fields and their decomposition into products of fields.

Record two lattices and the map between them. Lattice L1 (the one on page 93): the product, over the direct summand fields of a finite object of log(A,αF_v) or log(AF_{v_Q}), of the copy of the ring of integers transported from Ψ̄ by the isomorphism of page 93; this is the normalization (integral closure) in the product of fields. Lattice L2 (not on page 93): the image of the tensor product of the rings of integers of the factors. The map is the inclusion L2 → L1 induced by the inclusions of rings of integers. Assessment, not from the page: L2 can be a proper order in L1, so the two must not be identified. Every later use (log-volume 0 of the integral structures, Prop 3.9 (i)) refers to L1.
Prove that the integral structure transported to a summand field does not depend on the cofinal object chosen.
ambiguities: Assessment: the page does not mention a tensor product of rings of integers; an earlier description of these integral structures as tensor products of rings of integers was not what the page states and has been replaced.

IUT3.Rem3_1_1.content: (i) Concrete description of Prop 3.1: log(αF_v) ≅ k̄ with k = K_v, Ψ̄ ≅ O_k̄; integral structures are copies of O_k̄ (pages 93 to 94). (ii) Weights: log-volumes on the portion of log(αF_v) for K_v are taken with weight [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1}; for direct sums over v | v_Q the normalized weight is 1/([K_v:(F_mod)_v]·Σ_{w|v_Q}[(F_mod)_w : Q_{v_Q}]); for tensor products over α ∈ A the weight 1/∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}], normalized to 1/((∏_α[K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}])·Σ_{{w_α}}∏_α[(F_mod)_{w_α}:Q_{v_Q}]); all normalized so that multiplication by p_{v_Q} adds or subtracts log(p_{v_Q}) (pages 94 to 95). (iii) Such weighted sums of log-volumes do not in general arise as a positive real multiple of the logarithm of a measure in the usual sense. For a direct product region (a product of compact subsets of positive measure of the direct summands) the weighted sum is computed directly; a direct product pre-region uses relatively compact factors; for arbitrary Borel sets the construction of (iv) applies, with V = ∏_α V_{v_Q}, N_v = ∏_α [K_{v_α}:(F_mod)_{v_α}], M_v the (radial, if archimedean) summand of Prop 3.1; on direct product regions a suitable positive normalization factor times the log of the E-weighted measure gives the weighted sums of (ii) (pages 95 to 96). (iv) For a nonempty finite set V, nonempty finite sets E_v and measure spaces (M_v, μ_v), the E-weighted measure μ_E(S) ∈ R_{≥0} ∪ {+∞} of a Borel set S ⊆ M_V is the measure of S_E = (∏_{e∈E} S) ∩ M_{E*V} in M_{E*V} ≅ M_W; it depends only on N = {N_v = |E_v|}; for S = ∏_v S_v with S_v compact of positive measure, (1/N_E)·μ^log_E(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v)·μ^log_v(S_v), N_E = ∏_v N_v (pages 96 to 97).
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Prop 3.1
for (iv): V a nonempty finite set, E_v nonempty finite sets, (M_v, μ_v) nonempty measure spaces in the sense of (iii)
IUT3.Rem3_1_1.conclusion: Weighted sums of log-volumes are defined with the weights of (ii); on direct product regions they equal (1/N_E)·log μ_E(S) = Σ_v (1/N_v)·log μ_v(S_v), and the E-weighted measure μ_E extends them to arbitrary Borel sets; they are in general not a positive multiple of the log of an ordinary measure on the original product.
obligations: Verify the (iv) identity as a product-measure computation on M_{E*V} ≅ M_W (elementary once the spaces are fixed).
Fix the normalization factor of (iii) that relates (1/N_E)·log μ_E to the weighted sums of (ii); the page says only 'a suitable positive real number'.
ambiguities: The value set of μ_E is R_{≥0} ∪ {+∞}; finiteness for the regions used later is not stated at this point.

Pages 95 to 96: the weighted sums of log-volumes of (ii) are in general not a positive real multiple of the logarithm of a volume or measure in the usual sense; only for direct product (pre-)regions is their computation straightforward, and for these a suitable positive normalization factor times the logarithm of the E-weighted measure μ_E (a measure on M_{E*V} ≅ M_W, not on the original product of the direct summands) gives them.

IUT3.Rem3_1_2.content: The local holomorphic tensor packet constructions of Proposition 3.1 may be applied to the capsules of the F-prime-strip processions, the F-prime-strip analogues of the holomorphic processions of IUTchI, Proposition 4.11 (i), and Proposition 6.9 (i).
IUT3.Rem3_1_2.conclusion: The constructions of Proposition 3.1 apply to each capsule of an F-prime-strip procession. No proof given; the statement is an observation about applicability.
definitions_required: F-prime-strip analogue of a holomorphic procession (IUTchI, Remark 5.6.1, Remark 6.12.1)
obligations: Apply the constructions of Proposition 3.1 capsule by capsule; no new mathematics.

IUT3.Prop3_2.content: Local mono-analytic tensor packets: for an n-capsule {αD^⊢}_{α ∈ A} of D^⊢-prime-strips, defines the 1-tensor packet v_Q ↦ log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) = ⊕_{v | v_Q} log(αD^⊢_v), the n-tensor packet log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}) = ⊗_{α ∈ A} log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) (tensor product of ind-topological modules), and the submodules log(A,αD^⊢_v); the same notation is used for capsules of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips. Then (i) mono-analytic and holomorphic packets are related by natural poly-isomorphisms and (ii) mono-analytic log-shells give integral structures.
explicit_hypotheses: an n-capsule {αD^⊢}_{α ∈ A} of D^⊢-prime-strips relative to the given initial Θ-data (IUTchI, §0, Definition 4.1 (iii))
IUT3.Prop3_2.conclusion: (i) If the capsule arises from the capsule of F-prime-strips of Proposition 3.1, the poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii) induce natural poly-isomorphisms of ind-topological modules from the mono-analytic packets log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}), log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}), log(A,αD^⊢_v) through the F^{⊢×μ}-versions to the holomorphic packets of Proposition 3.1. (ii) The mono-analytic log-shells determine integral structures: topological submodules I(αD^⊢_{v_Q}), I(A D^⊢_{v_Q}), I(A,αD^⊢_v) on the Q-spans (by direct sums and tensor products at nonarchimedean v_Q; as closed unit balls of the induced direct sum and tensor product Hermitian metrics at archimedean v_Q), with Q-spans I^Q((−)) and the same notation for F- and F^{⊢×μ}-versions via the poly-isomorphisms of (i).
obligations: Define tensor products of ind-topological modules and show that the poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii) induce poly-isomorphisms of packets.
Define the integral structures at nonarchimedean v_Q from the mono-analytic log-shells and at archimedean v_Q as closed unit balls of the induced Hermitian metrics.
The proof (page 99) says the assertions follow immediately from the definitions and cited references; the blocking is inherited from Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii).
ambiguities: At archimedean v_Q the mono-analytic log-shell is regarded as the closed unit ball of a Hermitian metric (page 98); that this subset is indeed such a unit ball is taken for granted.

explicit_hypotheses: the capsule {αD^⊢}_{α ∈ A} arises from the capsule of F-prime-strips {αF}_{α ∈ A} of Proposition 3.1, with associated capsule {αF^{⊢×μ}} of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips
IUT3.Prop3_2.i.conclusion: The poly-isomorphisms log(†D^⊢_v) ≅ log(†F^{⊢×μ}_v) ≅ log(†F_v) of Proposition 1.2 (vi), (vii) induce natural poly-isomorphisms log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) ≅ log(αF^{⊢×μ}_{v_Q}) ≅ log(αF_{v_Q}), log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}) ≅ log(A F^{⊢×μ}_{v_Q}) ≅ log(A F_{v_Q}), log(A,αD^⊢_v) ≅ log(A,αF^{⊢×μ}_v) ≅ log(A,αF_v) between mono-analytic and holomorphic tensor packets.

explicit_hypotheses: v | v_Q with v_Q ∈ V_Q^non, or v | v_Q with v_Q ∈ V_Q^arc
IUT3.Prop3_2.ii.conclusion: For v_Q nonarchimedean, the mono-analytic log-shells I_{†D^⊢_v} of Proposition 1.2 (vi) determine, by direct sums and tensor products, topological submodules I(αD^⊢_{v_Q}) ⊆ log(αD^⊢_{v_Q}), I(A D^⊢_{v_Q}) ⊆ log(A D^⊢_{v_Q}), I(A,αD^⊢_v) ⊆ log(A,αD^⊢_v), regarded as integral structures on the Q-spans. For v_Q archimedean, regarding the mono-analytic log-shell of Proposition 1.2 (vii) as the closed unit ball of a Hermitian metric on log(†D^⊢_v) and taking the induced direct sum and tensor product Hermitian metrics, the closed unit balls give the corresponding integral structures. I^Q((−)) denotes the Q-span; the notation is transported to F- and F^{⊢×μ}-versions by (i).

IUT3.Prop3_4.content: Local packet-theoretic Frobenioids: (i) single packet monoids obtained as images of Ψ_{log(αF_v)}, its units and its realification inside log(A,αF_v); (ii) local LGP-monoids Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v, ∞Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v constructed by a functorial algorithm in a log-link ‡HT → †HT of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, whose components labeled j act on I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j;‡F_v). Fig. 3.1 depicts the splitting monoids q^{j^2} acting on the (j+1)-capsules S^±_{j+1}.

IUT3.Prop3_4.conclusion: (i) The images of Ψ_{log(αF_v)}, Ψ^×_{log(αF_v)}, Ψ^R_{log(αF_v)} under log(αF_v) → log(A,αF_v) are monoids with G_v(αΠ_v)-actions (v nonarchimedean) or with an Aut-holomorphic orbispace and Kummer structure (v archimedean), acting multiplicatively on subquotients of log(A,αF_v); they determine a Frobenioid (resp. collection of data) naturally isomorphic to log(αF_v). (ii) There is a functorial algorithm in the log-link ‡HT → †HT producing the LGP-monoids Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v and ∞Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v; for v ∈ V^bad the component labeled j ∈ {1, ..., l*} of the Galois invariants of the entire LGP-monoid is a subset of I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j;‡F_v) acting multiplicatively on it, and for any v the component labeled j of the Galois invariants of the unit portion is likewise a subset of I^Q(S^±_{j+1},j;‡F_v) acting multiplicatively on it.
obligations: See part records. Proof (page 103): the assertions follow immediately from the definitions and the cited references.
ambiguities: The notation (†HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}) in Ψ_{F_LGP}(†HT)_v is called a slight abuse of notation (page 103): the monoids are constructed from the log-link, not from †HT alone.

IUT3.Prop3_5.content: (i) Vertically coric LGP-monoids and their Kummer isomorphisms. (ii) Upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence: (a) at nonarchimedean v_Q the mono-analytic integral structure contains the Kummer images of units, also after the m'-th iterate of the log-link; (b) at archimedean v_Q the closed unit ball contains the units and the closed balls of radius π, with a surjection via iterates; (c) at bad v the splitting monoids are mutually compatible up to roots of unity, which via the log-link is 'addition by zero'. Invariance under the column translation symmetry.
explicit_hypotheses: a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,m HT}_{n,m∈Z} relative to the given initial Θ-data, arising from a Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Def 1.4)
for each n, the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater n,◦HT determined up to isomorphism by vertical coricity (Thm 1.5 (i))
obligations: State and prove the containments (a), (b) as inclusions of explicit subsets of p-adic and complex fields.
Prove that roots of unity in the domain map to 0 under the p-adic logarithm (c).

IUT3.Ex3_6.content: Concrete representations of the Frobenioid F^⊛_mod (the Frobenioid †F^⊛_mod of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (iii), i.e. of arithmetic line bundles on the stack S_mod of IUTchI, Remark 3.1.5, with the label † arising from data as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1): (i) a rational function torsor version F^⊛_MOD; (ii) a local fractional ideal version F^⊛_mod (fraktur); (iii) a natural isomorphism between them, unique on perfections and realifications.

F^⊛_mod the Frobenioid †F^⊛_mod of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (iii), with † arising from data as in IUTchI, Definition 3.1

IUT3.Ex3_6.i.content: Rational function torsor version. For each v ∈ V, the valuation of K_v gives a group homomorphism β_v : F^×_mod → K^×_v/O^×_{K_v}. An object T = (T, {t_v}_{v∈V}) of F^⊛_MOD consists of (a) an F^×_mod-torsor T and (b) for each v ∈ V a trivialization t_v of the torsor T_v obtained from T by change of structure group along β_v, such that some t ∈ T induces t_v for all but finitely many v. An elementary morphism T_1 → T_2 is an isomorphism T_1 ≅ T_2 of F^×_mod-torsors that is integral at each v (maps t_{1,v} into the O^▷_{K_v}-orbit of t_{2,v}); a morphism T_1 → T_2 is a positive integer n with an elementary morphism T_1^{⊗n} → T_2. 'One verifies immediately' that F^⊛_MOD has a natural Frobenioid structure ([FrdI], Definition 1.3) with base category the one-arrow category, linear morphisms the elementary morphisms and Frobenius degree n; and 'one verifies immediately' that sending an arithmetic line bundle on S_mod to its restriction to the generic point (an F^×_mod-torsor) with the local trivializations from the local integral structures gives a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity on the rational function monoids F^×_mod ([FrdI], Corollary 4.10).
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Ex3_6
for each v ∈ V, K_v and the homomorphism β_v : F^×_mod → K^×_v/O^×_{K_v} determined by the valuation of v
IUT3.Ex3_6.i.conclusion: F^⊛_MOD is a category with a natural Frobenioid structure (one-arrow base category; elementary morphisms linear; n the Frobenius degree), and there is a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity F^×_mod → F^×_mod on rational function monoids.
definitions_required: Frobenioid, linear morphism, Frobenius degree, rational function monoid ([FrdI])
obligations: Verify the Frobenioid axioms of [FrdI], Definition 1.3 for F^⊛_MOD (page 107: 'one verifies immediately').
Construct the isomorphism F^⊛_mod ≅ F^⊛_MOD and check that it induces the identity on F^×_mod (page 107: 'one verifies immediately').
ambiguities: Page 107: β_v is described as a group homomorphism to K^×_v/O^×_{K_v}; at archimedean v this quotient is R_{>0}, and the trivializations t_v there are elements of an R_{>0}-torsor; the text does not separate the two cases.
Page 107: 'evident notion' of composition of morphisms and of tensor powers is not spelled out; the natural composite of (n_1, φ_1) and (n_2, φ_2) is (n_1 n_2, φ_2 ∘ φ_1^{⊗ n_2}).

IUT3.Ex3_6.ii.content: Local fractional ideal version. An object J = {J_v}_{v∈V} of F^⊛_mod (fraktur) is a collection of 'fractional ideals' J_v ⊆ K_v: a finitely generated nonzero O_{K_v}-submodule of K_v for v ∈ V^non, a positive real multiple of O_{K_v} := {λ ∈ K_v : |λ| ≤ 1} for v ∈ V^arc, with J_v = O_{K_v} for all but finitely many v. F^×_mod acts by f·J = {f·J_v}; there are tensor powers J^{⊗n}, n ∈ Z. An elementary morphism J_1 → J_2 is an f ∈ F^×_mod integral with respect to J_1, J_2, i.e. f·J_{1,v} ⊆ J_{2,v} for every v ∈ V; a morphism is a positive integer n with an elementary morphism J_1^{⊗n} → J_2. 'One verifies immediately' that this category has a natural Frobenioid structure (one-arrow base category, elementary morphisms linear, n the Frobenius degree), and that associating to J the arithmetic line bundle on S_mod obtained from the trivial one by modifying its integral structure at each v as prescribed by J_v gives a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_mod inducing the identity on F^×_mod ([FrdI], Corollary 4.10).
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Ex3_6
IUT3.Ex3_6.ii.conclusion: F^⊛_mod (fraktur) is a category with a natural Frobenioid structure, and there is a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_mod inducing the identity F^×_mod → F^×_mod on rational function monoids.
obligations: Verify the Frobenioid axioms for the fractional ideal category and construct the isomorphism with F^⊛_mod (page 108: 'one verifies immediately', twice).

The underlying objects (fractional ideals at finite places, scaled unit balls at archimedean places, almost all trivial) are adelic data close to Mathlib's FractionalIdeal; the arithmetic line bundle picture is not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: Page 107: the tensor power J^{⊗n} for n ∈ Z is called 'evident'; for n < 0 it means the inverse fractional ideals.

IUT3.Ex3_6.iii.content: Composing the isomorphisms of (i) and (ii) gives a natural isomorphism of Frobenioids F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity on the rational function monoids F^×_mod. 'One verifies immediately' that this isomorphism is not necessarily determined by the condition that it induce the identity on F^×_mod, but the induced isomorphism between the perfections (hence also realifications) of F^⊛_mod (fraktur) and F^⊛_MOD is completely determined by this condition.
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Ex3_6
the isomorphisms of IUT3.Ex3_6.i and IUT3.Ex3_6.ii
IUT3.Ex3_6.iii.conclusion: There is a natural isomorphism F^⊛_mod (fraktur) ≅ F^⊛_MOD inducing the identity on F^×_mod; it is not necessarily determined by that condition, but the induced isomorphism on perfections and realifications is uniquely determined by it.
definitions_required: perfection and realification of a Frobenioid ([FrdI])
obligations: Prove that an isomorphism of these Frobenioids inducing the identity on F^×_mod is unique after passing to perfections (page 108: 'one verifies immediately'; no argument is given), and give an example showing non-uniqueness before perfection, as the text asserts.
ambiguities: Page 108 does not say which isomorphisms other than the composite also induce the identity on F^×_mod; the non-uniqueness is asserted without an example.

IUT3.Rem3_6_1.content: For the constructions of Example 3.6 (i), the homomorphisms β_v, v ∈ V, may be thought of as a collection of subquotients of the perfection (F^×_mod)^pf of F^×_mod, each equipped with a submonoid of 'nonnegative elements', completely determined by the ring structure of the field F_mod (its structure as the field of moduli of X_F).
explicit_hypotheses: the constructions of Example 3.6 (i)
IUT3.Rem3_6_1.conclusion: The data {β_v}_{v∈V} are equivalent to a collection of subquotients of (F^×_mod)^pf with submonoids of nonnegative elements, all determined by the ring structure of F_mod.
obligations: Make precise the passage from β_v : F^×_mod → K^×_v/O^×_{K_v} to a subquotient of (F^×_mod)^pf with a positive cone, and prove it is determined by the ring structure of F_mod.
ambiguities: Page 108 does not say which subquotient is meant; the natural reading is the image of (F^×_mod)^pf under the perfection of β_v, with nonnegative elements those of nonnegative valuation, but this is not stated.

IUT3.Prop3_7.content: Global packet-theoretic Frobenioids: from the number field image (†M̄^⊛_MOD)_α of (†M̄^⊛_mod)_α in log(A F_{v_Q}) one constructs Frobenioids (†F^⊛_MOD)_α (rational function torsor version) and (†F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_α (local fractional ideal version) isomorphic to (†F^⊛_mod)_α; from the log-link of Proposition 3.4 (ii) one constructs the global realified LGP- and 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Frobenioids C^⊩_LGP, C^⊩_𝔩𝔤𝔭 with F^⊩-prime-strips †𝔉^⊩_LGP, †𝔉^⊩_𝔩𝔤𝔭; and product embeddings into ∏_{j ∈ F_l^*} of realified copies, giving an algorithm producing objects of the global categories from local fractional ideals generated by the LGP-monoids at bad v.

Statements in the part records.
obligations: See part records. Proof (page 112): the assertions follow immediately from the definitions and the cited references.

IUT3.Prop3_7.v.content: Realified product embeddings and non-realified global Frobenioids.
explicit_hypotheses: the constructions of (iii), (iv)
IUT3.Prop3_7.v.conclusion: There is a commutative diagram of categories with horizontal embeddings C^⊩_LGP(†HT) ↪ ∏_{j ∈ F_l^*} (†F^⊛ℝ_MOD)_j and C^⊩_𝔩𝔤𝔭(†HT) ↪ ∏_{j ∈ F_l^*} (†F^⊛ℝ_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_j (tautological from (iii), (iv)) and vertical isomorphisms (left: from the second isomorphism of the final display of (iv); right: product of realifications of copies of the inverse of the second isomorphism of the final display of (ii)). Using the definition of (†F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_j via local fractional ideals and the product of realification functors ∏_j (†F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_j → ∏_j (†F^⊛ℝ_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_j (FrdI, Proposition 5.3), one obtains an algorithm constructing objects of C^⊩_𝔩𝔤𝔭(†HT) and C^⊩_LGP(†HT), compatibly with the local isomorphisms {†ρ_{𝔩𝔤𝔭,v}}, {†ρ_{LGP,v}}, from the local fractional ideals generated by elements of Ψ_{F_𝔩𝔤𝔭}(†HT)_v, v ∈ V^bad.

IUT3.Def3_8.content: (i) Θ-pilot objects and q-pilot objects; (ii) the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link and the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link between Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters, relative to a log-link, as full poly-isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips; (iii) the LGP-Gaussian and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices, whose vertical arrows are full log-links and horizontal arrows Θ^{×μ}_LGP-, resp. Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links.

Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data (for (ii), (iii))
IUT3.Def3_8.conclusion: Definitions of Θ-pilot and q-pilot objects, of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links, and of the LGP-Gaussian and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices; see the part records.
obligations: See part records.

IUT3.Def3_8.i.content: In the situation of Proposition 3.7 (iv), (v), write Ψ^⊥_{F_lgp}(−)_v := Ψ^⊥_{F_LGP}(−)_v for v ∈ V^bad (Proposition 3.5 (ii) (c)). A Θ-pilot object is the object of ∏_{j∈F*_l} (†F^⊛_MOD)_j or ∏_{j∈F*_l} (†F^⊛_mod (fraktur))_j, as well as its realification regarded as an object of †C^⊩_LGP = C^⊩_LGP(†HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}) or †C^⊩_lgp = C^⊩_lgp(†HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}) (Proposition 3.7 (iii), (iv), (v)), determined by any collection, indexed by v ∈ V^bad, of generators up to torsion of the monoids Ψ^⊥_{F_lgp}(†HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF})_v. A q-pilot object is the object of the global realified Frobenioid †C^⊩_△ of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (i), determined by any collection, indexed by v ∈ V^bad, of generators up to torsion of the splitting monoid of the split Frobenioid †F^⊢_{△,v} (the v-data of the F^⊢-prime-strip †F^⊢_△ of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (i)), concretely by the q_v, v ∈ V^bad (IUTchI, Example 3.2 (iv)).

v ∈ V^bad for the generators
IUT3.Def3_8.i.conclusion: Definition of the Θ-pilot object (in ∏_j (†F^⊛_MOD)_j or ∏_j (†F^⊛_mod)_j, or its realification in †C^⊩_LGP or †C^⊩_lgp) and of the q-pilot object (in †C^⊩_△), each determined by a V^bad-indexed collection of generators up to torsion of the relevant splitting monoids.
obligations: Show the object is independent of the choice of generators up to torsion (implicit in 'determined by any collection', page 112).

IUT3.Def3_8.ii.content: Let ‡HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} be a log-link of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters and *HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater. With *F^⊩_△ the F^⊩-prime-strip of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (i), and *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△, †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP, †F^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips associated to *F^⊩_△, †F^⊩_LGP, †F^⊩_lgp (Proposition 3.7 (iii), (iv); IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii), the functorial algorithm of Definition 4.9 (vi)), the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ is called the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → *HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}, relative to the log-link ‡HT → †HT, and the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link, relative to the same log-link (in the style of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (iii)).
explicit_hypotheses: a log-link ‡HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → †HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters
a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater *HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}
all relative to the given initial Θ-data
IUT3.Def3_8.ii.conclusion: Definition: Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link := the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△; Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link := the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△; both from †HT to *HT, relative to the log-link ‡HT → †HT.
obligations: Formalize F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips and full poly-isomorphisms; the link is then the set of all isomorphisms between two such prime-strips.

IUT3.Def3_8.iii.content: For a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters indexed by pairs of integers, the diagram whose vertical arrows n,mHT → n,m+1HT are the full log-links and whose horizontal arrow n,mHT → n+1,mHT is the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (resp. Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link) relative to the full log-link n,m−1HT → n,mHT (as in (ii)) is the LGP-Gaussian (resp. lgp-Gaussian) log-theta-lattice. Either diagram is represented symbolically (cf. Definition 1.4) by the oriented graph with vertices • (the n,mHT) and arrows • → • horizontally and vertically.
explicit_hypotheses: a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data
IUT3.Def3_8.iii.conclusion: Definition: the LGP-Gaussian (resp. lgp-Gaussian) log-theta-lattice is the Z × Z diagram with full log-links n,mHT → n,m+1HT and Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links (resp. Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links) n,mHT → n+1,mHT relative to n,m−1HT → n,mHT.
obligations: Represent the lattice as a Z × Z-indexed diagram once the links are formalized.
ambiguities: A definition, so there is no proof. Each horizontal arrow at height m uses the vertical log-link from height m − 1 (page 114).

IUT3.Rem3_8_1.content: The LGP-Gaussian and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices are closely related; the theory mainly uses the LGP-Gaussian one (reasons in Remark 3.10.1 (ii)), but the computation of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link involves the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link and related Θ-pilot objects essentially. Both the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and the Θ^{×μ}_lgp-link map Θ-pilot objects to q-pilot objects. The terminology 'Θ-pilot/q-pilot objects' is consistent with the notion of pilot object associated to an F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip (IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)).
explicit_hypotheses: the links and pilot objects of Definition 3.8
IUT3.Rem3_8_1.conclusion: The Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links each map Θ-pilot objects to q-pilot objects, and these pilot objects are pilot objects in the sense of IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii).
obligations: Prove that every isomorphism of the full poly-isomorphism †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ (resp. lgp) carries the Θ-pilot object to the q-pilot object (page 114: 'we note, for future reference'; no argument is given). This requires that the Θ-pilot object is the pilot object of †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP and the q-pilot object that of *F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ in the sense of IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii), and that isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips preserve pilot objects.
ambiguities: Page 114 states the mapping property and the consistency of terminology without argument.
