IUT3.Prop3_9.content: Log-volumes for packets and processions. Proof: 'follow immediately from the definitions'.
explicit_hypotheses: the situations of Prop 3.2 (i), (ii) (parts (i), (ii)), of Prop 3.7 (i), (ii) (part (iii)), and an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (part (iv))
IUT3.Prop3_9.conclusion: (i) packet-normalized and procession-normalized holomorphic log-volumes with the stated normalizations; (ii) compatible mono-analytic log-volumes, constructible from D^⊢-prime-strips; (iii) a global log-volume on families with zero local log-volume at all but finitely many v_Q, invariant under (M_MOD)_α and permutations of A, equal to the arithmetic degree relative to a suitable normalization; (iv) log-link compatibility of these log-volumes. Details in the part records.
obligations: See part records.
ambiguities: Weighted packet log-volumes are in general not the logarithm of a measure on the original product (Remark 3.1.1 (iii), page 95); on direct product regions they are a normalized logarithm of the E-weighted measure of Remark 3.1.1 (iv), pages 96 to 97. The local normalization is by the condition that multiplication by p_v adds −log(p_v) (page 115), achieved by the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, applied to Haar log-volumes with μ(O) = 1 (dividing by the local degree a second time would be wrong); see IUT3.Prop3_9.i.

IUT3.Prop3_9.i.content: Packet-normalized log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,α,v} : M(I^Q(−)) → R, where M(−) is the set of nonempty compact open subsets (nonarchimedean) or compact closures of nonempty open subsets (archimedean). The local holomorphic integral structures have log-volume 0; multiplying by p_v adds −log(p_v) (nonarchimedean); multiplying by e adds 1 (archimedean). μ^log_{A,v_Q} is invariant under permutations of A. Procession-normalization: average over the capsules of a procession.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Prop 3.2 (i), (ii)
v ∈ V, v | v_Q, α ∈ A
IUT3.Prop3_9.i.conclusion: Log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,v_Q}, μ^log_{A,α,v} : M(I^Q(−)) → R exist, determined by the p_{v_Q}-adic (respectively radial) log-volumes on the direct summand fields and the normalized weights of Rem 3.1.1 (ii) to (iv); the integral structures of Prop 3.1 (ii) have log-volume 0; multiplication by p_v adds −log(p_v) (respectively by e adds 1); μ^log_{A,v_Q} is invariant under permutations of A; on products over the capsules of a procession (as in Prop 3.4 (ii)) the procession-normalized log-volume is the average over the capsules.
obligations: Define the local log-volume on each direct summand field K_v as the logarithm of Haar measure normalized by μ(O_{K_v}) = 1 (p_{v_Q}-adic; radial at archimedean v_Q), and form the packet log-volume with the normalized weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, namely 1/([K_v : (F_mod)_v]·Σ_{w | v_Q} [(F_mod)_w : Q_{v_Q}]). These weights already contain the division by the local degree: with one place over v_Q, (F_mod)_v = Q_p and K_v quadratic, the plain Haar log-volume of p·O_{K_v} is −2·log(p) and the weight is 1/2, giving −log(p) as page 115 requires. Equivalently, one may divide each local Haar log-volume by its degree (as IUT IV, Proposition 1.4 (i), page 13, does) and then use weights without that factor; doing both divides twice and gives −(1/2)·log(p) in the example. A formalization must use exactly one of the two conventions and check that the total shift under multiplication by p_v is −log(p_v).

Define the packet log-volume as the weighted sum over direct summands with the weights of Rem 3.1.1 (ii) on direct product regions, and extend it to other elements of M(−) through the E-weighted measure of Rem 3.1.1 (iv). Do not define it as the logarithm of a single normalized Haar measure on the product: Rem 3.1.1 (iii), page 95, says such weighted sums do not in general arise as a positive multiple of the log of an ordinary measure; on direct product regions page 96 identifies them with a normalized log of μ_E on M_{E*V}, not of a measure on the original product.
Check the scaling rule against the weights: multiplication by p_v shifts each summand log-volume, and the normalized weights make the total shift −log(p_v).

Define the procession-normalized log-volume as the average over j ∈ F*_l (stated on pages 173 and 181), factor 1/l*; Prop 3.4 (ii) (page 102) and Rem 3.9.3 (page 120) corroborate the labels j ∈ {1, ..., l*}. Fix how the j = 0 packet of the procession enters.
ambiguities: The extension of the weighted sum from direct product regions to all of M(−) is given only through Rem 3.1.1 (iv) with 'a suitable normalization factor' (page 96); the factor is not displayed.

Page 115 states the normalization only through its effect (O has log-volume 0, multiplication by p_v adds −log(p_v)); the weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), page 94, carry the division by the local degree, so the local log-volume is the plain Haar log-volume with μ(O) = 1. Remark 3.1.1 (iii), page 95, says these weighted sums are in general not a positive multiple of the logarithm of a measure in the usual sense; page 96 identifies them, on direct product regions only, with a normalized logarithm of the E-weighted measure μ_E of Remark 3.1.1 (iv), which lives on M_{E*V} ≅ M_W, not on the original product.

IUT3.Prop3_9.ii.content: Mono-analytic compatibility: applying p_v-adic or radial log-volumes on mono-analytic log-shells, adjusted for the discrepancy between holomorphic and mono-analytic integral structures (Remark 3.9.1), gives log-volumes on M(I^Q(^α D^⊢_{v_Q})) etc. compatible with (i) via the natural poly-isomorphisms of Prop 3.2 (i), constructible by a functorial algorithm from D^⊢-prime-strips; procession-normalized versions compatible likewise; similarly for F^{⊢×μ}.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Prop 3.2 (i), (ii)
v ∈ V, v | v_Q ∈ V_Q
IUT3.Prop3_9.ii.conclusion: Compatibility of mono-analytic and holomorphic log-volumes under the poly-isomorphisms.
obligations: Prove invariance of the log-volume under every isomorphism in the poly-isomorphism (Ism at nonarchimedean v, independent ±1 at archimedean v).
Make the 'adjusting appropriately' of the discrepancy explicit (Remark 3.9.1 gives a factor of 2 at archimedean places).

IUT3.Prop3_9.iii.content: Global log-volume μ^log_{A,V_Q} on elements of ∏ M(I^Q(^A F_{v_Q})) with zero log-volume at all but finitely many v_Q, obtained by summing; invariant under multiplication by (M^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_α = (M^⊛_MOD)_α and permutations of A; for objects J = {J_v} of (F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_α its value equals the degree of the associated arithmetic line bundle, relative to a suitable normalization.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Proposition 3.7 (i), (ii)
elements of M(I^Q(A F_{V_Q})) ⊆ ∏_{v_Q} M(I^Q(A F_{v_Q})): families whose components have log-volume zero for all but finitely many v_Q (page 117)
IUT3.Prop3_9.iii.conclusion: Global log-volume equals arithmetic degree up to normalization.
obligations: Prove invariance under multiplication by number field elements (product formula).
Fix the normalization and prove equality with the degree.

Record the domain: M(I^Q(AF_{V_Q})) consists of families whose components have log-volume zero for all but finitely many v_Q (page 117); the global log-volume is the finite sum of the nonzero local terms.
ambiguities: 'relative to a suitable normalization' (page 117) is not specified; the sign and scaling of the comparison with the degree are left implicit.

The domain of the global log-volume (page 117) is defined by finite support: all but finitely many components have log-volume exactly zero, so the global log-volume is a finite sum. Summability of the local log-volumes is not what the page requires; a formalization must use the finite-support condition.

IUT3.Prop3_9.iv.content: log-link compatibility: (a) the log-volumes of (i) to (iii) determine log-volumes on the I^Q((−)) that appear in the construction of the local and global LGP and lgp monoids and Frobenioids at (n,m), relative to the log-link (n,m−1) → (n,m); (b) at the level of Q-spans of log-shells the log-volumes indexed by (n,m) are compatible with those indexed by (n,m−1) in the sense of Props 1.2 (iii), 1.3 (iii).
explicit_hypotheses: a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,m HT}_{n,m∈Z} relative to the given initial Θ-data, arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Def 3.8 (iii))
IUT3.Prop3_9.iv.conclusion: For a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice: (a) the log-volumes of (i), (ii), (iii) determine log-volumes on the I^Q((−)) appearing in the local/global LGP-, lgp-monoids and Frobenioids of the F^⊩-prime-strips n,m 𝔉^⊩_LGP, n,m 𝔉^⊩_lgp relative to the log-link n,m−1 HT → n,m HT; (b) at the level of Q-spans of log-shells, the log-volumes indexed by (n,m) are compatible with those indexed by (n,m−1) relative to that log-link.

IUT3.Rem3_9_1.content: Explicit descriptions in the spirit of Remark 3.1.1 (i). (i) For v_Q ∈ V^non_Q, let v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} be the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i} with ring of integers O_{k_i}, and I_i := (p*_{v_Q})^{-1}·log_{k_i}(O^×_{k_i}) ⊆ k_i, where p*_{v_Q} = p_v if p_{v_Q} is odd and p*_{v_Q} = p^2_{v_Q} if p_{v_Q} is even (Remark 1.2.2 (i)). Roughly, the mono-analytic integral structures of Proposition 3.2 (ii) in I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊕_i k_i and I^Q(AF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊗_{α∈A} I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) are I(αF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊕_i I_i and I(AF_{v_Q}) ≅ ⊗_{α∈A} I(αF_{v_Q}), while the local holomorphic integral structures O_{αF_{v_Q}}, O_{AF_{v_Q}} of Proposition 3.9 (i) are the subrings of integers of these direct sums of finite extensions of Q_{p_{v_Q}}; by the formula of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (iii), for the log-volume of I_i, '[one verifies easily that]' the log-volumes μ^log_{α,v_Q}(I(αF_{v_Q})) and μ^log_{A,v_Q}(I(AF_{v_Q})) can be computed entirely in terms of the initial Θ-data (details left to the reader). (ii) For v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q, with v_i, k_i as before, O_{k_i} := {λ ∈ k_i : |λ| ≤ 1} and I_i := π·O_{k_i} (Remark 1.2.2 (ii)), the discrepancy between the mono-analytic integral structures of Proposition 3.2 (ii), determined by I(†F_{v_i}) ≅ I_i ⊆ k_i, and the local holomorphic integral structures of Proposition 3.9 (i), in the topological rings I^Q(αF_{v_Q}), I^Q(AF_{v_Q}) (direct sums of complex archimedean fields), determined by taking the product of the respective sets of integers, may be computed entirely in terms of the initial Θ-data by two '[easily verified]' observations: (a) with the standard Hermitian metric on C, the tensor product metric on C ⊗_R C and the direct sum metric on C ⊕ C, any isomorphism of topological rings C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C (from the Chinese remainder theorem) is compatible with the metrics up to a factor of 2 (the metric on the right corresponds to 2 times the metric on the left); (b) the decomposition C ⊕ C with its Hermitian metric is preserved, relative to that isomorphism, by complex conjugation on either factor of C ⊗_R C and by multiplication by ±1 or ±√−1 via either factor; details left to the reader. (iii) The discrepancy between local holomorphic and mono-analytic integral structures is discussed further in IUTchIV, §1.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Proposition 3.9 (i) and Proposition 3.2 (ii)
for (i): v_Q ∈ V^non_Q, v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i}
for (ii): v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q, v_1, ..., v_{n_{v_Q}} the distinct elements of V over v_Q, k_i := K_{v_i}
IUT3.Rem3_9_1.conclusion: (i) At v_Q ∈ V^non_Q the mono-analytic integral structures are, roughly, ⊕_i I_i and its tensor powers, the holomorphic ones the rings of integers, and the log-volumes of the mono-analytic integral structures are computable from the initial Θ-data. (ii) At v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q the discrepancy between the two integral structures is computable from the initial Θ-data, using (a) C ⊗_R C ≅ C ⊕ C multiplies the metric by 2 and (b) the decomposition and metric are preserved by conjugations and by multiplication by ±1, ±√−1 on either factor.

Elementary and within reach of Mathlib.
Prove (ii) (b): invariance of the decomposition and metric under the listed operations.
Carry out the computation of (i) from AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.8 (iii); page 118 leaves 'the routine details to the reader', as does page 119 for (ii).

w ∈ V

IUT3.Rem3_9_3.content: Weights in the procession-normalization must be equal: for j' ≤ j1, j2 the same log-shell labeled j' occurs in capsules S^±_{j1+1} and S^±_{j2+1}, and compatibility with the inclusion morphisms of the procession forces equal weights.
IUT3.Rem3_9_3.conclusion: Only plain averages are compatible with the procession inclusions.
obligations: State precisely what compatibility with inclusion morphisms means for a weighted average, then prove that it forces equal weights.
ambiguities: The argument does not specify which quantity must be preserved under inclusions; the conclusion 'no choice but to assign the same weights' depends on that specification.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.content: Makes the log-link compatibility of log-volumes of Proposition 3.9 (iv) more explicit through 'realified semi-simplifications' Rss(M) of measure spaces: (i) the formalism Sub(M), Fn(M), ∫_M and Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0}, with restriction to ample compact subsets and products; (ii) why mere dilation of volumes by the log-link would leave log-volumes defined only modulo Z·log(λ); (iii) the nonarchimedean diagram k ⊇ O_k^× → log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k induces compatible R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of the Rss's, compatible with finite extensions; (iv) at bad v, the log-Kummer operations k ⇝ O_k^× × q^N ⇝ O_k^× ⇝ log_k(O_k^×) ⇝ k induce such isomorphisms without interference with q^N, which embeds N in R ∪ {−∞} by 1 ↦ −log(q); (v) extension to topological tensor products k_{i_A}; (vi) the archimedean analogue via |k| = k/O_k^×.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of Proposition 3.9 (iv)
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.conclusion: A reformulation, not a new result: log-link compatibility of log-volumes at v ∈ V^non (iii), at v ∈ V^bad in the log-Kummer setting (iv), for tensor packets (v) and at v ∈ V^arc (vi) is expressed as the existence of R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of realified semi-simplifications compatible with the normalized log-volume maps. Statements in the part records.
definitions_required: measure space in the sense of Remark 3.1.1 (iii)
obligations: See part records.
ambiguities: The remark offers 'one way to formulate' the compatibility (pages 123, 126); it does not assert that this formulation is equivalent to Proposition 3.9 (iv).

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.i.content: Realified semi-simplification of a measure space. For a measure space (M, μ_M): S ⊆ M is pre-ample if it is a relatively compact Borel set, ample if moreover μ_M(S) > 0, and (M, μ_M) is ample if it has an ample subset. Sub(M) is the set of pre-ample subsets; Fn(M) the Borel functions f: M → R_{≥0} with finite image and f^{-1}(R_{>0}) ∈ Sub(M), a monoid with R_{>0}-action containing Sub(M) via characteristic functions. Integration ∫_M: Fn(M) ↠ R_{≥0} is an R_{>0}-equivariant surjection, Rss(M) is the quotient set it determines, and ∫^Rss_M: Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0}.
explicit_hypotheses: (M, μ_M) an ample measure space in the sense of Remark 3.1.1 (iii)
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.i.conclusion: (a) ∫_M: Fn(M) → R_{≥0} is an R_{>0}-equivariant surjection restricting to S ↦ μ_M(S) on Sub(M), and induces an R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism of monoids ∫^Rss_M: Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0} with ∫_M = ∫^Rss_M ∘ FnRss_M; on Sub(M) the quotient identifies S₁, S₂ with μ_M(S₁) = μ_M(S₂) and sends a disjoint union to the sum. (b) If S ∈ Sub(M) is ample and compact, (S, μ_M|_S) is ample, extension by zero gives inclusions Sub(S) ⊆ Sub(M), Fn(S) ⊆ Fn(M), and there are R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(S) ≅ R_{≥0}·Rss(Fn(S)) ≅ Rss(M) compatible with ∫^Rss_S and ∫^Rss_M. (c) For ample (M₁, μ₁), (M₂, μ₂) the product is ample, and (S₁, S₂) ↦ S₁ × S₂ induces an R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism Rss(M₁) ⊗ Rss(M₂) ≅ Rss(M₁ × M₂) compatible with ∫^Rss_{M₁} ⊗ ∫^Rss_{M₂} and ∫^Rss_{M₁×M₂}, where a tensor product of monoids isomorphic to R_{≥0} is defined via groupification as a one-dimensional R-vector space with a R_{>0}-torsor of positive elements.
definitions_required: pre-ample, ample subset; ample measure space
tensor product of monoids isomorphic to R_{≥0}
obligations: Elementary measure theory within reach of Mathlib: define Fn(M) as simple functions with relatively compact support, prove that integration is an R_{>0}-equivariant monoid surjection onto R_{≥0} (surjectivity uses an ample subset and scaling), so the quotient by the fibers of ∫ is canonically R_{≥0}; prove the product statement from the product measure.
ambiguities: Rss(M) is the quotient by the fibers of ∫_M, so the isomorphism Rss(M) ≅ R_{≥0} holds by construction once ∫_M is surjective; the content of the formalism is the bookkeeping of R_{>0}-equivariance and compatibilities, not a nontrivial theorem.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.ii.content: A very rough heuristic: if one knew only that each application of the log-link dilates volumes by a factor λ ∈ R_{>0} \ {1}, then log-volumes consistent with all arrows of the log-Kummer correspondence would be well defined only in R/Z·log(λ) ≅ S¹, which is unacceptable for the log-volume estimates of Corollary 3.12. Example: on (Q_p, μ_{Q_p}) with μ(Z_p) = 1, multiplication by p induces bijections Sub(α_p), Fn(α_p), Rss(α_p), and Rss(α_p) is compatible with ∫^Rss_{Q_p} on both sides only up to the factor p^{-1}.
explicit_hypotheses: for the example: a prime p, M = Q_p with additive Haar measure normalized by μ(Z_p) = 1
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.ii.conclusion: (a) Multiplication by p on Q_p scales Haar measure by p^{-1}, so Rss(α_p) is not compatible with ∫^Rss_{Q_p} on domain and codomain, only up to the factor p^{-1} ≠ 1. (b) Heuristic: under a dilation by λ ≠ 1 per log-link, consistently computed log-volumes would lie in R/Z·log(λ).
obligations: (a) is the standard scaling property of Haar measure on Q_p under multiplication by p (whether Mathlib states it in this form was not checked); (b) is a heuristic with no claim to prove.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.iii.content: Nonarchimedean formulation of log-link compatibility via Rss, and compatibility with finite extensions.
explicit_hypotheses: k as in Remark 1.2.2 (i) (a finite extension of Q_{p_v}), with additive Haar measure μ_k normalized by μ_k(O_k) = 1
for the extension statement: finite extensions k₁ ⊆ k₂ of Q_{p_v}
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.iii.conclusion: (a) (k, μ_k) is ample and O_k^× ⊆ k is ample; for any compact ample S ⊆ O_k^× on which log_k is injective, μ_k(S) = μ_k(log_k(S)) (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7 (i), (c)); such S exist. (b) Hence the diagram k ⊇ O_k^× → log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k induces a commutative diagram of R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(k) ← Rss(O_k^×) ← Rss(S) → Rss(log_k(S)) → Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) → Rss(k) over R_{≥0}, the composite Rss(O_k^×) ≅ Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) being independent of S; composing with log: R_{≥0} ≅ R ∪ {−∞} and a normalization factor, these isomorphisms are compatible with the log-volume maps. (c) Since O_{k₂} is free of rank [k₂ : k₁] over O_{k₁} and Haar measure is invariant under automorphisms, k₁ ⊆ k₂ induces Rss(k₁)^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} ≅ Rss(O_{k₁})^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} ≅ Rss(O_{k₂}) ≅ Rss(k₂), compatible with (∫^Rss_{k₁})^{⊗[k₂:k₁]} and ∫^Rss_{k₂}.
definitions_required: log_k: O_k^× → k, the p-adic logarithm
obligations: Prove that the p-adic logarithm preserves Haar measure on compact subsets of O_k^× where it is injective (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7 (i), (c)); the p-adic logarithm on a general finite extension of Q_p is not assumed to be in Mathlib.
Prove the existence of compact ample S ⊆ O_k^× on which log_k is injective, and independence of the composite isomorphism from S ('easily verified', page 123).
Prove the finite extension statement from O_{k₂} ≅ O_{k₁}^{[k₂:k₁]} as compact groups.
ambiguities: The 'suitable normalization factor' (page 123) is not specified.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.iv.content: Log-volume compatibility in the log-Kummer correspondence at bad places.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of (iii), v ∈ V^bad, q := q_v
the submonoid O_k^× × q^N ⊆ k of the multiplicative monoid of k
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.iv.conclusion: The arrows of the log-Kummer correspondence of Proposition 3.5 (ii), seen from a vertically coric copy of k labeled (n,◦), correspond to the operations k ⇝ O_k^× × q^N ⇝ O_k^× ⇝ log_k(O_k^×) ⇝ k, and log-volume compatibility in this context is the statement that these operations induce R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(k) ≅ Rss(O_k^×) ≅ Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) ≅ Rss(k) compatible with the normalized log-volume maps to R ∪ {−∞}, avoiding any interference, up to multiplication by roots of unity, with q^N ⊆ k; the latter gives, via the log-volume of the images q^n·O_k, an embedding N ↪ Rss(k) ≅ R ∪ {−∞} with 1 ↦ −log(q), where log(q) := ord_v(q_v)·log(p_v). For v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non the same holds omitting q.
obligations: Compute the normalized log-volume of q^n·O_k as −n·log(q) (elementary once the normalization of (iii) is fixed).
Make 'avoid any interference, up to multiplication by roots of unity' precise: the operations restricted to O_k^× do not involve q^N.
ambiguities: 'Avoid any interference' (page 124) is not defined; reading it as 'the isomorphisms are defined using only the unit portion O_k^×, which meets q^N only in roots of unity' is an interpretation.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.v.content: Extension to topological tensor products k_{i_A} = ⊗_{α ∈ A} k_{i_α} (notation of Remark 3.9.1 (i)), with Haar measure normalized so that O_{k_{i_A}} has measure 1.

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.v.conclusion: Each direct summand field of k_{i_A} is a finite extension of a k as in (iii), (iv), so k_{i_A} is a product measure space and (iii), (iv) extend factor by factor (routine details left to the reader). Moreover, for each α ∈ A the k_{i_α}-algebra structure gives R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(Q_{p_v})^{⊗d_A} ≅ Rss(k_{i_α})^{⊗d_α} ≅ Rss(k_{i_A}), with d_α := ∏_{β ∈ A∖{α}} [k_{i_β} : Q_{p_v}] and d_A := d_α·[k_{i_α} : Q_{p_v}]; so log-link compatibility for Rss(k_{i_A}) is the functorially induced d_α-th tensor power of that for Rss(k_{i_α}), or equivalently the d_A-th tensor power of that for Rss(Q_{p_v}), the latter independent of α.
obligations: Carry out the factor-by-factor extension of (iii), (iv) to k_{i_A}; the text leaves the routine details to the reader (page 125).
Check the degree bookkeeping: k_{i_A} has dimension d_A over Q_{p_v} and dimension d_α over k_{i_α}.
ambiguities: Routine details left to the reader (page 125).

IUT3.Rem3_9_4.vi.content: Archimedean formulation: k a complex archimedean field with the standard Euclidean metric (O_k^× of length 2π), measures μ_{|k|} on |k| := k/O_k^× and μ_{O_k^×} on O_k^×; approximating O_k^× by small closed arcs, translating them to 0 and projecting to |k|, in the limit ε → 0, gives an R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism ρ_k: Rss(O_k^×) ≅ Rss(|k|).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Remark 1.2.2 (ii): a complex archimedean field k with the standard Euclidean metric
log_k(O_k^×) := exp_k^{-1}(O_k^×) with the measure pulled back from μ_{|k|} via the homeomorphism log_k(O_k^×) ≅ |k|
IUT3.Rem3_9_4.vi.conclusion: (|k|, μ_{|k|}), (O_k^×, μ_{O_k^×}) and (log_k(O_k^×), μ) are ample, and there is a commutative diagram of R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(|k|) ← Rss(O_k^×) ← Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) → Rss(|k|) over R_{≥0}, the first being ρ_k, the second induced by the universal covering exp_k on ample subsets mapped bijectively (AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7 (ii), (c)), the third by the homeomorphism log_k(O_k^×) ≅ |k|. Composing with log and a normalization factor, the diagram |k| ← k ⊇ O_k^× ← log_k(O_k^×) ⊆ k ↠ |k| induces R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphisms of the Rss's of |k|, O_k^×, log_k(O_k^×), |k|, each compatible with the log-volume maps restricting to the radial/angular log-volume maps of AbsTopIII, Proposition 5.7 (ii), (a). Analogues of (iv), (v) hold for v ∈ V^arc (routine details left to the reader).
obligations: Define ρ_k precisely (the limit ε → 0 of the arc construction) and prove that it is a well-defined R_{>0}-equivariant isomorphism ('one verifies immediately', page 126).
The archimedean analogues of (iv), (v) are left to the reader (page 126).
ambiguities: The construction of ρ_k by steps (a) to (d) with a limit ε → 0 (pages 125 to 126) is described procedurally; the limit and its independence of choices are not argued.
The 'suitable normalization factor' (page 126) is not specified.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.content: Holomorphic hulls of regions (pages 126 to 145), in ten parts: (i) definition of the holomorphic hull of a region of I^Q(−) containing a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume; (ii) ℙ (direct product regions), ℍ (hulls) and the hull map φ : ℙ → ℍ, characterized by (P1) φ(H) = H, (P2) P ⊆ φ(P), (P3) monotonicity, with φ(P) = ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P} H; (iii) hull-approximants Φ(P) ⊇ Ξ(P) and H_{Φ(P)}, H_{Ξ(P)}, a compact indeterminacy; (iv) φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)}, conditions (Ξ1), (Ξ2) for Ξ(P) ≠ ∅, strictness (Ξ3) and the example I = Q_p × Q_p; (v) the set-theoretic quotient E ⊼ S as a formalization of upper semi-commutativity; (vi) its application to S = φ(P) and to bounded families P_B; (vii) the obstructions (Ob1) to (Ob9) to comparing the output of the multiradial algorithms with the q-pilot object and their elimination via hulls, det_{⊗M}(−), the ⊼-formalism and the log-Kummer correspondence; (viii) to (x) the (sub)quotient operations (sQ1) to (sQ5), the compatibilities (cQ3), (cQ4) versus (iQ5), the 'closed loop', and why hulls and arithmetic line bundles over F_mod cannot be replaced by categories of regions or by line bundles over Q.

regions of I^Q(αF_{v_Q}), I^Q(AF_{v_Q}), I^Q(A,αF_v) as in Remark 3.1.1 (iii), (iv) and Remark 3.9.4
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.conclusion: Definitions: the holomorphic hull (i), the hull map φ : ℙ → ℍ with φ(P) = ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P} H (ii), the hull-approximants Φ(P), Ξ(P) (iii), the quotient E ⊼ S (v). Assertions: the hull is well defined (i); φ is uniquely characterized by (P1) to (P3) and any intersection of elements of ℍ of finite log-volume lies in ℍ (ii); φ(P) ∈ Φ(P), φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)}, Ξ(P) ≠ ∅ under (Ξ1) or globally (Ξ2), and μ^log(P) < μ^log(H_{Ξ(P)}) can occur (Ξ3) (iv); set maps between nonempty subsets of S induce identities on ⊼_S (v); H_1 ~ H_2 ⟺ H_1, H_2 ⊆ φ(P) under the quotient by φ(P) (vi). Parts (vii) to (x) are interpretive; see the part records.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i.content: For a subset U of I^Q(−) that contains a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume: if U is relatively compact, its holomorphic hull is the smallest subset λ·O (λ with every component nonzero in the direct sum decomposition) containing U; otherwise the hull is all of I^Q(−). 'One verifies immediately that the holomorphic hull is well-defined.'

a subset U of I^Q(αF_{v_Q}) (respectively I^Q(AF_{v_Q}), I^Q(A,αF_v)) containing a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume (> −∞)

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii.content: ℙ = direct product regions in I^Q(−) (Rem 3.1.1 (iii)); ℍ = hulls H ⊊ I^Q(−); ℍ ⊆ ℙ. Forming the hull gives φ : ℙ → ℍ, 'characterized uniquely' by (P1) φ(H) = H for H ∈ ℍ, (P2) P ⊆ φ(P), (P3) P₁ ⊆ P₂ ⇒ φ(P₁) ⊆ φ(P₂). Since 'as is easily verified' any intersection of elements of ℍ which is of finite log-volume (the qualifier applies to the intersection) determines an element of ℍ, it 'follows formally' that φ(P) = ⋂_{ℍ∋H⊇P} H. φ is described as an adjoint of ℍ ⊆ ℙ, a canonical splitting, an integration operation (page 127).
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Rem 3.9.5 (i)
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii.conclusion: φ is the unique map ℙ → ℍ with (P1), (P2), (P3), and φ(P) = ⋂_{ℍ∋H⊇P} H for every P ∈ ℙ.
obligations: Prove the closure claim for actual hulls: an intersection of hulls which has finite log-volume is a hull ('as is easily verified', page 127).
Prove that the hull map of Rem 3.9.5 (i) satisfies (P1), (P2), (P3) and maps ℙ into ℍ ('essentially a tautology', page 127).
ambiguities: Assessment: the order-theoretic fragments show the formula follows from (P1), (P2), (P3), ℍ ⊆ ℙ and φ(ℙ) ⊆ ℍ without the closure claim; the closure claim is needed only for existence. The text presents it as the reason for the formula.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv.content: (iii) For P ∈ ℙ: Φ(P) := {H ∈ ℍ : φ(P) ⊇ H, (μ^log(φ(P)) ≥) μ^log(H) ≥ μ^log(P)}, Ξ(P) := {H ∈ ℍ : φ(P) ⊇ H, μ^log(H) = μ^log(P)} ⊆ Φ(P), H_{Φ(P)} := ⋃_{H∈Φ(P)} H ⊆ φ(P), H_{Ξ(P)} := ⋃_{H∈Ξ(P)} H ⊆ H_{Φ(P)}: 'log-volume approximations' of P by hulls; the indeterminacy of choosing an element is compact (all choices lie in φ(P)), which would fail without the condition H ⊆ φ(P). (iv) φ(P) ∈ Φ(P), so φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)}; '(Ξ1) it is easily verified that Ξ(P) ≠ ∅' if either (Ξ^non1) every valuation of the Galois closure K^cl of K over Q dividing v_Q ∈ V^non_Q has residue field extension degree 1 and μ^log(P) = μ^log(Q) for some Q ∈ ℙ that is a Z_{p_{v_Q}}-submodule of I^Q((−)), or (Ξ^arc1) v_Q ∈ V^arc_Q; (Ξ2) letting v_Q vary in global situations (Proposition 3.9 (iii)), the global analogue of Ξ(P) is 'easily verified' to be nonempty; in general it is not clear whether Ξ(P) ≠ ∅. If P ∈ ℍ then {φ(P)} = Φ(P) = Ξ(P) and P = φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)} = H_{Ξ(P)}, but in general P ⊆ φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)} and μ^log(P) ≤ μ^log(φ(P)) are strict: (Ξ3) under (Ξ1), if (V_mod)_{v_Q} and A have cardinality ≥ 2, 'one verifies easily' that there exist P with μ^log(P) < μ^log(H_{Ξ(P)}). Example: I = Q_p × Q_p, H0 = Z_p × Z_p, H1 = p^{-1}Z_p × pZ_p, P = H0 ∪ ({p^{-1}} × Z_p), H_P = p^{-1}Z_p × Z_p; μ_I(P) = μ_I(H0) = 1 < 2 − p^{-1} = μ_I(H0 ∪ H1); 'one verifies immediately' that H_P corresponds to φ(P) = H_{Φ(P)} and to H_{Ξ(P)}.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i and IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv.conclusion: Strictness of the inequality μ^log(P) < μ^log(φ(P)) in examples.
obligations: Verify the example: μ(H1) = p·p^{-1} = 1, μ(H0 ∩ H1) = μ(Z_p × pZ_p) = p^{-1}, so μ(H0 ∪ H1) = 2 − p^{-1}; μ({p^{-1}} × Z_p) = 0.
Prove (Ξ1) under (Ξ^non1) or (Ξ^arc1), (Ξ2) and (Ξ3) (pages 128 to 129: 'easily verified'; no argument is given).
Prove in the example that H_P is both φ(P) and H_{Ξ(P)} (page 129: 'one verifies immediately', by translates of H0, H1 by automorphisms of the Z_p-module H_P).
ambiguities: Page 128: in (Ξ^non1) the quantifier over Q ∈ ℙ and the role of the residue degree condition are stated without proof of why they suffice.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vii.content: Why the hull plays a crucial role in Corollary 3.12: the output of possible images of the multiradial algorithms of Theorem 3.11 cannot be directly compared, in any a priori sense, with the objects of the local and global Frobenioids in the codomain F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link determined by the arithmetic line bundle giving rise to the q-pilot object (Definition 3.8 (i), (ii); IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)). The obstructions and how they are eliminated: (Ob1) O^×-indeterminacies on tensor packets of log-shells: the possible images are regions (elements of ℙ) in tensor packets of log-shells I_k (notation of Remark 1.2.2 (i), nonarchimedean), whereas the q-pilot line bundle is locally an ideal in the O_k-module O^mdl_k, which, unlike the ring O_k, has no canonical generator, only one up to multiplication by O^×_k, which does not stabilize I_k. (Ob2) Passing from a region P to its hull φ(P) ∈ ℍ gives a region stabilized by O^×_k that defines the local portion of a global arithmetic vector bundle relative to the ring structure labeled by some α ∈ A (typically the zero label 0 ∈ |F_l| when 0 ∈ A). (Ob3) Taking the determinant of the arithmetic vector bundle given by a hull yields an arithmetic line bundle, comparable with the q-pilot objects: (Ob3-1) weighted tensor powers/determinant: (Ob3-1-1) to be consistent with log-volumes as weighted sums (Remark 3.1.1), one takes suitable positive tensor powers, given by the weights (products of the N_v of Remark 3.1.1 (iv)), of the determinant line bundles of the direct summands of the tensor packet, and (Ob3-1-2) one tensors with the inverse of the 'determinant' of the structure sheaf O_(−) of Proposition 3.9 (i), an adjustment for ramification (routine details left to the reader); (Ob3-2) the exponents need not be relatively prime, so the operation is a 'determinant raised to some positive tensor power', written det_{⊗M}(−), with M the uniquely determined positive integer (cf. N_E of Remark 3.1.1 (iv)) such that det_{⊗M}(−) maps the result of tensoring O_(−) (Proposition 3.9 (i)) with an arithmetic line bundle to the M-th tensor power of that arithmetic line bundle; taking M sufficiently divisible one may assume the localization at each v ∈ V of any output of det_{⊗M}(−) is trivial (stack-theoretic twists at v ∈ V^bad, IUTchI, Remark 3.1.5); (Ob3-3) since the arithmetic degree of the output may be read, with suitable normalization factors, as the log-volume of the original arithmetic vector bundle, the step det_{⊗M}(−) may be omitted when only log-volumes are computed. (Ob4) Hence det_{⊗M}(−) yields objects comparable with the M-th tensor power of the q-pilot object; this 'slightly modified goal' causes no substantive problem (no indeterminacy confusing a line bundle with its M-th power, unlike I^ord in Remark 2.3.3 (vi)), because: (Ob4-1) the tensor-power Frobenioids are copies of the non-tensor-power ones via the naive Frobenius functor of degree M ([FrdI], Proposition 2.1 (i)), which determine them completely; (Ob4-2) conversely, extracting M-th roots determines the non-tensor-power Frobenioids only up to twists, since the rational function monoids ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (ii)) of the local Frobenioids are not divisible at v ∈ V^non; (Ob4-3) these 'tensor-power-twist indeterminacies' have no substantive effect on log-volume estimates (Ob3-3). (Ob5) Selecting a specific element of the collection of possible regions is internal to the algorithm; comparison with external objects such as the q-pilot line bundle requires independence of that choice, achieved by working with the hull φ(P_B) of the bounded collection P_B = {P_β}_{β∈B} of possible regions output by the algorithm and the ⊼-formalism of (v), (vi); the ⊼-formalism applies also, compatibly, to det_{⊗M}(φ(P_B)) and μ^log(φ(P_B)). (Ob6) Replacing P by μ^log(P) is tempting, but comparability with the q-pilot object forces hulls; Ξ(P) may be empty (iv), so Φ(P) is more natural, and independence of the choice (Ob5) forces μ^log(H_{Φ(P)}) or μ^log(H_{Ξ(P)}) in place of μ^log(P), which may be > μ^log(P) and indeed = μ^log(φ(P)) (iv). (Ob7) Why log-volumes cannot be the 'ultimate stage for comparison', i.e. why the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion (for v ∈ V^non, the local Galois groups G_v and units O^{×μ}_{F_v}, with their auxiliary structures, IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (i), (v), (vii)) cannot be eliminated from the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link: (Ob7-1) the G_v are invariant up to isomorphism under the Θ^{×μ}_LGP- and log-links (vertical and horizontal coricity, Theorem 1.5 (i), (ii)), which the theory needs; (Ob7-2) eliminating only the Frobenius-like units, i.e. using F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips (Definition 2.4 (iii)), fails because the Frobenius-like units in the link are related only to those at the same vertical coordinate, consistently with the ring structure of their Hodge theater, while their étale-like counterparts O^{×μ}(G_v) (IUTchII, Example 1.8 (iv)) are related by vertical coricity and the log-Kummer correspondences to the Frobenius-like units at every vertical coordinate, subject to arbitrary iterates of the log-link and a complicated confusion of unit group and value group portions; using étale-like units as the sole access route would make the data of the F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips 'over-constrained/over-determined'. So one cannot eliminate the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion; its inclusion underlies the log-Kummer correspondences and log-shells as multiradial containers. (Ob8) The output of the multiradial algorithms, even with hulls, yields a priori objects that differ from the corresponding multiplicative local and global Frobenioids of the input data by a vertical shift (an application of the log-link, which produces additive log-shells from the multiplicative O^{×μ}); applying the log-Kummer correspondence gives objects meaningfully comparable with the input data (Step (xi-d) of the proof of Corollary 3.12), but these belong to Frobenioids subject to the indeterminacies of arbitrary iterates of the log-link (Remark 3.12.2 (v)). (Ob9) Passing to realified semi-simplifications (Remark 3.9.4 (iii) to (vi)) in log-link compatibility of log-volumes is a quotient operation inducing a natural bijection between log-volumes of hulls in domain and codomain of the log-link, unaffected by the use of non-hull regions at intermediate steps, because: (Ob9-1) once comparable objects are obtained via det_{⊗M}(−) of a hull, the formal indeterminacies arising (the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies of (Ob4-3), the ⊼-formalism of (Ob5), the arbitrary iterates of the log-link of (Ob8)) do not affect comparability and act only as compatibility conditions for passing to coarse invariants such as the log-volume; (Ob9-2) by contrast, in (Ob1) to (Ob5) comparable objects had not yet been obtained, so the relation between the non-comparable output and comparable objects had not been explicitly computed. Related issues are discussed in (ix).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i to IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vi: ℙ, ℍ, φ, Φ(P), Ξ(P), the ⊼-formalism
the multiradial algorithms of Theorem 3.11 and the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link of Definition 3.8 (ii), in the context of Corollary 3.12
for (Ob1): the notational conventions of Remark 1.2.2 (i), at nonarchimedean valuations
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vii.conclusion: Interpretation: the output of the multiradial algorithms becomes comparable with the q-pilot object (more precisely, with its M-th tensor power) only after passing to the hull of the bounded family of possible regions, taking det_{⊗M}(−), applying the ⊼-formalism and relating vertical coordinates by the log-Kummer correspondence; for log-volume computations the step det_{⊗M}(−) may be omitted, and the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies, the ⊼-formalism and log-link iterates do not affect comparability; the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion cannot be removed from the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link.
obligations: Make precise det_{⊗M}(−) for a hull (the weighted tensor powers of (Ob3-1) and the correction of (Ob3-2), whose routine details page 132 leaves to the reader) and prove (Ob3-3): its arithmetic degree equals, after the stated normalization, the log-volume of the original arithmetic vector bundle; the normalization factor is not written as a formula.

Prove (Ob4-1), (Ob4-2): the naive Frobenius functor of degree M determines the tensor-power Frobenioids, and M-th roots determine the non-tensor-power Frobenioids only up to twists (cited from [FrdI]).
State and prove that the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies of (Ob4-3) leave log-volumes unchanged (page 134 asserts they have 'no substantive effect').

Prove (Ob9): the passage to realified semi-simplifications induces a natural bijection between log-volumes of hulls in the domain and codomain of the log-link (asserted on page 138 with reference to Remark 3.9.4).
ambiguities: Page 132: M is called 'uniquely determined' while also being allowed to be taken 'sufficiently large' and 'sufficiently divisible'; the two uses are not reconciled in the text.

Page 133, (Ob4): the claim that comparing with the M-th tensor power of the q-pilot object does not result in 'any substantive problems' is supported by the interpretations (Ob4-1) to (Ob4-3), not by a proof.
Pages 136 to 137, (Ob7-2): 'over-constrained/over-determined' is not given a formal meaning.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.viii_x.content: (viii) Like (sQ1) Kummer-detachment (Remark 1.5.4 (i); vertical arrows of Remark 3.10.2) and (sQ2) Galois evaluation (IUTchII, Remark 1.12.4; horizontal arrows of Remark 3.10.2), the operations (sQ3) passing from general regions to positive tensor powers of determinants of hulls and applying the ⊼-formalism, (sQ4) adjusting vertical shifts in the output by the log-Kummer correspondence (Ob8), and (sQ5) passing to log-volumes via realified semi-simplifications (Remark 3.9.4) are intricate (sub)quotient (or push forward, splitting, integration) operations. The theory may be regarded as a collection of (sub)quotient operation algorithms producing a relatively simple concrete (sub)quotient of the log-theta-lattice, whose goal is the computation of the projection of the 'Θ-intertwining' (the structure on an abstract F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip as arising from the Θ-pilot object in the domain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link) onto structures from the vertical column in the codomain, where the 'q-intertwining' (as arising from the q-pilot object in the codomain) is in force; this computation, 'when suitably interpreted, amounts, essentially tautologically, to the inequality of Corollary 3.12'. Each operation simplifies by introducing indeterminacies, balancing minimal indeterminacy against compatibility with prior structures (discussed for (sQ1) in Remarks 1.5.4, 2.1.1, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.3, 3.10.1 (ii), (iii); (sQ2) in IUTchII, Remark 1.12.4; (sQ3) in (Ob1) to (Ob7); (sQ4) in (Ob8); (sQ5) in Remark 3.9.4 and (Ob9)). (ix) Fundamental qualitative difference: (cQ3) hulls are stabilized by O_k, so det_{⊗M}(φ(P_B)) gives objects of the local and global Frobenioids in the codomain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link, and pull-back morphisms ([FrdI], Definition 1.3 (i)) give objects with natural faithful actions of G_v and O^{×μ}_{F_v}, i.e. the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip data; the quotient on ℍ induced by the ⊼-formalism corresponds to a '⊼-category' whose objects (⊼^lc_1) are objects of the local Frobenioid with a structure poly-morphism to det_{⊗M}(φ(P_B)) (the Aut(det_{⊗M}(φ(P_B)))-orbit of a linear morphism, [FrdI], Definition 1.2 (i)) and whose morphisms (⊼^lc_2) are compatible with it (optionally restricted to hull-approximants as in (Ob6)); categories of local-global ⊼-collections (⊼^lc-gl_1, ⊼^lc-gl_2, ⊼^lc-gl_3: local objects at each v ∈ V, a global object in the global realified Frobenioid, localization isomorphisms; cf. [FrdII], Example 5.6 (iii), (iv)) give, with the analogous category of local-global collections (⊼^fQ_2), a 'formal, or stack-theoretic, quotient' ⊼^fQ_2 modulo ⊼^fQ_1, like the tensor-power-twist indeterminacies (Ob4-3) and log-link iterates (Ob8), as opposed to coarse quotients such as the log-volume. (cQ4) The adjustment of vertical shifts, obtained by the log-Kummer correspondence, is tautologically compatible (vertical coricity, Theorem 1.5 (i)) with suitable isomorphisms between G_v and the étale-like units O^{×μ}(G_v), or, allowing arbitrary log-link iterates, with the Frobenius-like units O^{×μ}_{F_v}. (iQ5) By contrast, passing to log-volumes forgets G_v and the Frobenius-like units, i.e. the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion. (cQ3), (cQ4) are a kind of arithmetic holomorphicity (whence 'holomorphic hull'), (iQ5) forgets it. Consequence: precisely by passing through (sQ3), (sQ4) before (sQ5), the chain of poly-isomorphisms of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips that starts at the q-pilot F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip in the codomain, passes through the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link to the domain, through the poly-isomorphisms induced by (sQ1), (sQ2) (Remark 3.10.2; 'IPL' in Remark 3.11.1 (iii)), and through (sQ3), (sQ4), forms a closed loop up to the formal quotient indeterminacies of (cQ3), (cQ4) (Ob9-1); a non-closed loop would allow no nontrivial conclusions, as for the 'distinct labels approach' of Remark 3.11.1 (vii) (Ob9-2; Remark 3.12.2 (ii), (c^itw), (c^toy)). The closed loop completes the computation of the Θ-intertwining, up to indeterminacies, on an F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip constrained to be subject to the q-intertwining; by (Ob7) this cannot be done if subportions of the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip portion are omitted; this computation yields in Corollary 3.12 nontrivial, 'albeit essentially tautological', consequences such as its inequality (Substeps (xi-d) to (xi-g); Fig. 3.8); skipping (sQ3) or (sQ4) breaks the closed loop. (x) It is not possible, at least in any immediate sense, to avoid hulls by replacing the local and global Frobenioids of an F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip (IUTchII, Definition 4.9 (viii)) by more general categories of regions ∈ ℙ: such categories involve the multi-dimensional space I^Q((−)), an additive module of rank > 1, whose lines can only be related via its additive structure, whereas the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link is not compatible with additive structures, so the glued categories must be purely multiplicative, i.e. arithmetic line bundles (definable from multiplicative structures, unlike vector bundles of rank > 1); cf. (Ob1) to (Ob4). Working instead with arithmetic line bundles over Q amounts to a norm or determinant operation from F_mod to Q, or at v ∈ V^bad from K_v to Q_{p_v}, followed by a ramification correction (Ob3-1-2); 'one verifies immediately' that, since G_{p_v} ⊆ Gal(F̄/Q), the decomposition group of p_v containing G_v, admits no splitting G_{p_v} ≅ G_v × (G_{p_v}/G_v), such a norm operation cannot be extended in any meaningful sense to a G_v-equivariant operation on algebraic closures of K_v and Q_{p_v}; as the faithful action of G_v on the unit portion of the local Frobenioids of an F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip is central (Ob7), a norm operation is unsuited to defining the gluings of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i to IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vii
the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link of Definition 3.8 (ii) and the commutative diagram of Remark 3.10.2
for (x): v ∈ V^bad, G_{p_v} ⊆ Gal(F̄/Q) the decomposition group of p_v containing G_v
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.viii_x.conclusion: Interpretation: (sQ1) to (sQ5) are (sub)quotient operations whose composite computes the projection of the Θ-intertwining onto the q-intertwining structure; (sQ3), (sQ4) are compatible with the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip data and (sQ5) is not, so applying (sQ3), (sQ4) before (sQ5) closes the loop of poly-isomorphisms up to formal quotient indeterminacies, which is presented as what yields the inequality of Corollary 3.12; hulls cannot be avoided by working with categories of regions, and norms down to Q are unsuited because G_{p_v} does not split as G_v × (G_{p_v}/G_v).
obligations: Define the subquotient operations (sQ1) to (sQ5) as maps between explicit sets or categories so that the 'closed loop' of page 143 becomes a checkable composite, and state precisely in what sense its existence implies the inequality of Corollary 3.12 (page 140 says the computation 'amounts, essentially tautologically' to it).

Prove the group-theoretic claim of page 145: G_{p_v} admits no splitting G_{p_v} ≅ G_v × (G_{p_v}/G_v) (the text writes 'one verifies immediately'; note G_v need not be normal in G_{p_v}, so the quotient G_{p_v}/G_v must be read as a coset space or the claim restricted), and the consequence that the norm from K_v to Q_{p_v} has no G_v-equivariant extension in any 'meaningful sense'.
Make precise the claim of (x) that a category of regions must use the additive structure of I^Q((−)) to relate its lines.
ambiguities: Page 140: 'when suitably interpreted' and 'essentially tautologically' are not explained further here.
Page 145: G_{p_v}/G_v is written as a factor of a product; G_v is a subgroup of the decomposition group G_{p_v}, not in general normal, so the meaning of the quotient is unclear.
Page 143: a 'non-closed loop' yielding 'no nontrivial conclusions' is an informal criterion.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.v.content: The 'upper' quotient: for a set E and a proper subset S ⊆ E of cardinality at least 2, E ⊼ S := (E \ S) ⊔ {S} is the quotient of E collapsing S to a point, with ⊼_S := {S} ⊆ E ⊼ S. Any set map S₁ → S₂ between nonempty subsets of S induces on the quotient the identity map of ⊼_S, lying over the identity of E ⊼ S. This extends to empty S_i treated as formal intersections (formal inverse systems over E of nonempty subsets of S), so 'formal empty sets' in S also map to ⊼_S. Proposed as an abstract set-theoretic formalization of upper semi-commutativity/semi-compatibility (Remarks 1.2.2 (iii), 1.5.4 (iii), Proposition 3.5 (ii)), with S ⊆ E taken to be I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)); there the empty set always arises as the intersection of a nonempty set with the domain of definition of a set-theoretic logarithm map.
explicit_hypotheses: E a set, S ⊆ E a proper subset of cardinality ≥ 2
S₁, S₂ ⊆ S nonempty subsets and a map S₁ → S₂ (or formal inverse systems of nonempty subsets of S, for the extension to empty S_i)
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.v.conclusion: Every set map S₁ → S₂ between nonempty subsets of S induces, after passing to E ↠ E ⊼ S, the identity map ⊼_S → ⊼_S (the images of S₁ and S₂ both equal ⊼_S), lying over the identity of E ⊼ S; the same holds for formal inverse systems, so formal empty subsets of S also map to ⊼_S.
definitions_required: formal inverse system (category-theoretic formal fiber product over E)
obligations: Elementary and within reach of Lean and Mathlib: define the quotient of E by the relation collapsing S (for example as a Quot by the relation x ~ y iff x = y or x, y ∈ S) and prove that the image of any nonempty subset of S is the single class of S, so that any map S₁ → S₂ descends to the identity on that class.
The extension to empty S_i via formal inverse systems needs a definition of 'formal intersection' before it can be stated.
ambiguities: The extension to empty S_i (page 130) is described informally ('treated as a formal intersection'); no definition of the formal inverse system is given.
The claim that this is a formalization of upper semi-commutativity (page 130) is interpretive; how the containments of Proposition 3.5 (ii) become maps S₁ → S₂ is not specified.

IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vi.content: Applies the ⊼-formalism of (v) with S ⊆ E taken to be φ(P) ⊆ I^Q((−)) for P ∈ ℙ, to identify P with its log-volume hull-approximants in Φ(P) or Ξ(P) (nonempty subsets of φ(P) ∈ ℍ), passing to a quotient in which the indeterminacy discussed in (iii) is eliminated; also for bounded families P_B = {P_β}_{β ∈ B} of elements of ℙ with relatively compact union, using φ(P_B) := ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P_β ∀β} H.
explicit_hypotheses: P ∈ ℙ (direct product regions), with hull φ(P) ∈ ℍ and hull-approximants Φ(P), Ξ(P) as in IUT3.Rem3_9_5.ii and IUT3.Rem3_9_5.iii_iv
for the family version: a collection P_B = {P_β}_{β ∈ B} ⊆ ℙ with ⋃_β P_β ⊆ I^Q((−)) relatively compact
implicit_hypotheses: φ(P) is a proper subset of I^Q((−)) of cardinality ≥ 2, as (v) requires; this holds since φ(P) ∈ ℍ consists of hulls H ⊊ I^Q((−)) with nonempty interior
IUT3.Rem3_9_5.vi.conclusion: Under the quotient map I^Q((−)) ↠ I^Q((−)) ⊼ φ(P), the images of H₁, H₂ ∈ ℍ coincide if and only if H₁, H₂ ⊆ φ(P); so the equivalence relation on ℍ induced by the quotient is H₁ ~ H₂ ⟺ H₁, H₂ ⊆ φ(P). The same applies to bounded families P_B with φ(P_B) := ⋂_{ℍ ∋ H ⊇ P_β for all β ∈ B} H.
obligations: State and prove the displayed equivalence. The 'if' direction is immediate from (v). The 'only if' direction is not a general fact about quotients: for arbitrary subsets H₁ ≠ H₂ of E that both meet φ(P) and agree outside φ(P), the images coincide. Assessment (drawing on the description of hulls in IUT3.Rem3_9_5.i, page 127, not re-read for this record): it should hold for hulls because a hull is a product over the direct summands of fractional ideals λ·O, and such a product not contained in φ(P) is determined by its part outside φ(P); a formalization must use this shape of hulls.
Prove that φ(P_B) is an element of ℍ for a bounded family (finite log-volume of the intersection), as in Remark 3.9.5 (ii).
ambiguities: Assessment: The 'only if' of the equivalence on page 130 depends on the specific form of hulls (products of fractional ideals λ·O, containing 0), not only on the ⊼-formalism of (v); the text says 'one verifies easily' and gives no argument.

IUT3.Rem3_9_7.content: Elementary observations on computing log-volumes of regions as in Proposition 3.9: (i) the condition 'zero log-volume for all but finitely many v_Q' can be met by taking, at all but finitely many nonarchimedean w_Q with p_{w_Q} unramified in K, the component I(A F_{w_Q}) ⊆ I^Q(A F_{w_Q}), which has zero log-volume, is a mono-analytic invariant and equals its own holomorphic hull; (ii) log-volumes of more general relatively compact E ⊆ I^Q((−)) may be defined as the infimum over E* ∈ M(I^Q((−))) containing E, possibly −∞, or essentially equivalently via the inverse system of such E* (of direct product regions when E is a direct product pre-region), which keeps log-volumes finite; (iii) the same for collections {E_{v_Q}} contained in collections {E*_{v_Q}} as in (i).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of Proposition 3.9 (i), (ii), (iii); for (i), w_Q ∈ V_Q^non with p_{w_Q} unramified in K
IUT3.Rem3_9_7.conclusion: (i) For each nonarchimedean w_Q with p_{w_Q} unramified in K, O_{(−)} = I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)) has zero log-volume, is a mono-analytic invariant, and equals its own holomorphic hull. (ii) and (iii) are definitions: log-volume of a relatively compact E (or a collection {E_{v_Q}}) as the infimum of log-volumes of admissible supersets, with value possibly −∞; essentially equivalent to working with the inverse system of such supersets.
obligations: Prove (i): for p_{w_Q} unramified in K, the subset I((−)) ⊆ I^Q((−)) has zero normalized log-volume and is its own holomorphic hull (the text cites Proposition 3.2 (ii), Proposition 3.9 (i) and the final sentence of AbsTopIII, Definition 5.4 (iii)).
Make 'essentially equivalently' in (ii), (iii) precise: the infimum of the inverse system's log-volumes equals the infimum definition.
ambiguities: 'Essentially equivalently' (pages 146, 147) is not explained; the inverse-system formulation keeps log-volumes finite while the infimum can be −∞, so the two are not literally the same.

IUT3.Prop3_10.content: Global Kummer theory and non-interference with local integers, for a collection of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters {n,mHT} arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, with n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} the D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater determined up to isomorphism by the vertical coricity of Theorem 1.5 (i): (i) vertically coric global LGP- and 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Frobenioids with Kummer isomorphisms; (ii) the global number field meets the product of local integral monoids only in roots of unity, and a log-Kummer correspondence invariant under vertical translation; (iii) log-link-compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD and of F^{⊩⊥}-prime-strips.
explicit_hypotheses: a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m ∈ Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters relative to the given initial Θ-data, thought of as arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii), Proposition 3.5, Remark 3.8.2)
for each n, n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} determined up to isomorphism via the vertical coricity of Theorem 1.5 (i)
implicit_hypotheses: the full log-links are taken compatibly with the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetries (Remark 1.3.2, Proposition 3.4 (ii))
IUT3.Prop3_10.conclusion: (i) functorial algorithms in n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} giving vertically coric number fields, monoids, Frobenioids and F^⊩-prime-strips, with Kummer isomorphisms from the corresponding objects of each n,mHT, compatible with the non-coric algorithms of Proposition 3.7; (ii) (†M^⊛_MOD)_α ∩ ∏_v Ψ_{log(A,αF_v)} = (†M^{⊛μ}_MOD)_α, the roots of unity, inside ∏_v I^Q(A,αF_v) = I^Q(A F_{V_Q}); and the actions of the groups (n,mM^⊛_MOD)_j on I^Q(S^±_{j+1}F(n,◦D_≻)_{V_Q}) via all pre-composites of Kummer isomorphisms with iterates of log-links are mutually compatible up to identity indeterminacies at adjacent m, giving a log-Kummer correspondence invariant under the vertical translation symmetries; (iii) isomorphisms (n,mF^⊛_MOD)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α, their realifications, and n,m𝔉^{⊩⊥}_LGP ≅ 𝔉^{⊩⊥}(n,◦HT^D)_LGP, all mutually compatible as m varies with the log-links. Statements in the part records.

IUT3.Prop3_10.i.content: Vertically coric global LGP- and 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Frobenioids and the associated Kummer theory.
explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Prop3_10
A ⊆ J as in Proposition 3.3
IUT3.Prop3_10.i.conclusion: Applying the constructions of Proposition 3.7 (i) to (iv) to the F-prime-strips F(n,◦D_≻)_t and their full log-links, compatibly with the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetries, gives functorial algorithms in n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} producing fields M̄^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡(n,◦HT^D)_α = M̄^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α ⊇ M^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡(…)_α = M^⊛_MOD(…)_α, M̄^⊛_mod(…)_α ⊇ M^⊛_mod(…)_α, Frobenioids F^⊛_mod(…)_α ≅ F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡(…)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(…)_α, and F^⊩-prime-strips F^⊩(…)_gau ≅ F^⊩(…)_LGP ≅ F^⊩(…)_𝔩𝔤𝔭 (vertically coric). For each n, m these algorithms are compatible with those of Proposition 3.7 (i) to (iv) (with † = (n,m), ‡ = (n,m−1)) relative to the Kummer isomorphisms Ψ_cns(n,m′F_≻)_t ≅ Ψ_cns(n,◦D_≻)_t and (n,m′M^⊛_mod)_j ≅ M^⊛_mod(n,◦D^⊚)_j, (n,m′M̄^⊛_mod)_j ≅ M̄^⊛_mod(n,◦D^⊚)_j for m′ = m, m−1, giving Kummer isomorphisms from the (n,m)-objects (fields, monoids, Frobenioids, F^⊩-prime-strips gau, LGP, 𝔩𝔤𝔭) to the vertically coric ones, compatible with the equalities, inclusions and isomorphisms above.
obligations: Formalize the global Kummer isomorphisms of IUTchII, Corollaries 4.6 to 4.8, and prove compatibility of the vertically coric constructions with the non-coric ones of Proposition 3.7.
ambiguities: 'Compatible in the evident sense' (page 147) is not spelled out.

IUT3.Prop3_10.ii.content: Non-interference with local integers, and the global log-Kummer correspondence.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Propositions 3.2 (ii), 3.4 (i), 3.7 (i), (ii), 3.9 (iii)
IUT3.Prop3_10.ii.conclusion: (a) (†M^⊛_MOD)_α ∩ ∏_{v ∈ V} Ψ_{log(A,αF_v)} = (†M^{⊛μ}_MOD)_α, the finite subgroup of roots of unity, the intersection taken in ∏_v I^Q(A,αF_v) = ∏_{v_Q} I^Q(A F_{v_Q}) = I^Q(A F_{V_Q}). (b) Regarding the groups (n,mM^⊛_MOD)_j as acting on portions of I^Q(S^±_{j+1}F(n,◦D_≻)_{V_Q}) not via a single Kummer isomorphism but via the totality of pre-composites of Kummer isomorphisms with iterates of the log-links of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, these actions are mutually compatible up to identity indeterminacies at an adjacent m, as a consequence of (a); this gives a log-Kummer correspondence between the totality over m ∈ Z of the groups labeled (n,m), with their actions, and I^Q labeled (n,◦), invariant under the translation symmetries of the n-th column (Proposition 1.3 (iv)).
external_dependencies: Lang: Algebraic Number Theory, page 144, proof of Theorem 5
obligations: (a) Identify ∏_v Ψ_{log(A,αF_v)} with the elements integral at every place (norm at most 1 at archimedean v) and apply Kronecker's theorem; Mathlib has NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_le_one (a nonzero algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have norm at most 1 is a root of unity), so (a) is within reach once the local monoids are modeled as unit balls of completions.

(b) Define 'mutually compatible up to identity indeterminacies at an adjacent m' and derive it from (a); the text gives only 'precisely as a consequence of' (a) with references to Remarks 1.2.3 (ii), 3.11.4 and Definition 1.1 (ii), (iv).
ambiguities: In (a), Ψ_{log(A,αF_v)} at archimedean v consists of elements of norm at most 1 (Definition 1.1 (ii)); the intersection is therefore with elements integral at all places in the sense of Lang, page 144, as the proof states (page 149).
In (b), 'identity indeterminacies' and the precise sense of compatibility are not defined; the claim is an assertion following from (a) without a written derivation.

explicit_hypotheses: the hypotheses of IUT3.Prop3_10
IUT3.Prop3_10.iii.conclusion: The Kummer isomorphisms of (i) induce, via the log-Kummer correspondence of (ii), isomorphisms of Frobenioids (n,mF^⊛_MOD)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α and (n,mF^⊛ℝ_MOD)_α ≅ F^⊛ℝ_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α that are mutually compatible, as m varies over Z, with the log-links of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice; together with the Kummer isomorphisms of (i), the global log-Kummer correspondence of (ii) and the splitting monoid portion of the log-Kummer correspondence of Proposition 3.5 (ii), they induce isomorphisms of F^{⊩⊥}-prime-strips n,m𝔉^{⊩⊥}_LGP ≅ 𝔉^{⊩⊥}(n,◦HT^D)_LGP, also mutually compatible as m varies with the log-links.
obligations: Define 'mutually compatible, as m varies, with the log-links' as a commutativity statement for the isomorphisms at m and m+1 with the log-link, and derive it from (ii); the text says only that the isomorphisms are induced via (ii).
ambiguities: Remark 3.10.1 (i) (pages 149 to 150) explains that such isomorphisms exist for F^⊛_MOD because its construction involves only the global group and subquotients of its perfection, but not for F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡, whose log-Kummer correspondence is only upper semi-compatible.

IUT3.Rem3_10_1.content: (i) The log-Kummer correspondence induces the isomorphisms of Proposition 3.10 (iii) for F^⊛_MOD because its construction uses only (†M^⊛_MOD)_α and subquotients of its perfection; F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡 uses local monoids subject only to the upper semi-compatible log-Kummer correspondence of Proposition 3.5 (ii), so no log-link-compatible isomorphisms of that kind exist for it. (ii) The precise compatibility of F^⊛_MOD makes it suited to Kummer-detachment indeterminacies (the mutual compatibility in Proposition 3.10 (iii) asserts in effect that they do not arise), which is why the LGP- rather than 𝔩𝔤𝔭-Gaussian lattice is used; its multiplicative nature makes it ill-suited to étale-transport indeterminacies. (iii) F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡, additive and closely related to coric mono-analytic log-shells, is suited to étale-transport indeterminacies; despite distortions one may compute (estimate) global arithmetic degrees of its objects via bi-coric log-volumes (Proposition 3.9), the topic of Corollary 3.12, with concrete estimates in IUTchIV. (iv) Fig. 3.2 summarizes; the isomorphisms F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡(n,◦HT^D)_α ≅ F^⊛_MOD(n,◦HT^D)_α and F^⊩(…)_LGP ≅ F^⊩(…)_𝔩𝔤𝔭 of Proposition 3.10 (i) relate the multiplicatively and additively biased Frobenioids via the global ring structure of the number field.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Prop3_10
IUT3.Rem3_10_1.conclusion: Interpretive. The only mathematical assertions are: (i) one cannot construct log-link-compatible isomorphisms of Frobenioids for (†F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡)_α as in Proposition 3.10 (iii) (page 150); (ii) the mutual compatibility of Proposition 3.10 (iii) amounts to the absence of Kummer-detachment indeterminacies for F^⊛_MOD/LGP-structures (page 150).
obligations: Make 'cannot construct log-link-compatible isomorphisms for F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡' a precise non-existence statement and prove it.
Define Kummer-detachment indeterminacy precisely enough to state that it 'does not arise'.
ambiguities: The impossibility claim in (i) (page 150) is argued from the imprecise nature of one-sided inclusions, not proved.
Fig. 3.2 (page 151) compares the two structures qualitatively ('rigid', 'subject to substantial distortion'); these are not mathematical statements.

IUT3.Rem3_10_2.content: The F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips †F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP, †F^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-, Θ^{×μ}_lgp-links (Definition 3.8 (ii)) were built from the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip †F^{⊩▶×μ}_env of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii). Working in the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Definition 3.8 (iii)), with '†' replaced by '(n, m)' or '(n, ◦)', there is a commutative diagram of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips: upper row F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_env ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_gau ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_LGP ≅ F^{⊩▶×μ}(n,◦)_lgp, lower row n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_gau ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp, with vertical arrows from lower to upper row. Here 'n,◦' abbreviates n,◦HT^{D-Θ^{±ell}NF} (Proposition 3.10 (i)); the first vertical arrow is the F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip version of the Kummer isomorphism of the final display of Proposition 2.1 (ii) (cf. Proposition 2.1 (iii), (iv), (v)); the second to fourth vertical arrows are those of the Kummer isomorphisms of the final display of Proposition 3.10 (i); the first lower horizontal arrow is the version of the evaluation isomorphism of the final display of IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (ii); the second and third lower horizontal arrows are the versions of the tautological isomorphisms of the final displays of Proposition 3.7 (iii), (iv); the first upper horizontal arrow is the version of the étale-like evaluation isomorphism implicit (via IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (iv), (v)) in the construction of that evaluation isomorphism; the second and third upper horizontal arrows are the versions of the natural isomorphisms of the second display of Proposition 3.10 (i). In summary, n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP and n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp were constructed from n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env and are related to it by the lower horizontal arrows, each of which may be constructed by conjugating the corresponding upper horizontal arrow by the Kummer isomorphisms (the vertical arrows).
explicit_hypotheses: the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice of Definition 3.8 (iii), with † replaced by (n, m) or (n, ◦)
the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 (ii) and Proposition 3.10 (i)
IUT3.Rem3_10_2.conclusion: The displayed diagram of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips commutes ('from the theory developed so far', page 152); hence n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP and n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_lgp are obtained from n,mF^{⊩▶×μ}_env via the lower horizontal arrows, each of which is the conjugate of the corresponding upper horizontal arrow by the vertical Kummer isomorphisms.
obligations: Prove commutativity of each square of the diagram on page 152 from the cited constructions; the text recalls it 'from the theory developed so far' and gives no argument.
Conjugating an upper horizontal arrow by the vertical arrows recovers the lower arrow: this is immediate once the squares commute and the vertical arrows are isomorphisms.
ambiguities: Page 152: the diagram mixes Frobenius-like (lower row, labeled n,m) and étale-like (upper row, labeled n,◦) data; the vertical arrows depend on m through the Kummer isomorphisms, which the notation does not show.
