IUT3.Rem3_11_1.content: Interpretation of Thm 3.11: (ii) the q-pilot could be replaced by q^λ; the codomain is coric. (iii) definitions of IPL (input prime-strip link) and SHE (simultaneous holomorphic expressibility); SHE corresponds to a closed loop of the subquotient operations of Rem 3.9.5. (iv) APT and HIS. (v) input/output summary. (vi) the naive tautological algorithm 'λ-th power of q' has SHE at the cost of sacrificing the analogue of IPL (page 164). (vii) distinct labels: IPL holds, while for SHE the diagram reads '??' (it is 'by no means clear' how to establish it); forced identification: SHE holds, while for IPL the diagram reads '??'; considering both assignments simultaneously and consistently makes q well defined only up to q^{λ^n}, n ∈ Z, a trivial multiradial representation {q^{λ^n}}_{n∈Z} that satisfies the formal analogues of both IPL and SHE (pages 164 to 165). (viii) the trivial representation is a toy model for IPL and SHE but useless for the log-volume estimates of Cor 3.12 (page 165).
IUT3.Rem3_11_1.conclusion: Definitions of the properties IPL, SHE, APT, HIS used in Cor 3.12 Step (xi).
obligations: Give IPL and SHE as precise properties of an algorithm (input type, output type, the relation to be preserved).
ambiguities: IPL and SHE are stated informally; their formal content (which map, which structure) is the main missing vocabulary for Cor 3.12.

IUT3.Rem3_11_2.content: (i) Theorem 3.11 (i) does not use the multiradiality formalism of IUTchII, §1, but its approach (data (a), (b), (c) up to (Ind1), (Ind2)) is essentially a special case of the tautological approach of IUTchII, Example 1.9 (ii), applied to the vertically coric, a priori uniradial, constructions of Propositions 3.5 (i), 3.10 (i). (ii) The transitions symmetry to labels to processions (Fig. 3.3: F_l^{⋊±} ⇒ F_l ⇒ |F_l| ⇒ ±-processions; F_l^* ⇒ F_l^* labels ⇒ ⊛-processions, with F_l^* ↪ |F_l|) require all labels; the index sets of mono-analytic ±-processions are naked sets determined up to isomorphism by cardinality, so their construction is independent of the arithmetic holomorphic structures, which is what makes them usable in Theorem 3.11 (i); for j ∈ {0, ..., l*} there are j+1 possibilities for the element labeled j, giving (l*+1)! = l^±! label identifications. (iii) The Kummer isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioids in IUTchII, §4 (Corollary 4.6 (ii), (v)), built from quotients of local value groups by local units, fail to give a log-Kummer correspondence, since a multiplicative quotient by units corresponds across the log-link to an additive quotient by their logarithms; hence Theorem 3.11 (ii) uses F^⊛_MOD and F^⊛ℝ_MOD. (iv) For F^⊛ℝ_MOD-based Frobenioids the localization functors ‡ρ_v can be reconstructed from the effect of multiplication by global monoids on log-volumes of local mono-analytic tensor packets (routine details left to the reader); this, with the incompatibilities in (iii), is why splitting monoids at good v are omitted from Theorem 3.11.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11
IUT3.Rem3_11_2.conclusion: Interpretive. Mathematical claims: (ii) the number of label identifications for the index sets of capsules in mono-analytic ±-processions is (l*+1)! = l^±!; the construction of these index sets is independent of the arithmetic holomorphic structures. (iii) the Kummer isomorphisms of global realified Frobenioids of IUTchII, Corollary 4.6 (ii), (v), do not satisfy the mutual compatibility of the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (ii). (iv) the localization functors of the F^⊩-prime-strips n,m𝔉^⊩_LGP can be reconstructed from log-volume data.
external_dependencies: IUTchII: Example 1.9 (ii), §1, Remark 2.6.3, Remark 3.5.2, Remark 3.5.3, Remark 4.5.2 (ii), Remark 4.5.3 (ii), Corollary 4.6 (ii), (v), Propositions 4.2 (ii), 4.4 (ii), Remark 1.12.2 (iv)
IUTchI: §4, §6, Remark 6.6.1, Proposition 6.7, Proposition 6.9 (i), (ii), (iii), Remark 4.7.2 (i), Proposition 4.11 (ii), Definition 5.2 (iv)
obligations: The count (l*+1)! of label identifications is elementary: a choice of j+1 elements for each capsule of size j+1, j = 0, ..., l*, gives ∏_{j=0}^{l*} (j+1) = (l*+1)!; formalizable directly.
State and prove the failure in (iii) precisely (which compatibility fails, for which objects).
Prove the reconstructibility of the localization functors in (iv); the text leaves the routine details to the reader (page 169).
ambiguities: Page 168: '(l*+1)! = l^±!' is consistent with l^± = l* + 1; the count reads the procession as having capsules of sizes 1, ..., l* + 1 with one labeled element each to identify.
'Essentially a special case of the tautological approach' (page 167) is not made precise.

IUT3.Rem3_11_3.content: Relation between the log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 3.11 (ii) and the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii). (i) The squares of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice are far from 1-commutative, but the bi-coricity of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv) may be interpreted as saying the squares are 1-commutative with respect to these bi-coric data. (ii) To relate both unit and value group portions of domain and codomain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link on adjacent vertical lines (n−1,∗), (n,∗), one must use a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (n−1,m) → (n,m); a vertically once-shifted approach (value groups at (n−1,m), (n,m), units at (n−1,m−1), (n,m−1)) fails a priori by the noncommutativity of (i); the single link needs the compatibility properties of Theorem 3.11 (iii) to insulate the cyclotomes of the Kummer theory of the étale theta function and κ-coric functions from the Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies. (iii) Treating units in a once-shifted fashion via bi-coricity requires relating Frobenius-like units to étale-like structures simultaneously via (a) the usual Kummer isomorphisms and (b) their composites with one iterate of the log-link, which is possible only with a relation invariant under pre-composition with iterates of the log-link, as achieved by the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii). (iv) Summary: these correspondences relate unit and value group portions across adjacent vertical lines, insulate the cyclotomes, and are compatible with bi-coricity of mono-analytic log-shells and hence with relating LGP-monoids on adjacent vertical lines; this plays a key role in the proof of Corollary 3.12.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11, an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice
IUT3.Rem3_11_3.conclusion: Interpretive; no new theorem. The claims a formalization would have to address: (i) squares of the lattice commute when restricted to bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells; (ii) a once-shifted correspondence of value groups and unit groups across adjacent vertical lines is not available a priori; (iii) a framework relating Frobenius-like to étale-like structures compatibly with both Kummer isomorphisms and their composites with the log-link exists only if it is invariant under pre-composition with iterates of the log-link, which the log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 3.11 (ii) provides.
obligations: Make (i) precise: for each square of the lattice, the two composites agree on the bi-coric F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips and mono-analytic log-shells up to the stated indeterminacies.
Make the 'only if' of (iii) precise ('may only be realized if', page 170) and prove it, or record it as motivation.
ambiguities: (i) uses 'may be interpreted as the statement that' (page 169): an interpretation of Theorem 1.5, not a separate claim.

The necessity claims of (ii), (iii) ('it is necessary', 'fails, at least from an a priori point of view', 'may only be realized if', pages 169 to 170) are not proved; they motivate the use of the log-Kummer correspondence in Corollary 3.12.

IUT3.Rem3_11_4.content: On the compatibility in the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d). (i) Using the log-Kummer correspondence there amounts to forgetting the labels of the Frobenius-like vertices and identifying their data with the étale-like core, so multiplication of the data of Theorem 3.11 (ii), (b), (c) by roots of unity must be identified with the identity: only orbits under roots of unity are meaningful. This is harmless for theta values, since the theory is invariant under multiplication of the theta values by 2l-th roots of unity (Fig. 3.4: μ_{2l} acting on {q^{j^2}}_{j=1..l*}), and for number fields, since one only uses global Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD, F^⊛_𝔪𝔬𝔡 built from local data and the entire number field, which is stable under roots of unity (Fig. 3.5). The cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism indeterminacies from forgetting labels (Remark 2.3.3 (vi)) are trivial for theta values and amount to multiplication by ±1 on copies of F_mod^× for number fields; for the local data at v ∈ V^non giving the holomorphic log-shells they are trivial, because cyclotomic rigidity there only relates geometric and arithmetic cyclotomes and no 'vicious circles' arise. Hence the a priori indeterminacies in the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) are 'invisible': no substantive effect on the objects. (ii) This list of indeterminacies is complete, since Kummer isomorphisms are completely determined by isomorphisms between cyclotomes and the Galois action on roots of elements of the monoid (FrdII, Definition 2.1 (ii)), and compatibility with Galois actions is tautological. (iii) The invisible indeterminacies of (i) are an analogue of (Ind3) for the data of Theorem 3.11 (ii), (a); multiradiality and radial/coric decoupling (Remarks 2.3.2, 2.3.3) assert that (Ind1), (Ind2) have no effect on the geometric containers underlying Theorem 3.11 (ii), (b), (c).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Thm3_11, in particular the final portion of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d)
implicit_hypotheses: the theta values q^{j^2} and copies of F_mod are considered only up to the stated root-of-unity actions
IUT3.Rem3_11_4.conclusion: Claims: (a) the indeterminacies that might arise a priori in the log-Kummer correspondence portions of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) are invisible, i.e., they have no substantive effect on the objects; this is the sense in which the compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d), is to be understood (page 172). (b) The list of such indeterminacies is complete (page 172), because Kummer isomorphisms are determined by (1) isomorphisms of cyclotomes and (2) the Galois action on roots of elements of the monoid (page 173).
obligations: Define 'no substantive effect' as a precise invariance: for each object used in Corollary 3.12 (log-volumes of hulls of unions of possible images), show it is invariant under the listed indeterminacies (roots of unity on theta values, ±1 on F_mod^×, identity on local cyclotomes).

Prove completeness (ii): every indeterminacy of the log-Kummer correspondence in Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d) factors through a change of cyclotome isomorphism; the text's argument is a 'general nonsense' observation citing FrdII, Definition 2.1 (ii).
The claim that the theory is invariant under multiplication of theta values by 2l-th roots of unity must be traced to the earlier constructions (Remark 2.3.3).
ambiguities: 'Invisible' and 'no substantive effect' (page 172) are not defined; Corollary 3.12 relies on the compatibility of Theorem 3.11 (iii), (c), (d), whose meaning this remark fixes, so the precise reading matters for the proof of Corollary 3.12 (Step (xi)).
Completeness (ii) (pages 172 to 173) is argued informally; 'no possibility that further indeterminacies might arise' is not derived from a definition of indeterminacy.

IUT3.Cor3_12.content: Log-volume estimates for Θ-pilot objects. In the situation of Thm 3.11, with −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} and −|log(q)| ∈ R as defined in the statement (IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement), −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|. Proof: an opening reduction and Steps (i) to (xii). Not stated as a Lean Prop. Lean lemmas about the two numbers alone are recorded as fragments of IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement, IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction and IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.f; they do not formalize this corollary.
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Thm 3.11
IUT3.Cor3_12.conclusion: Two conjuncts: (F) −|log(Θ)| ∈ R, and (I) −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|. The 'i.e.' clause of page 174 (C_Θ ≥ −1 for every real C_Θ with −|log(Θ)| ≤ C_Θ·|log(q)|) reformulates (I) only: it holds vacuously when −|log(Θ)| = +∞ (IUT.PaperIII.Corollary312.constantForm_of_top). The statement is therefore (F) ∧ (I), equivalently (F) ∧ (the 'i.e.' clause); finiteness is kept as a separate conjunct in both formulations.
obligations: See the step records and docs/COR312_ANALYSIS.md.
Prove (F) separately: compactness of the 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} (asserted '[easily verified]' on page 175) and the all-but-finitely-many support condition of the global log-volume (Prop 3.9 (iii), page 117).

IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement.content: −|log(Θ)| ∈ R ∪ {+∞} is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume (average over j ∈ F*_l) of the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of a Θ-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms of Thm 3.11 (ii), in the multiradial representation of Thm 3.11 (i), subject to Ind1, Ind2, Ind3. −|log(q)| ∈ R is the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the image of a q-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms, in the multiradial representation, not subject to the indeterminacies; △ is the result of identifying the labels 0 and ⟨F*_l⟩. |log(q)| > 0 is 'easily computed' from the q-parameters at v ∈ V^bad (≠ ∅).
explicit_hypotheses: situation of Thm 3.11
implicit_hypotheses: the union of possible images is a subset of the packets on which the hull is defined (Rem 3.9.5 (i) requires a relatively compact subset of finite log-volume)
IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement.conclusion: (F) −|log(Θ)| ∈ R, and (I) −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|; the 'i.e.' clause on page 174 is equivalent to (I) only under (F).
definitions_required: possible image of a Θ-pilot object
obligations: Define the set of possible images: the orbit of the image under the action generated by (Ind1) and (Ind2), together with the containments allowed by (Ind3).
Define the hull of the union and its log-volume.
Prove |log(q)| > 0 from ord_v(q_v) > 0 at bad v and V^bad ≠ ∅.
Prove finiteness (F) as its own claim: the compactness of each 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} asserted on page 175, and the support condition of Prop 3.9 (iii) (page 117) for the family of hulls.

The comparison is with the hull of the union of the possible images: a single image whose hull dominates the q-pilot region is a sufficient route, not a necessary one (two singleton images of measure 1/4 each jointly have log-volume log(1/2), while each has log(1/4)).
ambiguities: Averaging index: the statement (page 173) and Step (x) (page 181) say explicitly that the average is over j ∈ F*_l, so the factor is 1/l* (not displayed); Prop 3.4 (ii) (page 102) and Rem 3.9.3 (page 120) corroborate the labels j ∈ {1, ..., l*}. Pages 153 and 174 index the packets and the sets U, Ū by j ∈ |F_l|; they state no average. Page 183 speaks of a log-volume 'normalized, with respect to j ∈ |F_l|', with no factor; an average over |F_l| would carry 1/(l*+1). How the j = 0 component of a region indexed over |F_l| enters the average over F*_l (dropped, or identified with the diagonal label ⟨F*_l⟩ through △, pages 174 and 181) is not stated.
The extracted text of page 174 reads 'V^bad (= ∅)'; the rendered page reads '(≠ ∅)'. This is an extraction artifact, not a discrepancy in the paper.

'possible images' and 'subject to the indeterminacies' are not defined as a set by an explicit formula; whether Ind3 enlarges each image to a containing region or acts as a separate indeterminacy is not stated.

IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction.content: Since |log(q)| > 0 one may assume −|log(Θ)| < 0 whenever it is real. U = {n,◦U_{j,v_Q}} for j ∈ |F_l|, v_Q ∈ V_Q: unions of possible images in n,◦U^Q_{j,v_Q} = I^Q(S^±_{j+1}; n,◦D^⊢_{v_Q}). Ū = their holomorphic hulls relative to the holomorphic structure labeled n,◦. From the '[easily verified] compactness' of the 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} and the definition of log-volume, −|log(Θ)| is finite, hence negative. One may restrict to possible images that can be interpreted as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip.
explicit_hypotheses: inherits the hypotheses of IUT3.Cor3_12.Statement
IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction.conclusion: Without loss of generality −|log(Θ)| < 0 whenever −|log(Θ)| ∈ R (a nonnegative value already satisfies (I)); −|log(Θ)| is finite, hence negative, by the compactness of the 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} and the definition of the log-volume; one may restrict to possible images interpretable as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip.
obligations: The numerical reduction concerns the inequality conjunct only; finiteness is a separate claim.

Prove compactness of each 1,◦U_{j,v_Q} (union over the orbit of the action generated by (Ind1) and (Ind2), enlarged by (Ind3)); page 175 calls it '[easily verified]' and gives no argument. Requires the action to factor through a compact or finite group and the (Ind3) enlargements to be bounded. A direct product Ind1 × Ind2 is not assumed: page 154 does not state that the actions commute.
Prove that compactness implies each local hull is a proper λ·O, hence of finite local log-volume (Rem 3.9.5 (i)).

Prove the support condition: the local log-volumes of the hulls vanish for all but finitely many v_Q (Prop 3.9 (iii), page 117), so that the global average is a real number; placewise compactness alone does not give this.
Justify that restricting to possible images interpretable as F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips does not change the hull or only shrinks it in a way consistent with the inequality.
ambiguities: The WLOG reduction is numerical (fragment IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction.frag.inequality_of_nonneg). The finiteness claim rests on '[easily verified] compactness' (page 175), for which no argument is given.
The restriction to images interpretable as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip shrinks the union; the effect on the hull and hence on −|log(Θ)| is not discussed.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI.content: Step (i) fixes the setting: one concentrates on a single arrow of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, the single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link 0,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → 1,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}, which consists of the full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips 0,0F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ (Definition 3.8 (ii)). This poly-isomorphism 'may be thought of' as consisting of a unit portion, the associated full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips 0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊢×μ}_△, and a value group portion, the associated full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips 0,0F^{⊩▶}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊩▶}_△ (Definition 2.4 (iii)). Key sentence (page 175): 'This value group portion of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link maps Θ-pilot objects of 0,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} to q-pilot objects of 1,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} [cf. Remark 3.8.1].'
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Corollary 3.12: initial Θ-data and a collection {n,mHT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}}_{n,m∈Z} of distinct Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters arising from an LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Theorem 3.11; Definition 3.8 (iii))
the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link 0,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF} → 1,0HT^{Θ^{±ell}NF}, i.e. the full poly-isomorphism 0,0F^{⊩▶×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊩▶×μ}_△ (Definition 3.8 (ii))

the reduction at the start of the proof (pages 174 to 175): without loss of generality −|log(Θ)| < 0 whenever −|log(Θ)| ∈ R, and attention is restricted to possible images of a Θ-pilot object that may be interpreted as an F^{⊩▶}-prime-strip (IUT3.Cor3_12.Reduction)
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI.conclusion: The argument works with the single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (0,0) → (1,0); its full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips is regarded as a unit portion (full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strips) together with a value group portion (full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips), and the value group portion maps Θ-pilot objects of 0,0HT to q-pilot objects of 1,0HT. Justification in the text: Definition 3.8 (ii), Definition 2.4 (iii), and, for the pilot objects, a reference to Remark 3.8.1, which states this without argument.
obligations: Show that the full poly-isomorphism of F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strips determines, and is determined by, the pair consisting of the full poly-isomorphisms of the associated F^{⊢×μ}- and F^{⊩▶}-prime-strips (the text says it 'may be thought of as consisting of' these two portions; whether the decomposition is a bijection of sets of isomorphisms is not stated).

Prove that every isomorphism in the value group portion carries the Θ-pilot object of 0,0HT to the q-pilot object of 1,0HT (page 175, by reference to Remark 3.8.1, page 114, where it is stated without argument).
ambiguities: Page 175: 'may be thought of as consisting of' leaves open whether the unit and value group portions are independent (a product decomposition of the poly-isomorphism) or only two projections of it.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepII.content: Step (ii): the units of the Frobenioids in the F^{⊢×μ}-prime-strip 0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP are subject to Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies, i.e. (Ind1), (Ind2) (Theorem 3.11 (iii) (a), (b)), whereas the cyclotomes in the Kummer theory of the étale theta function and of κ-coric functions, which give rise to the value group portion 0,0F^{⊩▶}_LGP, are insulated from these indeterminacies (Theorem 3.11 (iii) (c), (d); Remark 3.11.3 (iv); Fig. 3.6). For the étale theta function this follows from §2, in essence from the cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments ([EtTh]); for κ-coric functions it follows from the algorithms of IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii). Fig. 3.6 (page 176): local LGP-monoids (Proposition 3.4 (ii)) and copies of F_mod (Proposition 3.7 (i)) require mono-analytic containers and have Kummer theory incompatible with (Ind1), (Ind2); the étale theta function and mono-theta environments (Corollary 2.3) and global ∞κ-coric and local ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric structures (Remark 2.3.2) are independent of mono-analytic containers and have Kummer theory compatible with (Ind1), (Ind2) (Remark 2.3.3). Key sentence (page 175): the cyclotomes 'are insulated from these Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies'.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2) of Theorem 3.11 (i), acting through Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP) (Theorem 3.11 (iii) (a), (b))
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepII.conclusion: The units of 0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP are subject to (Ind1), (Ind2), while the cyclotomes of the Kummer theory of the étale theta function and of κ-coric functions, which give rise to 0,0F^{⊩▶}_LGP, are insulated from the Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies. Justification in the text: citation of Theorem 3.11 (iii) (c), (d), Remark 3.11.3 (iv), §2 (cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments, [EtTh]) and IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii).
external_dependencies: EtTh: cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments
obligations: Prove that the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms for mono-theta environments and for κ-coric functions are fixed by every element of Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP) (external: [EtTh]; IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii); within this paper Theorem 2.2 (ii) and Theorem 3.11 (iii) (c), (d)).

Status: the insulation claim is backed by Theorem 3.11 (iii) (c), (d), by external citations ([EtTh]; IUTchI) and by Remark 3.11.3 (iv), whose record is BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_JUSTIFICATION; the step takes the weakest of these.
ambiguities: Fig. 3.6 (page 176) cites Remark 2.3.2 for the κ-coric case, where the formulation in the style of Corollary 2.3 is left to the reader (page 76); the text of Step (ii) cites IUTchI instead.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIII.content: Step (iii): it is of crucial importance to relate simultaneously both the unit and the value group portions of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link(s) on the 0-column (the vertical line indexed by 0) to the corresponding portions on the 1-column. Key sentence (page 176): 'if one attempts to relate the unit portions via one Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link [say, from (0, m) to (1, m)] and the value group portions via another Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link [say, from (0, m′) to (1, m′), for m′ ≠ m], then the non-commutativity of the log-theta-lattice renders it practically impossible to obtain conclusions that require one to relate both the unit and the value group portions simultaneously [cf. the discussion of Remark 3.11.3, (i), (ii)]. This is precisely why we concentrate on a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link [cf. (i)].'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the 0-column and 1-column of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice; Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links (0, m) → (1, m) and (0, m′) → (1, m′) with m′ ≠ m
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIII.conclusion: Relating the unit portions through one Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link and the value group portions through another at a different height is, by the non-commutativity of the log-theta-lattice, 'practically impossible' for conclusions needing both simultaneously; hence a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link is used. Justification in the text: assertion with a reference to Remark 3.11.3 (i), (ii).
obligations: The impossibility claim (page 176) is informal and supported only by a reference to Remark 3.11.3 (i), (ii); to be checkable it must be stated as a precise non-commutativity statement about the composites of log-links and Θ^{×μ}_LGP-links. It motivates the choice of a single link; the later steps do not use it as a premise.
ambiguities: 'Practically impossible' (page 176) has no formal meaning.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIV.content: Step (iv): ultimately one wishes to apply the bi-coricity of the units (Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv)) to compute the 0-column Θ-pilot object in terms of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of the 1-column. For this one must work with units that are vertically once-shifted, i.e. lie at (n, m − 1), relative to the value group structures, which lie at (n, m) (Remark 3.11.3 (ii)). Key sentences (pages 176 to 177): 'The solution to the problem of simultaneously accommodating these apparently contradictory requirements, i.e., "vertical shift" vs. "impossibility of vertical shift" [cf. (iii)], is given precisely by working, on the 0-column, with structures that are invariant with respect to vertical shifts [i.e., "(0, m) ↦ (0, m + 1)"] of the log-theta-lattice [cf. the discussion surrounding Remark 1.2.2, (iii), (a)] such as vertically coric structures [i.e., indexed by "(n, ◦)"] that are related to the "Frobenius-like" structures which are not vertically coric by means of the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11, (ii). Here, we note that this "solution" may be implemented only at the cost of admitting the "indeterminacy" constituted by the upper semi-compatibility of (Ind3).'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the requirement of Step (iii) that unit and value group portions be related through a single Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link
the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii) and the indeterminacy (Ind3)
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIV.conclusion: On the 0-column one works with vertically coric structures (indexed by (n, ◦)), invariant under the vertical shifts (0, m) ↦ (0, m + 1), related to the non-coric Frobenius-like structures by the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii); the price is the indeterminacy (Ind3) (upper semi-compatibility). Justification in the text: references to Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), Remark 3.11.3 (ii), Remark 1.2.2 (iii) (a) and Theorem 3.11 (ii).
obligations: Formalize the passage from Frobenius-like data at (0, m) to vertically coric data at (0, ◦) via Theorem 3.11 (ii), and record the loss as the containment (Ind3).

The need for units at (n, m − 1) relative to value groups at (n, m) is taken from Remark 3.11.3 (ii) (record BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_JUSTIFICATION) and the price (Ind3) from Theorem 3.11 (ii); this step states both and does not derive them.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepV.content: Step (v): the computation of the 0-column Θ-pilot object in terms of the arithmetic holomorphic structure of the 1-column begins by relating the units on the 0- and 1-columns through the unit portion 0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊢×μ}_△ of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link from (0, 0) to (1, 0) (Step (i)) and then applying the bi-coricity of the units of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv). The mono-analytic log-shell interpretation of this bi-coricity (Theorem 1.5 (iv)) is applied to regard the mono-analytic log-shells as multiradial mono-analytic containers (Remark 1.5.2 (i), (ii), (iii)) for the local and global value group structures constituting the Θ-pilot object on the 0-column (Fig. 3.6); the parallel treatment of theta-related and number field-related objects is 'reminiscent' of IUTchII, Remark 4.11.2 (iv). Key sentence (page 177): 'we will relate the various Frobenioid-theoretic [i.e., "Frobenius-like", cf. Remark 1.5.4, (i)] local units at v ∈ V, splitting monoids at v ∈ V^bad, and global Frobenioids indexed by (0, m), for m ∈ Z, to the vertically coric [i.e., indexed by "(0, ◦)"] versions of these bi-coric mono-analytic containers by means of the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11, (ii), (a), (b), (c), i.e., by varying the "Kummer input index" (0, m) along the 0-column.'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the unit portion 0,0F^{⊢×μ}_LGP ≅ 1,0F^{⊢×μ}_△ of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (Step (i))
the bi-coricity of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv) and the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii) (a), (b), (c)
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepV.conclusion: Plan of computation: transport units from the 0-column to the 1-column via the unit portion of the link and bi-coricity, use the mono-analytic log-shells as multiradial containers for the value group structures of the 0-column Θ-pilot object, and relate the Frobenius-like local units, splitting monoids and global Frobenioids at (0, m) to their vertically coric (0, ◦) versions by the log-Kummer correspondences, varying m.
obligations: Show that the bi-coric log-shells at (0, ◦) and (1, ◦) are identified through the unit portion of the link and Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv), so that regions in one can be transported to the other.

Status: the use of mono-analytic log-shells as multiradial containers is backed by Remark 1.5.2 (i), (ii), (iii), whose record is BLOCKED_BY_EXTERNAL_THEOREM; Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv) and Theorem 3.11 (ii) (a), (b), (c) are EXTRACTED.
ambiguities: IUTchII, Remark 4.11.2 (iv) is cited on page 177 only as 'reminiscent'; it is not used as a premise, so it is not listed as an external dependency.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVI.content: Step (vi) recalls: the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii) (b), (c) are obtained as a consequence of the splittings, up to roots of unity, of the relevant monoids into unit and value group portions constructed by the Galois evaluation operations of Remarks 2.2.2 (iii) (for (b)) and 2.3.2 (for (c)). The Kummer theory of the local LGP-monoids of Proposition 3.4 (ii) depends essentially on IUTchII, §3 (especially Corollaries 3.5, 3.6), which depends essentially on the Kummer theory of mono-theta environments of [EtTh]: the discrete rigidity of [EtTh] avoids Ẑ-divisors/line bundles, which are fundamentally incompatible with conventional divisors/line bundles and with mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity (Remark 2.1.1 (v)); 'isomorphism class compatibility' (compatibility with the topology of the tempered fundamental group, Remark 2.1.1) allows the Kummer theory of mono-theta environments to be applied relative to the ring-theoretic basepoints on either side of the log-link (Remarks 2.1.1 (ii), 2.3.3 (vii); IUTchII, Remark 3.6.4 (i)). Key sentence (page 178): 'it is precisely by establishing this conjugate synchronization arising from the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry relative to these basepoints that occur on either side of the log-link that one is able to conclude the crucial compatibility of this conjugate synchronization with the log-link [cf. Remark 1.3.2].' Similarly, the MLF-Galois pair approach to cyclotomic rigidity at v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non (IUTchII, Corollary 1.11 (a), Remark 1.11.1 (i) (a), Proposition 4.2 (i); AbsTopIII, Proposition 3.2 (iv); Remark 2.3.3 (viii)) amounts to Galois cohomology computations (proof of AbsAnab, Proposition 1.2.1 (vii)) manifestly compatible with the topology of the profinite groups, not requiring Kummer towers (IUTchII, Remark 3.6.4 (i)); the corresponding property at v ∈ V^arc (IUTchII, Proposition 4.4 (i)) follows from IUTchI, Remark 3.4.2 (co-holomorphicizations). The number field approach (IUTchI, Example 5.1 (v), Definition 5.2 (vi), (viii)) depends on Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}, which is 'fundamentally incompatible' with the topology of the profinite groups (it 'clearly cannot be obtained as some sort of limit of corresponding properties of (Z/NZ)^×'), but admits a natural multiradial formulation (Theorem 3.11 (iii) (d); Remarks 2.3.2, 3.11.3), unlike the uniradial MLF-Galois pair approach (IUTchII, Remark 1.11.3). Key sentence (page 179): 'Finally, we recall that [one verifies immediately that] the various approaches to cyclotomic rigidity just discussed are mutually compatible in the sense that they yield the same cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism in any setting in which more than one of these approaches may be applied.' Fig. 3.7 (page 179): mono-theta environments: multiradial, compatible; MLF-Galois pairs via Brauer groups: uniradial, compatible; number fields via Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}: multiradial, incompatible (compatibility with F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, profinite/tempered topologies, ring structures, log-link).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii) (b), (c)
for the MLF-Galois pair approach: v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non; for the archimedean property: v ∈ V^arc; for mono-theta environments: v ∈ V^bad
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVI.conclusion: Recollection of the sources of the log-Kummer correspondences and of three approaches to cyclotomic rigidity (Fig. 3.7), with the assertion, given without argument, that the three approaches yield the same cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism wherever more than one applies (page 179).
external_dependencies: IUTchII: §3, Corollaries 3.5, 3.6; Remark 3.6.4 (i); Corollary 1.11 (a); Remark 1.11.1 (i) (a); Proposition 4.2 (i); Proposition 4.4 (i); Remark 1.11.3
EtTh: discrete rigidity; Kummer theory of mono-theta environments; isomorphism class compatibility
obligations: Prove mutual compatibility of the three cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms of Fig. 3.7 in every setting where two of them apply (page 179: '[one verifies immediately that]'; no argument is given).

Make precise and prove that Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1} 'cannot be obtained as some sort of limit of corresponding properties of (Z/NZ)^×' (page 178; asserted without argument). The identity Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1} itself is elementary.
The compatibility of conjugate synchronization with the log-link (page 178) is taken from Remark 1.3.2.
ambiguities: Page 179: 'mutually compatible' is defined only as yielding the same isomorphism where more than one approach applies; the settings where two approaches overlap are not listed.
Page 178: the sense of 'fundamentally incompatible with the topology of the profinite groups involved' is informal.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVII.content: Step (vii): the constructions underlying the bi-coricity theory of Theorem 1.5 (iii), (iv) depend essentially on the conjugate synchronization arising from the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, which relates the local monoids and Galois groups at distinct labels ∈ |F_l| in a fashion simultaneously compatible with the vertically coric structures and Kummer theory that give rise to the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii), and with the property of distinguishing (not identifying) data indexed by distinct labels ∈ |F_l| (Remark 1.5.1 (i), (ii)). Key sentence (page 179): 'Since, moreover, this crucial conjugate synchronization is fundamentally incompatible with the F^⊛_l-symmetry, it is necessary to work with these two symmetries separately, as was done in [IUTchI], §4, §5, §6 [cf. [IUTchII], Remark 4.7.6].' The F^⊛_l-symmetry allows one to 'descend to F_mod' at the level of absolute Galois groups (IUTchII, Remark 4.7.6). Both symmetries are compatible with the vertical coricity and Kummer isomorphisms of the 0-column (log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii) (b) for F^{⋊±}_l, (c) for F^⊛_l); their vertically coric versions depend essentially on the arithmetic holomorphic structure of the 0-column, hence give rise to multiradial structures via the tautological approach of Remark 3.11.2 (i), (ii).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the F^{⋊±}_l- and F^⊛_l-symmetries of IUTchI, §4, §5, §6
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVII.conclusion: Bi-coricity depends on conjugate synchronization from the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry, compatible with the log-Kummer correspondences and with distinguishing distinct labels; this synchronization is incompatible with the F^⊛_l-symmetry, so the symmetries are treated separately; both are compatible with vertical coricity and the Kummer isomorphisms of the 0-column and yield multiradial structures (Remark 3.11.2 (i), (ii)). Justification in the text: citations of IUTchI, §4 to §6, IUTchII, Remark 4.7.6, Remark 1.5.1, Theorem 3.11 (ii) (b), (c) and Remark 3.11.2.
definitions_required: conjugate synchronization; F^{⋊±}_l- and F^⊛_l-symmetries (IUTchI, §4 to §6)
obligations: Formalize conjugate synchronization and the F^{⋊±}_l- and F^⊛_l-symmetries; the incompatibility of conjugate synchronization with the F^⊛_l-symmetry (page 179) is cited from IUTchI, §4 to §6 and IUTchII, Remark 4.7.6.
Status: the multiradiality of the vertically coric symmetries is backed by Remark 3.11.2 (i), (ii) (page 180), whose record is BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_JUSTIFICATION.
ambiguities: Page 179: 'fundamentally incompatible' is not made precise here.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVIII.content: Step (viii): to construct the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry one uses global ±-synchronizations of local ±-indeterminacies. Key sentence (page 180): 'Since the local tempered fundamental groups at v ∈ V^bad do not extend to a "global tempered fundamental group", these global ±-synchronizations give rise to profinite conjugacy indeterminacies in the vertically coric construction of the LGP-monoids [i.e., the theta values at torsion points] given in [IUTchII], §2, which are resolved by applying the theory of [IUTchI], §2, cf. the discussion of [IUTchI], Remark 6.12.4, (iii); [IUTchII], Remark 4.5.3, (iii); [IUTchII], Remark 4.11.2, (iii).'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry of Step (vii); v ∈ V^bad
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepVIII.conclusion: The global ±-synchronizations used for the F^{⋊±}_l-symmetry produce profinite conjugacy indeterminacies in the vertically coric construction of the LGP-monoids (IUTchII, §2), and these are resolved by the theory of IUTchI, §2.
obligations: Make precise and prove that the local tempered fundamental groups at v ∈ V^bad 'do not extend to a global tempered fundamental group' (page 180; asserted without argument), and that this is the source of the profinite conjugacy indeterminacies.
The resolution of these indeterminacies is cited from IUTchI, §2 (external).
ambiguities: Page 180: 'do not extend' is not given a formal meaning.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIX.content: Step (ix): the copies of F_mod, i.e. the global Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD, F^⊛_mod (fraktur) and their realifications, play an important role: the ring structure of the global field F_mod furnishes a translation apparatus between the multiplicative structures constituted by the global realified Frobenioids related via the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link and the additive representations of these global Frobenioids in the mono-analytic log-shells (Step (v)). Key sentences (page 180): 'the precise compatibility of the ingredients for "F^⊛_MOD" with the log-Kummer correspondence renders "F^⊛_MOD" better suited to describing the relation to the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link [cf. Remark 3.10.1, (ii)]. On the other hand, the local portion of "F^⊛_mod", i.e., which is subject to "upper semi-compatibility" [cf. (Ind3)], hence only "approximately compatible" with the log-Kummer correspondence, renders it better suited to explicit estimates of global arithmetic degrees, by means of log-volumes [cf. Remark 3.10.1, (iii)].'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the global Frobenioids F^⊛_MOD, F^⊛_mod of Proposition 3.7 and Proposition 3.10
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepIX.conclusion: F^⊛_MOD, precisely compatible with the log-Kummer correspondence, is used to describe the relation to the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link; F^⊛_mod, whose local portion is only upper semi-compatible (Ind3), is used for explicit estimates of global arithmetic degrees by log-volumes. Justification in the text: reference to Remark 3.10.1 (ii), (iii).
obligations: Formalize F^⊛_MOD and F^⊛_mod and the compatibility (precise, resp. upper semi-) of each with the log-Kummer correspondence, as established in Proposition 3.10 and Theorem 3.11 (ii) and discussed in Remark 3.10.1 (ii), (iii).
Status: both claims are backed only by Remark 3.10.1 (ii), (iii), whose record is BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_JUSTIFICATION.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepX.content: Step (x): summary. The theory of 'Kummer-detachment' (Remarks 1.5.4 (i); 2.1.1; 3.10.1 (ii), (iii)), furnished by Theorem 3.11 (ii), (iii), relates the Frobenioid-theoretic (Frobenius-like) structures in the domain, at (0, 0), of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (Step (i)) to the multiradial representation of Theorem 3.11 (i) (a), (b), (c), but only at the cost of the indeterminacies (Ind1), arising from compatibility with the permutation symmetries of the étale-picture (Theorem 3.11 (i)); (Ind2), arising from compatibility with the Aut_{F^{⊢×μ}}(−)-indeterminacies on the domain/codomain of the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link (Step (ii); Theorem 3.11 (i), (iii)), i.e. the horizontal arrows; (Ind3), arising from compatibility with the log-Kummer correspondences of Theorem 3.11 (ii), i.e. the vertical arrows. These may be thought of as data describing a 'formal quotient', like fine moduli spaces. Key sentence (page 181): 'the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes [i.e., where the average is taken over j ∈ F*_l] of Theorem 3.11, (i), (a), (c), furnish a means of constructing a sort of associated "coarse space" or "inductive limit" [...] in the sense that [one verifies immediately, cf. Proposition 3.9, (ii), that] the resulting log-volumes ∈ R are invariant with respect to the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2), and have the effect of converting the indeterminacy (Ind3) into an inequality [from above].' The log-link compatibility of the log-volumes (Proposition 3.9 (iv); final portion of Theorem 3.11 (ii)) ensures they are compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms and log-links of the log-Kummer correspondence. The averages over j ∈ F*_l 'may be thought of as a consequence of' the F^⊛_l-symmetry acting on the labels of the theta values giving rise to the LGP-monoids (IUTchII, Corollary 4.10 (i), symbol △, via the identification of the symbols '0' and '⟨F*_l⟩'; Remark 3.9.3). The tensor products in the local mono-analytic tensor packets of Theorem 3.11 (i) (a) identify multiplication by elements of Z, hence its effect on log-volumes, at different labels ∈ F*_l.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI
the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3) of Theorem 3.11
the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volumes of Theorem 3.11 (i) (a), (c), averaged over j ∈ F*_l
implicit_hypotheses: the weights of Remark 3.1.1 (ii), which already divide by the local degree, as in IUT3.Prop3_9

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXII.content: Step (xii): the global realified Frobenioids appearing in the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link play an important role in the argument of (xi). Since only log-volumes are computed, it might seem possible to dispense with the global Frobenioids and work only with the local Frobenioids at v ∈ V. Key sentences (pages 185 to 186): 'observe that since the isomorphism of [local or global!] Frobenioids arising from the Θ^{×μ}_LGP-link only preserves isomorphism classes of objects of these Frobenioids [cf. the discussion of Remark 3.6.2, (i)], to work only with local Frobenioids means that one must contend with the indeterminacy of not knowing whether, for instance, such a local Frobenioid object at some v ∈ V^non corresponds to a given open submodule of the log-shell at v or to, say, the p_v^N-multiple of this submodule, for N ∈ Z. Put another way, one must contend with the indeterminacy arising from the fact that, unlike the case with the global Frobenioids "F^⊛_MOD", "F^{⊛R}_MOD", objects of the various local Frobenioids that arise admit endomorphisms which are not automorphisms. This indeterminacy has the effect of rendering meaningless any attempt to perform a precise log-volume computation as in (xi).'
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT3.Cor3_12.StepI and the argument of Step (xi)
v ∈ V^non, N ∈ Z
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXII.conclusion: The global realified Frobenioids cannot be replaced by local Frobenioids: the link preserves only isomorphism classes of objects (Remark 3.6.2 (i)), and local Frobenioid objects admit non-invertible endomorphisms, so an object at v ∈ V^non would not determine whether it corresponds to a given open submodule of the log-shell or to its p_v^N-multiple; this would render the log-volume computation of (xi) meaningless.
obligations: Prove that isomorphism classes of objects of the global realified Frobenioid determine the degree (log-volume), while those of the local Frobenioids at v ∈ V^non do not determine the p_v^N scaling (pages 185 to 186; asserted without argument, with a reference to Remark 3.6.2 (i)).
Prove that objects of the local Frobenioids admit endomorphisms that are not automorphisms, whereas those of F^⊛_MOD, F^{⊛R}_MOD do not (page 185; asserted without argument).
Status: the preservation of only isomorphism classes is backed by Remark 3.6.2 (i), whose record is BLOCKED_BY_EXTERNAL_THEOREM; the endomorphism claim and the conclusion have no backing.
ambiguities: Page 186: 'rendering meaningless' is informal; the step explains why global Frobenioids are used and does not itself prove a step of the inequality.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.d.content: The hull outputs are localizations of arithmetic vector bundles of rank > 1, while the q-pilot object is an arithmetic line bundle. Forming a suitable positive tensor power of the determinant (Rem 3.9.5 (vii), (Ob3), (Ob4)) and applying the log-volume '[suitably normalized, with respect to j ∈ |F_l|]' to the region 1,◦Ū and to the region of the q-pilot object at (1,0) on 1,◦U^Q gives completely comparable objects R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} = {λ ∈ R | λ ≤ −|log(Θ)|} ⊆ R and −|log(q)| ∈ R, where −|log(Θ)| is by definition the (negative) log-volume of 1,◦Ū and −|log(q)| the log-volume of the q-pilot region. Global arithmetic degrees are log-volumes (Prop 3.9 (iii)). The log-Kummer correspondence in the 1-column rectifies the vertical shift between the unit portion of 1,0 𝔉_△^{⊩▶×μ} and the log-shells forming 1,◦U.
IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.d.conclusion: Nature of the justification in the text: argument with citation.

The set R_{≤−|log(Θ)|} is introduced as 'possible log-volumes of pilot-object output data'; why every real number below −|log(Θ)| is a possible log-volume, rather than only the log-volumes of actual possible images, is not argued.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.e.content: The relationship between the pilot-object log-volume −|log(q)| and the input F^{⊩▶×μ}-prime-strip is the one imposed by the holomorphic structure in the 1-column. Assessment: at the level of real numbers the premise of the last step is the conclusion; any non-circular argument must establish the inclusion at the level of regions or of the algorithm.
The inclusion is equivalent to the inequality conjunct only; with −|log(Θ)| = +∞ it holds trivially, so finiteness must be proved separately.

IUT3.Cor3_12.StepXI.g.content: Summary: the algorithm, followed by hull and log-volume, yields two tautologically equivalent ways to compute the log-volume of the q-pilot object at (1,0) (Fig. 3.8): via Kummer-detachment and the log-Kummer correspondence from the Θ-pilot at (0,0) compatibly with the link, then the permutation symmetry to (1,◦) and comparison via hull and log-volume; or directly from the q-pilot object at (1,0).

IUT3.Rem3_12_3.content: (i) Analogy with hyperbolic Riemann surfaces S of finite type (genus g_S, r_S punctures, χ_S = −(2g_S − 2 + r_S), Kähler form dμ_S from the Poincaré metric): the inequality of Corollary 3.12 corresponds to χ_S = −∫_S dμ_S < 0, the hyperbolicity of S from Gauss-Bonnet and positivity of dμ_S; the positivity corresponds to the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism of an indigenous bundle in p-adic theory and, in the theory of log-shells, to the maximal incompatibility between Kummer isomorphisms and the coric data of the Frobenius-picture of Proposition 1.2 (x), which gives rise to the upper semi-commutativity of Remark 1.2.2 (iii) and the upper semi-compatibility (Ind3) of Theorem 3.11 (ii) underlying the inequality (Step (x) of the proof of Corollary 3.12). (ii) Analogy with classical complex Teichmüller theory: canonical algorithms relating alien arithmetic holomorphic structures give a relatively strong estimate of log-volume distortion.
explicit_hypotheses: for (i): S a hyperbolic Riemann surface of finite type
IUT3.Rem3_12_3.conclusion: Analogy only; no assertion about the objects of the paper. The one classical statement invoked is χ_S = −∫_S dμ_S < 0 for a hyperbolic Riemann surface of finite type with the Poincaré Kähler form (Gauss-Bonnet), and the remark attributes the inequality of Corollary 3.12 to (Ind3) via Step (x) of its proof.
obligations: None for the paper's objects. The attribution of the inequality of Corollary 3.12 to (Ind3) is recorded in IUT3.Cor3_12.StepX.
ambiguities: Heuristic analogy; 'maximal incompatibility' (page 195) is not defined.

IUT3.Rem3_12_4.content: Analogy between IUT and p-adic Teichmüller theory (Fig. 3.10): splitting monoids at bad v ↔ canonical coordinates on the ordinary locus; bad primes ↔ ordinary locus, good primes ↔ supersingular locus; bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells O^{×μ} ↔ multiplicative Teichmüller representatives; uniradial local holomorphic units O^× with F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry ↔ positive characteristic ring structures; theta value labels F_l^* ↔ the factor p in the mod p/p^2 portion of Witt vectors, and averaging over F_l^* ↔ dividing by p; the multiradial representation via F_l^*-labeled mono-analytic log-shells ↔ derivative of the canonical Frobenius lifting, whose absolute comparison is the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2); F_l^* ↔ infinitesimal moduli or absolute moduli over F_1; the inequality from upper semi-compatibility (Ind3) ↔ the inequality from interference between Frobenius conjugates. (v) For a canonical smooth proper hyperbolic curve X over the Witt vectors A of a perfect field of characteristic p, with ordinary locus Û and canonical Frobenius lifting Φ, dividing the derivative of Φ by p gives only an inclusion ω_{X_k} ↪ Φ^*ω_{X_k} (square Hasse invariant), hence at the level of global degrees the inequality (1 − p)(2g_X − 2) ≤ 0.
explicit_hypotheses: for (v): A the ring of Witt vectors of a perfect field k of characteristic p; X a smooth proper hyperbolic curve over A of genus g_X, canonical in the sense of p-adic Teichmüller theory; Û ⊆ X̂ the ordinary locus; Φ: Û → Û the canonical Frobenius lifting
IUT3.Rem3_12_4.conclusion: Analogy only for the paper's objects. The p-adic statement cited in (v): the derivative of Φ divided by p yields an inclusion, not an isomorphism, ω_{X_k} ↪ Φ^*ω_{X_k}, whence (1 − p)(2g_X − 2) ≤ 0 (pOrd, Chapter II, Proposition 2.6; Chapter III, §1). The remark states that the inequality of Corollary 3.12 arises from circumstances 'entirely analogous' to this one, namely (Ind3).
definitions_required: canonical curve, ordinary locus, canonical Frobenius lifting, square Hasse invariant (pOrd, pTeich)
external_dependencies: pOrd: Chapter II, Proposition 2.6; Chapter III, §1
obligations: None for the paper's objects.
The degree computation in (v) is elementary given the inclusion: deg ω = 2g_X − 2 and deg Φ^*ω = p(2g_X − 2), so the inclusion forces 2g_X − 2 ≤ p(2g_X − 2).
ambiguities: Heuristic analogy; 'entirely analogous' (page 198) is not a mathematical claim that can be checked.

IUT3.Rem3_6_2.content: (i) Frobenioids isomorphic to the realification of F^⊛_mod lying on opposite sides of an enhanced version of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link are to be related; at the level of objects only isomorphism classes preserved by the isomorphisms of Frobenioids make sense, and these are determined by the divisor and rational function monoids of the model Frobenioid ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (i), (ii)). The rational function monoid F^×_mod of F^⊛_mod has the fundamental property that F^×_mod ∪ {0} admits a natural additive structure; this fails for (a) the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification of F^⊛_mod and (b) subgroups Γ ⊆ F^×_mod (such as {1} or the S-units for a nonempty finite S ⊆ V_mod) that are not the multiplicative group of a subfield of F_mod (AbsTopIII, Remark 5.10.2 (iv)). This allows objects of F^⊛_mod to be represented additively, as modules (Example 3.6 (ii)): 'adding' two elements of a Γ-torsor is meaningful only if Γ is additively closed. The additive representation is used to relate objects of F^⊛_mod on opposite sides of the enhanced Θ^{×μ}_gau-link, a priori related only multiplicatively at the level of realifications, by means of additive mono-analytic log-shells (IUTchII, Remark 4.7.2). (ii) The construction of F^⊛_mod (fraktur) depends essentially on the additive structure of F^×_mod, whereas that of F^⊛_MOD is strictly multiplicative; the construction of Example 3.6 (i) is essentially that of [FrdI], Example 6.3 ([FrdI], Theorem 5.2 (i)); F^⊛_MOD is identified with F^⊛_mod via the natural isomorphism of Example 3.6 (i), as often done below.
explicit_hypotheses: the Frobenioids of Example 3.6
for (b): a subgroup Γ ⊆ F^×_mod; S ⊆ V_mod a nonempty finite subset
IUT3.Rem3_6_2.conclusion: Isomorphism classes of objects of the relevant Frobenioids are determined by divisor and rational function monoids; F^×_mod ∪ {0} carries a natural additive structure, which fails for the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification of F^⊛_mod and for subgroups Γ ⊆ F^×_mod not of the form K^× for a subfield K ⊆ F_mod; this is what allows the additive (module) representation of objects of F^⊛_mod used to relate the two sides of the enhanced Θ^{×μ}_gau-link via log-shells. Convention: F^⊛_MOD is identified with F^⊛_mod via Example 3.6 (i).
definitions_required: divisor monoid and rational function monoid of a Frobenioid ([FrdI])
obligations: Formalize 'admits a natural additive structure' for a subgroup Γ ⊆ F^×_mod as: Γ ∪ {0} is closed under addition (then it is K^× ∪ {0} for a subfield K); prove that {1} and the S-unit groups for nonempty finite S are not additively closed (elementary), and that the rational function monoids of the perfection or realification carry no such structure.
The determination of isomorphism classes by the divisor and rational function monoids is cited from [FrdI], Theorem 5.2.
ambiguities: Page 109, (b): 'subgroups that do not arise as the multiplicative group of some subfield'; the claim that such Γ admit no natural additive structure is stated with a reference, not proved.
'A certain enhanced version' of the Θ^{×μ}_gau-link (pages 108, 109) is not specified on these pages.

IUT3.Rem3_8_2.content: 'One verifies immediately' that the main results so far on Gaussian log-theta-lattices, namely Theorem 1.5, Proposition 2.1, Corollary 2.3 (cf. Remark 2.3.2) and Proposition 3.5, generalize immediately ('formally') to LGP- and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices, since their substantive content concerns portions of the log-theta-lattices substantively unaffected by the transition from Gaussian to LGP- or lgp-Gaussian.
